You will explore the fundamental principles that underpin the law, including consented and transparent data use, purpose limitation, and data minimization. The course clearly defines the rights granted to Data Principals, such as the right to access, correct, and nominate, alongside the critical obligations imposed on Data Fiduciaries, including implementing security safeguards and reporting breaches. Furthermore, the session breaks down the new consent framework, the role of the Data Protection Officer, and the stringent penalty structure, which can extend up to 250 crores. By completing this course, learners will be prepared to navigate the complexities of the DPDP Act and foster a culture of data privacy and accountability within their organizations.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023: An Overview
desc: In an era of rapid digitization, protecting personal data has become a critical aspect of governance. This course delves into the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, a landmark legislation enacted to safeguard the privacy of Indian citizens. The program begins by establishing the context, stemming from the Supreme Court's declaration of the right to privacy as a fundamental right. It then systematically breaks down the Act's key components across several modules. Learners will explore the definitions of personal data, the grounds for lawful data processing such as consent and legitimate uses, and the specific obligations imposed on Data Fiduciaries, including purpose limitation, data minimization, and breach notification. The course also details the rights granted to Data Principals, such as the right to access, correct, and erase their data, and outlines the available exemptions. By the end of this course, participants will be prepared to review their organization's data handling practices and implement the necessary processes to comply with this pivotal law, fostering a culture of data responsibility within the government.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection: Insights from Secretary S. Krishnan
desc: In an era of rapid digitalization, protecting personal data has become a critical national priority. This course delves into the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, explaining its significance in the Indian legal landscape, especially after the Supreme Court recognized privacy as a fundamental right. The curriculum breaks down the essential components of the Act, defining key roles such as the Data Principal (the individual), the Data Fiduciary (the entity collecting data), and the Data Processor. It highlights the empowerment of citizens through new rights and controls over their data. Through discussions on real-world scenarios like digital arrest scams and identity theft, the course underscores the urgent need for robust data governance and heightened citizen awareness. By the end of this session, learners will understand the framework of the DPDP Act and be better equipped to navigate the digital world safely and responsibly, fostering a culture of privacy and accountability.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Platforms for Governance and Taxation
desc: This course delves into the end-to-end lifecycle of a national-scale digital infrastructure project, as exemplified by India's Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN). It begins by contextualizing the challenge of creating a resilient and evolving platform for over 1.4 crore taxpayers. The curriculum covers the core architectural principles, including the rationale for choosing battle-tested technologies like Java and Hadoop, and the strategic shift towards a microservices model to ensure modularity and independent failure domains. A significant portion is dedicated to infrastructure decisions, weighing the pros and cons of on-premise versus cloud deployments, and the financial and operational implications of each. Learners will explore the critical importance of governance, from structuring Managed Service Provider (MSP) contracts and enforcing SLAs to establishing robust review bodies like an Architecture Review Board and Change Control Board. The course also provides a deep dive into cybersecurity, disaster recovery planning, and the necessity of continuous integration and automated testing to maintain platform agility and trust. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to lead or advise on large-scale digital transformation projects in government, with a clear understanding of the technical, managerial, and strategic components required for success.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Platforms Strategy Growth and Engagement
desc: In today's digital-first economy, platforms have become central to how we connect, transact, and innovate. This course offers a comprehensive guide to understanding the mechanics and strategies that drive successful digital platforms. It begins by establishing the foundational context, explaining why platforms are a disruptive force in modern markets and how they create ecosystems of users, sellers, and service providers. Key learning areas include the critical challenges of platform launch and growth, with a focus on building critical mass and fostering cross-side network effects, illustrated through case studies of companies like Airbnb and OLX. The course further delves into the strategic use of data for personalization and loyalty, a cornerstone of platform success. You will also analyze diverse monetization strategies, from freemium models to value-added services, equipping you with the knowledge to evaluate platform viability. By the end, learners will be equipped with practical tools and analytical frameworks to effectively build, manage, or engage with digital platforms in any sector.

title: DIGITAL PLI/RPLI POLICY BONDS
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the 'ePLI bond,' a Digital India initiative by the Department of Posts to modernize service delivery. Learners will explore the transition from physical to digital policy bonds, understanding the context of this change within the government's push for digitization. The curriculum details the step-by-step process for policyholders to download and access their PLI/RPLI bonds on the DigiLocker mobile app. It covers key technical and security aspects, including the role of Aadhaar for authentication, the validity of digital signatures under the IT Act 2000, and the use of encrypted QR codes for verification by postal staff. By the end of this course, participants will be equipped to effectively inform and assist citizens in utilizing this hassle-free digital service, contributing to a more transparent and efficient system.

title: Digital Public Infrastructure for Agriculture
desc: The Indian agricultural sector, despite its economic significance, faces structural challenges that past digital solutions have struggled to address due to fragmentation and data silos. This course provides a comprehensive overview of how Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) offers a foundational solution to these issues. It delves into the core concept of DPI as a set of common digital "rails"—encompassing identity, data exchange, and consent mechanisms—that enable interoperability and foster a collaborative ecosystem. Learners will explore the specific application of these principles within agriculture, known as Agri-DPI. The curriculum covers essential topics such as farmer registries, open digital architecture, and robust data governance frameworks. Participants will learn to evaluate different architectural models, from centralized to decentralized, and understand the importance of incorporating trust and inclusion from the design phase. By the end of the course, learners will be equipped to outline an actionable DPI pilot project, applying their knowledge to solve real-world challenges faced by farmers, policymakers, and the broader agricultural market. This course is essential for officials and practitioners aiming to drive scalable and sustainable digital transformation in agriculture.
org: DPI Academy by Artha Global and eGov Foundation

title: Digital Public Infrastructure- DigiLocker
desc: Delve into the architecture and principles of India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), the backbone of the nation's digital transformation. This course explains the interconnected systems like Aadhaar, UPI, and API Setu that form the 'India Stack.' The primary focus is on DigiLocker, exploring its function as a secure, citizen-centric platform for issuing, storing, and verifying digital documents. You will learn about its federated architecture, which allows government departments and private entities to issue and request documents via secure APIs without centralizing data storage. The session covers critical concepts such as the consent layer, which empowers users with control over their data as mandated by the DPDP Act, and the evolution towards Verifiable Credentials for selective, privacy-preserving information sharing. By the end of this course, you will understand how DigiLocker facilitates 'ease of living' by enabling paperless processes for services like passport applications, financial KYC, and more, making it a cornerstone of modern e-governance.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Public Infrastructure: Security by Design
desc: Dive into the foundational principles of creating secure and scalable Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) in this insightful course. As governments worldwide accelerate their digital transformation journeys, understanding how to build secure DPIs has become paramount. This course addresses the context by explaining why a 'security by design' mindset is crucial for protecting citizen data and ensuring the integrity of public services. Key learning areas include a detailed examination of DPI's layered architecture, the core components that enable services like digital identity and payment interfaces, and the governance frameworks necessary for effective oversight, including public-private collaboration. Upon completion, learners will be able to analyze the structure of a DPI, evaluate its security posture, and understand its role in fostering a trusted, inclusive, and innovative digital ecosystem for all citizens. This knowledge is essential for officials involved in technology policy, digital project implementation, and public service delivery.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital safety essentials
desc: In an increasingly digital world, understanding how to protect oneself online is a critical skill for everyone. This course, 'Fundamentals of Digital Safety and Online Security,' serves as an essential introduction to safe internet practices. It is designed for a general audience with no prior technical knowledge. The curriculum covers key areas such as identifying common threats like phishing and malware, creating strong passwords, managing privacy settings, and practicing safe browsing habits. Through a series of practical tips and clear guidance, learners will understand the importance of digital hygiene. The course concludes with interactive quizzes to reinforce learning and check comprehension, ensuring that participants can confidently apply these safety essentials to their daily online activities, both personal and professional. Upon completion, learners will be better equipped to safeguard their digital footprint and contribute to a more secure online environment for all.

title: Digital Safety for Women Employees
desc: In an increasingly digital government landscape, ensuring the safety and security of all employees online is paramount. This course, 'Digital Safety and Cyber Awareness for Women Employees,' provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and mitigating digital risks. It is specifically tailored to empower women professionals, helping them build the confidence and skills needed to navigate the digital environment safely. The curriculum covers the identification of common cyber threats such as phishing, social engineering, and online harassment. It delves into the legal provisions and rights available to individuals, ensuring they are aware of the recourse for any digital misconduct. Furthermore, the course outlines the official procedures for reporting cyber threats and incidents, fostering a proactive security culture. By completing this module, learners will not only enhance their personal digital safety but also contribute to the overall cyber resilience of their organization, promoting a respectful and secure online work environment.

title: Digital Shift in Urban Accounting : Karnataka's Municipal Finance
desc:
Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) are critical to city-level service delivery, making sound financial management essential for informed decision-making. In Karnataka, municipal accounting followed the Karnataka Municipal Accounting Manual, 1965, prescribing a manual, single-entry, cash-based system. Delays in revenue data, inconsistent figures and weak financial visibility limited effective management.

Recognising that credible governance depends on credible financial data, Karnataka introduced the Fund Based Accrual Accounting System (FBAAS) in 2006. Based on ICAI principles, FBAAS strengthened financial tracking, transparency and compliance by classifying municipal resources into governmental, proprietary and fiduciary funds. Its integration with Khajane 2 and e-Sweekruthi enabled seamless information flows across departments. This case examines how accounting reform, institutional ownership and digital integration can transform municipal financial governance.

title: Digital Switching
desc: This course offers a detailed exploration of digital switching systems, a critical component of modern telecommunications infrastructure. The curriculum is designed to build a strong foundational understanding, starting with why networks require switches and how they function to direct information. Learners will first be introduced to the basic crossbar switch, its operational logic, and its inherent 'strictly non-blocking' property. The course then addresses the challenge of crosspoint complexity and introduces multi-stage interconnection networks (MINs) as a solution. A significant portion is dedicated to the analysis of Clos networks, including the Clos theorem for non-blocking conditions, and the Slepian-Duguid theorem for rearrangeably non-blocking systems, utilizing tools like Paull's matrix for analysis. The course also covers time-division switching (TST switches) and concludes with an examination of packet switching, including self-routing Banyan and Delta networks, which are fundamental to the internet and data communication. Upon completion, learners will be able to analyze and compare different switching architectures and understand the trade-offs between complexity, cost, and performance in network design.

title: Digital Technologies for Climate Resiliency
desc: Developed under the Ministry of Power’s Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), this course provides a comprehensive overview of building climate-resilient power infrastructure. The curriculum delves into the various threats facing Distribution Companies (DISCOMs), including natural disasters, technological failures, and human-induced events like cyber-attacks. Through an analysis of global and Indian case studies, learners will explore the operational and financial impacts of grid disruptions. The course introduces a multi-faceted resilience framework covering organizational, technological, financial, and planning dimensions. Key learning areas include system hardening, disaster response planning, and the deployment of digital solutions such as smart grids, advanced metering, and remote monitoring. Participants will gain the knowledge to develop and implement effective strategies to mitigate risks, ensure business continuity, and enhance the overall resilience of power distribution networks.

title: Digital Tools for Crime Prevention: Trinayan and Sashakt
desc: In an era of rapid technological advancement, modern policing requires innovative tools to ensure public safety and operational efficiency. This course provides a comprehensive overview of two pioneering mobile applications, Trinayan and Sashakt, designed by the Chhattisgarh Police to transform law enforcement practices. The curriculum delves into the specific functionalities of each application, demonstrating how Trinayan empowers officers with real-time CCTV network mapping, geo-tagging of crime scenes, and rapid access to crucial video evidence. It also covers the Sashakt application, which provides on-the-spot verification of stolen or suspect vehicles by cross-referencing a live database, significantly aiding in recovery and investigation. Learners will understand how to leverage these digital tools to enhance data-driven decision-making, improve inter-district coordination, and shorten investigation timelines. The course emphasizes the practical application of this technology in the field, showcasing its role in building a more transparent, accountable, and preventive policing framework. Ultimately, it presents a powerful case study on how digital transformation can strengthen the capacity of law enforcement agencies to protect communities effectively.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: Digital Transformation and Financial Inclusion with AADHAAR
desc: Delve into the strategic evolution of Aadhaar and its profound impact on India's governance and financial landscape. This course chronicles Aadhaar's journey from a simple digital identity to the cornerstone of the country's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI). It examines the key policy decisions, technological innovations, and institutional collaborations that enabled this transformation. Key learning areas include the architecture of the Aadhaar ecosystem, its integration with Jan Dhan Yojana and mobile technology to form the powerful JAM trinity, and its role in enabling e-KYC, Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AEPS), and Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT). The course also addresses the challenges faced, including privacy safeguards and legal frameworks established through Supreme Court rulings. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze the success of this large-scale platform and apply lessons in policy design, institutional synergy, and secure digital transformation to their own domains.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation Building the Future with AI
desc: Dive deep into the architecture of digital transformation with this insightful discussion on building the future of public services. This course captures a conversation between leaders at the forefront of India's digital economy, focusing on the lessons learned from creating the Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The content provides a strategic overview of the principles required for developing robust, scalable, and secure digital public infrastructure. Key learning areas include the balance between reliability and feature development, the practical application of AI-assisted engineering with human oversight, and the governance frameworks essential for managing national-scale platforms. Participants will also explore how to cultivate an innovative, outcome-oriented work culture that attracts and retains top talent. This course is designed to equip public officials with the strategic mindset and practical knowledge to lead and implement successful digital transformation projects within their domains.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation eSanjeevani
desc: Delve into the journey of eSanjeevani, one of India's most impactful digital health initiatives. This course examines the strategic vision, policy innovation, and operational execution behind the creation and scaling of a nationwide telemedicine service. The discussion covers the platform's foundational context, including the challenge of healthcare accessibility and the role of the National Health Policy. Key learning areas include the hub-and-spoke model, microservice architecture, the importance of institutional collaboration with bodies like C-DAC, and the governance frameworks that ensure security and scalability. Learners will gain valuable insights into the practicalities of implementing large-scale digital public infrastructure, drawing parallels from the successful Aadhaar-based instant PAN project. By the end, participants will be able to analyze the critical success factors for digital transformation in the public sector and appreciate how technology can be leveraged to achieve citizen-centric service delivery at scale.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation in Railway Ticketing and Freight Operations
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the digital transformation of railway ticketing and freight management systems in Indian Railways. It examines the transition from traditional manual processes to modern digital platforms that improve operational efficiency, transparency, and customer service. Learners will gain an understanding of key systems such as the Passenger Reservation System (PRS), Unreserved Ticketing System (UTS), National Train Enquiry System (NTES), and Freight Operations Information System (FOIS), and their role in streamlining passenger and freight operations. The course also explores digital workflows, mobile ticketing, real-time tracking, data analytics, fraud prevention mechanisms, and emerging technologies that are shaping the future of railway services. By the end of the course, participants will be able to understand, analyze, and support the effective use of digital technologies in railway ticketing and freight management.

title: Digital Transformation of Revenue Administration
desc: This podcast-style course offers an engaging and in-depth exploration of the digital transformation of revenue administration through the lens of India’s landmark Goods and Services Tax (GST) implementation. Presented by Shri Manish Kumar Sinha, CEO of GSTN, the discussion traces the journey from a fragmented pre-GST tax structure to a unified “One Nation, One Tax” ecosystem. Through a conversational and expert-led format, listeners gain insights into the institutional evolution of the Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN), including its transition to a fully government-owned entity and the development of a robust digital infrastructure capable of handling large-scale data with high reliability. This podcast-style course is ideal for government officials, IT professionals, and practitioners seeking to understand large-scale digital transformation through an accessible and discussion-driven format.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation Powered by AADHAAR
desc: Delve into the comprehensive story of Aadhaar, from its conceptualization to its implementation as a transformative national project. This course provides a detailed overview of the strategic decisions, technology architecture, and governance models established by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). You will explore how Aadhaar became the backbone for critical services like Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AEPS), fundamentally changing financial and social inclusion. The curriculum focuses on the practical challenges and solutions related to scaling a national IT system, building citizen trust, and ensuring data security. By analyzing this landmark case study, government officers and policymakers will learn to apply key principles to the design and management of future large-scale digital public infrastructure projects, enhancing citizen-centric service delivery.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation with Agile Project Management
desc: In an era of rapid technological change, government agencies must adapt to deliver services effectively. This course, 'Digital Transformation through Agile Project Management,' offers a comprehensive guide for public sector professionals to navigate this new landscape. It begins by establishing the fundamentals of project management within a government context, then transitions to the core principles of the Agile Manifesto. You will learn why Agile is critical for modern digital initiatives, fostering teamwork, transparency, and continuous learning to respond effectively to evolving public needs and policy changes. The course delves into practical frameworks, including Scrum, Kanban, and Extreme Programming (XP), providing the tools to manage projects in iterative sprints. It draws clear comparisons between Agile, Hybrid, and traditional waterfall models, highlighting how Agile reduces risk and improves stakeholder engagement. By the end of this course, you will be prepared to apply Agile practices to strengthen digital governance, enhance project outcomes, and drive impactful, citizen-focused transformation within your organization.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation with Cyber Secure Governance
desc: In an era of rapid digital transformation, ensuring the security of public infrastructure is paramount. This course positions cybersecurity not merely as a technical challenge, but as a critical governance function that underpins public trust and national security. It is designed for public officials who are responsible for steering their organizations through digitalization, providing them with a comprehensive framework for integrating security into every aspect of governance. The curriculum is structured to build a holistic understanding, starting with the foundations of digital trust and the evolving global threat landscape. Learners will delve into the creation of robust governance policies, standards, and best practices. Key modules cover the implementation of multi-layered technical and organizational security controls, strategies for institutional preparedness and resilience against cyber incidents, and a thorough review of the legal and regulatory frameworks governing cybersecurity. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to lead their institutions in developing a proactive security culture, moving from basic awareness to a mature, audit-driven approach that safeguards critical digital assets and ensures the continuity of e-Governance services.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
desc: Delve into the strategic framework of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), a pioneering effort to revolutionize India's healthcare landscape. This course unpacks the mission's core objective: to establish a seamless, interoperable digital health ecosystem for all citizens. You will explore the context behind this massive digital transformation, understanding why a unified infrastructure is critical for modern healthcare delivery. The curriculum covers key building blocks, including the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), Health Facility Registry (HFR), and Healthcare Professionals Registry (HPR), explaining how they function together. Furthermore, the course examines the robust governance structures, leadership strategies, and policy decisions that have guided ABDM's successful rollout. By analyzing the interplay of technology, data security, and public trust, learners will grasp how ABDM is creating a secure, efficient, and patient-centric healthcare system. This program is essential for anyone looking to understand the future of public health and digital governance in India and beyond.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Effective Procurement and Project Management
desc: As India advances its digital transformation agenda, the ability to effectively procure and manage large-scale IT projects is paramount for public sector officials. This course offers a comprehensive guide to the foundational pillars of digital project execution. It begins by detailing how to craft robust Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) that establish clear scope, budget, and feasibility. The curriculum then moves to designing and evaluating Requests for Proposals (RFPs) that attract high-quality vendors and mitigate risks. Key learning areas include applying proven project management methodologies, such as Agile, to ensure on-time and on-budget delivery, and establishing strong governance structures. Furthermore, the course provides in-depth knowledge on defining, monitoring, and enforcing Service Level Agreements (SLAs) to ensure vendor accountability and sustained service quality. By mastering these principles, learners will be equipped to lead and contribute to the success of critical digital governance initiatives, turning policy vision into operational reality.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Financial Reporting and Analytical System
desc: Dive into the strategic design and implementation of FINnet, India’s national-level Financial Intelligence Platform. This course offers a comprehensive look at how a greenfield digital system was conceptualized and executed to strengthen the country's financial crime prevention framework, in alignment with global standards set by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). You will explore the transition from traditional procurement to outcome-driven RFPs, ensuring business goals are met through effective vendor evaluation and Service Level Agreement (SLA) management. The curriculum covers the technical and governance challenges of migrating over a decade of legacy data to support real-time, AI-powered analytics. Participants will learn about building secure, scalable platforms and applying robust governance strategies, including exit management and phased implementation. By the end of this course, you will be equipped to evaluate and apply best practices for managing complex, large-scale digital transformation projects within the public sector.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Government e-Marketplace
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) and its pivotal role in India's digital transformation journey. It addresses the critical need for reform in public procurement by showcasing how GeM was conceived and implemented to enhance transparency, efficiency, and inclusivity. The curriculum examines the key pillars of GeM's success, including its agile Section-8 company structure, innovative policy frameworks, and the robust technology backbone that supports its nationwide operations. Key learning areas include an analysis of GeM's procurement innovations, its seamless integration with other Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) like Aadhaar, GSTN, and PFMS, and its profound impact on promoting MSME participation in public contracts. By the end of the course, learners will be equipped to analyze the systemic benefits of GeM, evaluate its replicable governance model, and appreciate how a strategic blend of vision, policy, and technology can drive large-scale, impactful governance reforms.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: National Payments Corporation of India
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the digital transformation driven by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It examines the critical context of why India needed a unified, interoperable payments system and how NPCI was established to fulfill this vision under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The narrative delves into the evolution of India's digital payment ecosystem, covering key innovations such as IMPS, RuPay, AePS, and the revolutionary Unified Payments Interface (UPI). Learners will explore how UPI was designed as a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to facilitate real-time, secure, and low-cost transactions, dramatically accelerating financial inclusion. The course also analyzes the synergistic impact of the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) Trinity in bringing millions of unbanked citizens into the formal financial system. Upon completion, participants will have a deep appreciation for the policy, technology, and governance strategies that made India a global benchmark in digital payments, and they will be able to analyze the key components that drive successful digital public infrastructure projects.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
desc: Delve into the transformative journey of the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), the world's largest publicly funded health assurance scheme. This course provides a comprehensive overview of how the National Health Authority (NHA) successfully shifted from a policy vision to impactful, large-scale implementation through a sophisticated digital ecosystem. You will learn about the core components of this digital transformation, including the use of a centralized, interoperable platform built on India Stack principles to enable seamless, real-time claims processing and portability across states. The curriculum covers the innovative design of Health Benefit Packages, standardized pricing models, and the flexible trust, insurance, and hybrid operational models adopted by states. Furthermore, it highlights the critical role of technology in ensuring stringent fraud control and data-driven governance. This course is essential for policymakers, public administrators, healthcare professionals, and technology leaders seeking to understand how to leverage digital innovation for equitable and efficient public service delivery.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana
desc: Delve into the transformative journey of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), a cornerstone of India's Digital India mission. This course examines the context and critical need for financial inclusion that led to the program's launch in 2014. You will explore the key pillars of its success, including the 'mission-mode' execution strategy that enabled rapid, large-scale rollout and the seamless integration of technologies like Aadhaar, RuPay, and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to ensure last-mile service delivery. The curriculum highlights the profound social and economic impact of PMJDY, particularly in empowering women and rural populations by providing them with access to banking and credit. Furthermore, the course analyzes how this initiative laid a robust foundation for India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), paving the way for future innovations in governance, health, and education. By understanding this case study, you will gain valuable insights into executing large-scale public welfare programs.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Transformation: Public Financial Management System
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS), a cornerstone of India's digital public infrastructure. It addresses the critical need for transparent and efficient management of public funds in modern governance. The curriculum delves into the origins and evolution of PFMS, detailing its architecture and its transformative impact on fiscal operations. Key learning areas include the mechanics of real-time payments, the successful implementation of Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) across thousands of schemes, and the integration with over 650 financial systems. The course also covers specific modules like e-Bill, e-Utilisation Certificate, and the SNA-SPARSH model, which are vital for end-to-end financial accountability. Learners will gain insights into the strategic coordination required among various stakeholders and the technological backbone provided by NIC. The course concludes by looking ahead to PFMS 2.0, envisioning a future driven by AI, enhanced interoperability, and citizen-centric digital financial services, preparing officials to navigate the next wave of public finance transformation.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Digital Utility Journey Towards Energy Transition
desc: The global energy landscape is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by the need for sustainability and technological innovation. This course delves into the journey of a digital utility amidst this energy transition. It begins by establishing the context of decarbonization, decentralization, and digitalization as the key drivers reshaping power grids. You will explore the technical and operational challenges of integrating renewable, inverter-based resources, and the implications for grid stability and protection. A key focus is the evolving role of the Distribution System Operator (DSO) from a traditional manager to an orchestrator of complex systems involving Distributed Energy Resources (DERs), electric vehicles, and active consumer participation. The curriculum covers the importance of asset visibility, data analytics, and asset performance management in building a proactive, predictive, and resilient grid. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped with the strategic insights needed to navigate the complexities of grid modernization and lead their organizations toward a sustainable and efficient energy future.

title: Dimensioning in AutoCAD
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of AutoCAD's powerful dimensioning capabilities, designed for professionals who require precision in their technical drawings. The curriculum is structured to build proficiency from fundamental concepts to advanced applications, ensuring drawings are clear, accurate, and compliant with industry standards. Learners will begin by understanding the critical role of dimensioning in engineering and architecture. The course then delves into the practical application of various dimensioning tools, covering linear, aligned, angular, radial, diameter, and ordinate dimensions. A significant focus is placed on creating and managing dimension styles and substyles, allowing for full control over the appearance of dimensions, including text, arrows, lines, and units. Participants will also learn advanced techniques such as creating baseline and continued dimensions, applying tolerance formats, and using grip editing to modify dimensions efficiently. By the end of this course, you will be able to produce meticulously annotated, professional-grade drawings, significantly improving your workflow and the quality of your design output.
subDomain: Digital Tools ( MS office, Excel, & PPT) & Platforms

title: Dimensions of Forensics in Criminal Law
desc: This course provides a structured understanding of forensic investigations within India’s updated criminal justice framework. It covers mandatory forensic procedures under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, evidentiary rules under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, and the functioning of forensic laboratories. Learners will study different types of forensic evidence, constitutional safeguards, medico-legal duties, chain-of-custody protocols, and technological systems supporting e-forensics. The course also highlights landmark judicial decisions that demonstrate how forensic science enhances the quality, transparency, and admissibility of investigations.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD
keywords: Bureau of Police Research and Development

title: Dimensions of Maritime Security
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of maritime security, positioning it as a critical and complementary component of a nation's overall security framework. It challenges conventional, military-focused views by introducing a broader paradigm of 'Governance by National Security' (GBNS), which aims to enhance the well-being of a nation's people. Learners will examine how national security governance extends across eight distinct terrains, with a special focus on the ocean. The curriculum systematically breaks down the concept of 'ocean property,' a framework for assessing a nation's maritime net worth through four key elements: ocean advantage, resources, environment, and islands. The course also clarifies the role of maritime law in establishing the rule of law at sea and explains why maritime security is a vital concern for all countries, including landlocked states that rely on global commons. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to analyze maritime issues from a strategic governance perspective and integrate ocean-related policies into comprehensive national security planning, thereby maximizing a nation's potential for sustainable development and security.

title: DIPAM - Overview of the Disinvestment Landscape
desc: This course offers a detailed exploration of India's disinvestment and public asset management strategy. It begins by establishing the context of economic reforms that necessitated changes in the government's approach to Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs). Learners will gain a thorough understanding of the key learning areas, including the evolution of disinvestment policies over the decades, the different methodologies used for reducing government shareholding, and the strategic rationale behind them. The curriculum specifically covers the core components of the new PSE policy, distinguishing between strategic and non-strategic sectors. By analyzing major disinvestment transactions, participants will be able to appreciate the real-world application and financial implications of these policies. Ultimately, this course equips learners with the knowledge to understand the intricate relationship between disinvestment, public finance, and India's long-term economic vision.
org: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management

title: DIPAM - Review of Financial Concepts and Frameworks
desc: This course offers a detailed exploration of financial analysis, designed for officials involved in investment and public asset management. The curriculum begins with the fundamentals of financial statements, teaching you how to read and interpret balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements to gauge a company's stability and profitability. You will then delve into the practical application of key financial ratios to conduct a thorough performance assessment. The course provides in-depth coverage of critical valuation techniques, including intrinsic valuation using Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) models and market-based approaches through Relative Valuation. It also addresses common value distortions that can arise during company evaluation. To provide a holistic perspective, the module introduces the principles of technical analysis as a complementary tool for financial decision-making. Through practical examples, you will gain the confidence to analyze financial data, value enterprises, and contribute to strategic investment and asset management decisions within the public sector.
org: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management

title: DIPAM Induction
desc: This introductory course is designed to familiarize learners with the essential workings of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM). In the context of India's economic governance, DIPAM plays a crucial role in managing the central government's equity in public sector undertakings and overseeing strategic disinvestment. This module provides the foundational knowledge required to understand this vital institution. Key learning areas include the department's historical evolution, its core mission and vision, and its detailed organizational structure. Learners will explore the primary functions of DIPAM's various divisions, from asset monetization to portfolio management. Upon completion, participants will have a clear and structured understanding of DIPAM's mandate and its contribution to the nation's economic objectives, preparing them for roles related to public finance and asset management.
org: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management

title: Direct and L1 Procurement on GeM
desc: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has transformed public procurement in India, creating a transparent and efficient ecosystem. This course is essential for any Central or State Government official involved in the procurement lifecycle, providing the critical knowledge needed to operate effectively on the platform. It delves into the core functionalities of GeM, with a specific focus on Direct and L1 purchasing methods as mandated by the General Financial Rules (GFR-2017). The curriculum begins by establishing the purpose of GeM and the roles of its users. It then provides a detailed interpretation of GFR Rule 149(i) and (ii), which are the cornerstones of Direct and L1 procurement. Through practical demonstrations and step-by-step guidance, learners will master the procedural workflows for both types of purchases directly on the GeM portal. The course also includes a comparative analysis of the benefits and limitations associated with each method, empowering officials to make strategic and compliant procurement decisions. Upon completion, participants will be fully equipped to manage procurement tasks with confidence, ensuring adherence to financial rules and promoting value for public money.
org: Mahatma Gandhi State Institute of Public Administration Punjab

title: Direct Post
desc: This introductory course is designed to familiarize learners with the Direct Post service, a cost-effective solution for direct marketing and advertising. The program begins by defining Direct Post, outlining the types of unaddressed postal articles that can be sent, such as pamphlets, brochures, and samples. It explains the importance of this service for businesses seeking to reach a broad audience in targeted geographical areas without specific addresses. Key learning areas include the specific conditions for availing the service, such as the minimum of 1,000 articles per posting, A3 size restrictions, and bundling requirements. The course walks through the procedural aspects, covering the registration process at designated post offices, calculation of charges, advance payment methods, and the issuance of invoices. Furthermore, it clarifies the delivery mechanism, explaining that articles are delivered as unaccountable mail but a final delivery report is provided to the customer. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to effectively utilize the Direct Post service in compliance with postal regulations.

title: Direct Purchase on GeM
desc: This training program offers a detailed, step-by-step guide to mastering the direct purchase functionality within the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). The course is designed for public procurement officials and government buyers who need to make small-value purchases efficiently. It begins by explaining the context of direct purchasing, its financial limits (up to ₹25,000), and its importance in streamlining procurement. Key learning areas covered include navigating the GeM interface, searching for products or services, and utilizing various filters such as 'Make in India', MSE, and seller ratings to make informed choices. The module meticulously guides learners through the process of adding items to the cart, proceeding to checkout, verifying order summaries, and handling financial approvals. By the end of this course, participants will be able to confidently execute a direct purchase, generate a contract, and ensure compliance with all procedural requirements, thereby enhancing their operational efficiency in public procurement.

title: Direct to Device Service: Satellite to Mobile Phone
desc: This course introduces the concept of Direct-to-Device (D2D) communication within Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) and explores how modern connectivity is evolving beyond traditional ground-based networks. It covers the transition toward a Unified 3D Network Architecture, in which terrestrial networks integrate with satellite systems across LEO, MEO, and GEO orbits to provide seamless and global connectivity. The course examines the D2D paradigm shift, focusing on how smartphones and other devices can connect directly to satellites. It explores the two key approaches to D2D implementation: modified devices operating in Mobile Satellite Service (MSS) spectrum and unmodified devices operating in terrestrial spectrum. The course also introduces the FR1 and FR2 spectrum framework, the technical foundations of NTN through different payload architectures, and the role of 3GPP Releases 17 and 18 in enabling NTN integration with 5G networks.

title: Direct Trainer Skills
desc: This foundational course is designed to equip aspiring and new trainers with the core competencies needed to excel in their roles. In the context of public service, effective training is paramount for capacity building and enhancing organizational efficiency. This program provides a structured journey into the world of instructional delivery, starting with the theoretical underpinnings of adult learning principles. Learners will delve into the Systematic Approach to Training (SAT), a proven methodology for creating logical and effective learning experiences. The course will guide participants through practical skills such as selecting the right training methods for different objectives, structuring a compelling lecture, and mastering the art of giving constructive feedback. By the end of this course, you will not only understand the key responsibilities of a direct trainer but also possess the foundational skills to design and deliver training that inspires learning and drives performance within your organization.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Disaster Management - Role of Telecommunications
desc: In the face of natural and man-made calamities, a resilient telecommunication network is the backbone of effective disaster response, enabling coordination for rescue, relief, and rehabilitation. This course offers an in-depth examination of the telecommunications ecosystem's role within India's disaster management framework. Participants will gain a thorough understanding of the legal structures, including the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and the operational mandates of the NDMA, SDMA, and District Authorities. The course focuses heavily on the Department of Telecommunications' Standard Operating Procedure (SOP-2020), detailing measures for mitigation, preparedness, and response. Key learning areas include analyzing telecom network vulnerabilities, such as power dependency and OFC damage, and implementing crucial response strategies like Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) and Priority Call Routing. Furthermore, the course explores advanced early warning technologies, including the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) and Cell Broadcast systems, providing officials with the knowledge to build and maintain robust communication channels. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to effectively coordinate with various stakeholders and ensure telecom services are promptly restored and maintained during emergencies.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Disaster Management and Preparedness
desc: In an era of increasing natural and man-made calamities, effective disaster management is critical for ensuring public safety and resilience. This course is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of disaster preparedness and response, tailored for public officials and volunteers. It addresses the fundamental question of why disaster management is a national priority by detailing key legislative and policy frameworks, such as the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and the National Policy on Disaster Management. Key learning areas include the classification of different disaster types, the principles of disaster preparedness, and the structured approach to managing crisis situations. Participants will learn practical evacuation and rescue techniques essential for on-ground operations. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze disaster scenarios, apply systematic response protocols, and understand the crucial function of volunteer networks in saving lives.

title: Disaster Management and Preparedness-Disaster Response Training
desc: In an era of increasing natural and man-made calamities, effective disaster management is critical for ensuring public safety and resilience. This course is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of disaster preparedness and response, tailored for public officials and volunteers. It addresses the fundamental question of why disaster management is a national priority by detailing key legislative and policy frameworks, such as the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and the National Policy on Disaster Management. Key learning areas include the classification of different disaster types, the principles of disaster preparedness, and the structured approach to managing crisis situations. Participants will learn practical evacuation and rescue techniques essential for on-ground operations. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze disaster scenarios, apply systematic response protocols, and understand the crucial function of volunteer networks in saving lives and mitigating harm. This knowledge empowers individuals to become valuable assets in their communities' disaster response efforts, contributing to a more secure and prepared nation.

title: Disaster Management Part 2 - Role of DoT
desc: In the event of a disaster, robust and resilient communication networks are paramount for effective response and recovery. This course provides a detailed examination of the functions and responsibilities of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) in disaster management. Participants will learn how DoT's Licensed Service Areas (LSAs) proactively coordinate with state governments and telecom operators to prepare for, and respond to, emergencies. The curriculum covers essential procedures such as organizing STDCC meetings, ensuring Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) readiness to maintain connectivity when one network fails, and identifying critical telecom sites for protection. Furthermore, the course delves into the technical and operational aspects of the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP), an XML-based system for sending rapid, targeted warning messages across various media. Upon completion, learners will have a comprehensive understanding of the strategic importance of telecom resilience and the specific actions taken by DoT to safeguard communication services during a crisis.
org: Ministry of Communications- Department of Telecommunications

title: Disaster Management Plan for natural and man-made disasters M-1
desc: In an era of increasing uncertainty, having a robust Disaster Management Plan (DMP) is essential for ensuring public safety and organizational continuity. This course offers a detailed guide to formulating an effective DMP. It begins by establishing the context and importance of disaster preparedness in the public sector. You will learn to differentiate between various types of disasters, covering natural calamities such as earthquakes, cyclones, and floods, and man-made crises including terrorist attacks, bomb threats, and the growing threat of cybercrime. The course outlines the key components of a DMP, from initial risk assessment and mitigation strategies to response protocols and recovery procedures. By the end of this module, you will be equipped to draft a comprehensive plan tailored to your organization's specific vulnerabilities, helping to safeguard personnel, assets, and public services during a crisis.

title: Disaster Management Plan for natural and man-made disasters M-1 Hindi
desc: यह विस्तृत पाठ्यक्रम सरकारी अधिकारियों और सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के कर्मचारियों को आपदा प्रबंधन के महत्वपूर्ण पहलुओं से परिचित कराने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। आज के अनिश्चित समय में, प्राकृतिक और मानव निर्मित दोनों प्रकार की आपदाओं के लिए एक मजबूत योजना का होना अनिवार्य है। यह पाठ्यक्रम एक व्यापक आपदा प्रबंधन योजना (डीएमपी) की आवश्यकता और इसके प्रमुख घटकों की गहन समझ प्रदान करता है। शिक्षार्थी विभिन्न प्रकार की आपदाओं की पहचान करना सीखेंगे, जिनमें भूकंप, चक्रवात और बाढ़ जैसी प्राकृतिक घटनाएं तथा आतंकवादी हमले, बम धमकियां और साइबर सुरक्षा उल्लंघन जैसी मानव निर्मित घटनाएं शामिल हैं। पाठ्यक्रम प्रत्येक प्रकार की आपदा के लिए विशिष्ट कार्य योजनाओं को विकसित करने पर व्यावहारिक मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करता है, जिसमें रोकथाम, तैयारी, प्रतिक्रिया और पुनर्प्राप्ति के चरण शामिल हैं। इस पाठ्यक्रम को पूरा करने पर, प्रतिभागी अपने संगठनों के लिए आपदा प्रबंधन योजनाओं के विकास और कार्यान्वयन में प्रभावी रूप से योगदान करने में सक्षम होंगे, जिससे सार्वजनिक सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित होगी और संकट के समय नुकसान को कम किया जा सकेगा।

title: Disciplinary and Appeal Rules 1968 in Indian Railways
desc: This course offers an in-depth understanding of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968, a critical legal framework for maintaining accountability and order within Indian Railways. The content is structured to provide a clear, procedural guide for public servants, particularly those in administrative, HR, and vigilance functions. Key learning areas include a detailed breakdown of minor penalties such as censure and withholding of promotion, and major penalties like compulsory retirement and dismissal from service. The course meticulously outlines the step-by-step disciplinary process, from the issuance of a charge sheet and conducting an inquiry to the final imposition of a penalty. Furthermore, it explains the vital safeguards available to employees, such as the right to appeal, seek revision, or request a review of disciplinary orders. It also covers the conditions and procedures related to suspension and the provision of subsistence allowance, ensuring learners can apply these rules while upholding the principles of natural justice.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: Discipline-Driven Professionalism in Defence Establishments
desc: In the structured environment of defence and government establishments, professional conduct is paramount to operational efficiency and institutional integrity. This course offers a comprehensive guide to the principles of discipline-driven professionalism that every employee must embody. It moves beyond basic rules to explore the nuances of workplace etiquette, ensuring that personnel reflect the highest standards of conduct in all interactions. The curriculum delves into key areas including non-verbal communication, with a deep dive into body language and micro-expressions to avoid. It covers verbal discipline using models like 'Pace, Pitch, Pause, Power' and outlines best practices for phone etiquette in shared office spaces. Learners will also understand the psychology of navigating common areas such as corridors and doorways, and the unspoken rules of interacting at a colleague's desk. Special emphasis is placed on respectful and efficient engagement with senior officers and fostering a gender-safe, dignity-first environment. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to navigate various workplace scenarios with confidence and professionalism. They will be able to apply these principles to build a positive and respectful office culture, enhance interpersonal effectiveness, and uphold the decorum expected within a defence organization, ultimately contributing to a more disciplined and harmonious workplace.
keywords: Body Language Deep Dive for Modern Offices
Colleague’s Desk in a Common Bay

title: Discover Prompt Engineering
desc: Dive into the world of Artificial Intelligence with this foundational course on prompt engineering. As AI tools become more integrated into professional environments, the ability to communicate effectively with them is a critical skill. This course provides a comprehensive overview of why prompt engineering is essential for maximizing the potential of AI. You will learn the key principles of designing clear, specific, and context-aware prompts. The curriculum breaks down the six essential components of a perfect prompt: task, context, examples, persona, format, and tone. Through practical examples and real-world use cases in areas like customer service, content creation, and data analysis, you will gain the skills to move beyond generic queries. By the end of this course, you will be equipped to craft sophisticated prompts that instruct AI models to generate high-quality, tailored responses, thereby improving your productivity and innovation in any role.

title: Discussion on the Newly Introduced Telecom Interception Rules
desc: This course offers an in-depth examination of the newly introduced Telecom Interception Rules, 2024. It begins by tracing the evolution of surveillance laws in India, from the colonial-era Indian Telegraph Act of 1885 to the landmark Puttaswamy judgment on privacy, which set the stage for the Telecom Act, 2023. The core of the course is a detailed analysis of the 2024 rules, covering essential provisions such as senior-level authorization for interception, time-bound surveillance orders, the role of review committees, and mandatory data destruction protocols. The discussion critically evaluates the inherent tension between national security needs and individual civil liberties, using real-world case studies like the 26/11 Mumbai attacks and the Pegasus spyware controversy to illustrate both the necessity and the risks of interception. Furthermore, the course explores challenges related to encrypted OTT platforms and concludes by suggesting potential reforms to enhance judicial oversight, transparency, and accountability in India's surveillance framework.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Disposal of Scrap Goods
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the rules, procedures, and guidelines for the disposal of scrap materials within government organizations. Emphasizing transparency, accountability, and efficiency, the course explains the classification and survey process for identifying unserviceable items, and the roles of the Competent Authority and Survey Committee. It covers recognized disposal methods—including petty sales, limited tender, open tender, e-auction, and direct sale—with special attention to the handling of hazardous and electronic waste. Additionally, the course details reserve price determination, bidder eligibility, regulatory compliance with frameworks such as GFR 2017 and environmental laws, and delivery procedures to ensure secure, fair, and compliant disposal aligned with public interest. Upon completion, participants will be proficient in managing the scrap disposal process in a manner that is both procedurally correct and financially prudent, safeguarding public resources while adhering to all regulatory mandates.
org: Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management- Faridabad

title: Dispute Resolution in International Contracts
desc: International infrastructure projects often involve complex contracts, multiple stakeholders, diverse legal jurisdictions, and significant financial and technical risks, making effective dispute prevention and resolution essential. This course provides a practical understanding of key mechanisms for managing and resolving contractual disputes, including negotiation, mediation, Dispute Adjudication Boards (DABs/DAABs), and international arbitration. It covers arbitration procedures, international conventions, institutional rules, India’s Arbitration and Conciliation Act, and the recognition and enforcement of domestic and foreign arbitral awards. Learners will also explore the development of effective dispute resolution clauses, claims management, contract administration, evidence preservation, documentation, government approvals, and accountability requirements.

title: Diversification Initiatives of Coal India Limited
desc: In a rapidly changing global energy landscape, strategic adaptation is crucial for long-term success. This course delves into the diversification journey of Coal India Limited (CIL), a key player in India's energy sector. It provides a detailed examination of CIL's major initiatives to move beyond coal and embrace a more sustainable and varied energy portfolio. Key learning areas include the development of thermal power projects, the strategic implementation of coal gasification technology, and ventures into fertilizer production and pumped storage plants. Furthermore, the course highlights CIL's significant investments in solar energy, aligning with national net-zero targets. Upon completion, learners will understand how CIL is transforming business challenges into growth opportunities, reinforcing its leadership position while contributing to India's sustainable energy future.

title: Diving Deeper into Solutions for Climate Resilient Healthcare
desc: This course delves into the multifaceted challenges that climate change poses to global healthcare systems and presents actionable solutions for building resilience. You will begin by understanding how climate change exacerbates health risks, from the spread of infectious diseases to the rise in non-communicable diseases and mental health issues. The curriculum then explores a range of adaptation strategies, focusing on strengthening health system capacity, ensuring supply chain stability, and implementing decentralized energy solutions for healthcare facilities. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to the financial aspects of climate adaptation in health. You will learn about climate finance principles, innovative mechanisms like debt-for-health swaps, and the roles of public and private investors in funding these critical initiatives. The course concludes with a regional analysis of the climate-health nexus in Asia, highlighting specific vulnerabilities and the collaborative efforts underway to protect communities. Upon completion, you will be equipped to contribute to policy-making and strategic planning for a sustainable and climate-resilient health future.

title: Do's and Dont's for Government Employees- Hindi
desc: This foundational course, 'Code of Conduct for Government Employees,' is specifically designed to guide public servants in navigating the ethical and procedural landscape of government service. In the context of public administration, maintaining impeccable conduct is not just a requirement but a cornerstone of good governance, directly impacting public trust and the effectiveness of government machinery. This program serves as an essential guide to the standards of behavior expected from every government employee. The course systematically covers the core tenets of the civil service conduct rules. Key learning areas include understanding the principles of integrity, impartiality, and devotion to duty; maintaining political neutrality; and handling of official information with confidentiality. It elaborates on the 'Do's,' such as promptness and courtesy in public dealings, and the 'Don'ts,' including the prohibition of accepting gifts, engaging in private trade, or misusing official position. Learners will gain clarity on actions that constitute misconduct and the procedural implications. Upon completion, participants will be better equipped to apply these principles in their daily work, make ethical decisions, and avoid potential conflicts of interest. This knowledge is crucial for fostering a professional, transparent, and accountable work culture within government organizations, ultimately contributing to enhanced service delivery and public confidence.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: DoPT and its Training Institutes
desc: This introductory course delves into the ecosystem of civil service training and development in India, centered around the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). It is designed for public officials seeking to understand the core administrative structures that shape their professional growth. The curriculum provides a comprehensive look at DoPT's functions, including its oversight of LBSNAA, its management of ISTM as an attached office, and its grant provisions for IIPA. Participants will explore why these institutions are critical to the Indian governance framework. Key learning areas include the specific mandates of LBSNAA, ISTM, and IIPA, and how their activities contribute to building a skilled and efficient civil service. Upon completion, learners will be able to appreciate the interconnectedness of these organizations and their collective impact on national public administration, equipping them with essential knowledge for their career in government service.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Dos and Don'ts of Disaster Preparedness
desc: In an era of increasing climate variability and unforeseen events, effective disaster preparedness is crucial for resilient governance and public safety. This foundational course is designed to provide a comprehensive overview of essential protocols for a multitude of disaster situations. The curriculum covers a broad spectrum of emergencies, from natural calamities like earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, and cyclones to man-made incidents such as chemical, biological, or nuclear emergencies. Through a clear and concise list of 'do's and don'ts', learners will understand the immediate actions to take before, during, and after a disaster. The course aims to build a culture of preparedness, enabling government functionaries and citizens to act swiftly and decisively, thereby reducing vulnerability and mitigating the impact of disasters on life and property. Upon completion, participants will be better equipped to protect themselves and assist their communities in times of crisis.
org: National Institute of Disaster Management - NIDM

title: Dos and Don'ts of Social Media
desc: In an era of digital transformation, social media has become a primary channel for communication and information dissemination. This course is designed to equip government employees with the knowledge and skills to navigate this landscape responsibly. It begins by exploring the evolution of social media and its unique features compared to traditional media. The curriculum then delves into practical guidelines for managing a professional presence online, with specific modules on the etiquette and best practices for using platforms such as X and WhatsApp. A key focus is on distinguishing between official and personal communication, ensuring that all online activities align with the standards of public service. Furthermore, the course explicitly covers the Central Civil Services (CCS) Conduct Rules, providing a clear framework for compliance. Upon completion, learners will be prepared to use social media effectively and ethically, safeguarding both their professional reputation and sensitive government information.

title: DoSJE - Matters handled by Administration and Establishment Division
desc: This introductory module offers a comprehensive overview of the subject matters handled by the Administration and Establishment Division. The course is structured to provide learners with a clear and concise understanding of why this division is critical to the smooth functioning of a government organization. Key learning areas include a detailed breakdown of the division's core responsibilities, the specific tasks allocated to the Establishment Section, and the processes that govern its operations. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify the key functions of the division and recognize its importance in maintaining administrative order and efficiency. This knowledge is directly applicable to officials working in or interacting with administrative units, enabling them to perform their duties with greater clarity and confidence in procedural matters.
org: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment

title: DoSJE - Matters handled by Statistics Division
desc: This module is designed to familiarize learners with the specific matters handled by the Statistics Division of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment. It provides a detailed examination of the division's work allocation, focusing on its critical role in data management, monitoring, and evaluation for social welfare programs. Key topics include the division's responsibilities related to Gender Budgeting, the PRAGATI portal for project monitoring, and the E-Samiksha platform. The course delves into the Information, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Social Audit (I-MESA) Scheme, explaining its components like information dissemination, project monitoring, and social audits. Furthermore, learners will understand the process behind creating the Annual Report and the Handbook on Social Welfare Statistics. Upon completion, participants will have a clear understanding of how the Statistics Division contributes to evidence-based policy-making and enhances transparency and accountability in the social justice sector.
org: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment

title: DoSJE - Scheme of National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction
desc: The rising challenge of substance abuse requires a structured and compassionate response from the government and its functionaries. This course is designed to equip learners with a thorough understanding of the government's primary initiative in this area: the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). It provides a detailed examination of the scheme's architecture, from the national level down to the State Action Plans (SAP) and District Action Plans (DAP), ensuring a holistic view of its implementation framework. Participants will delve into the specifics of the support systems available for victims of substance use. The course explains the operational modalities of key institutions such as De-addiction Centers, including Grant-in-Aid Institutions (GIAs), District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs), and Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs). Through engaging scenarios, interactive activities, and inspiring success stories, learners will not only grasp the theoretical aspects of the schemes but also appreciate their real-world impact. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify the various benefits available to victims and understand the processes for accessing them. This knowledge is crucial for officials involved in social justice, healthcare, and community development, enabling them to effectively contribute to the national goal of reducing drug demand and rehabilitating affected individuals.
org: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment

title: DoSJE - Schemes for Welfare of SCs
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the various welfare schemes implemented by the Government of India for the upliftment of Scheduled Caste (SC) communities. It establishes the context of social justice and empowerment as a core tenet of governance, addressing historical disparities and promoting equal opportunities. The module is designed to equip learners with detailed knowledge of critical initiatives that span educational, economic, and social domains. Key learning areas include a thorough review of schemes such as the Scholarship for Higher Education for Young Achievers (SHREYAS), National Overseas Scholarship for SCs, and the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY). Additionally, it covers the legal frameworks supporting these efforts, including the implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955, and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify the objectives, eligibility criteria, and benefits of each scheme, enabling them to better support the implementation and outreach of these vital programs.
org: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment

title: DoT Guidelines on EMF Emissions
desc: This course delves into the critical subject of Electromagnetic Field (EMF) emissions and the regulatory landscape governed by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) in India. It begins by establishing the context of EMF, explaining electromagnetic energy, its types, and applications, highlighting the importance of managing its impact. The curriculum is structured to provide a thorough understanding of the Indian regulatory framework for EMR, comparing it with international standards like the ICNIRP guidelines. Participants will explore the specific guidelines issued to Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), State Governments, and Local Service Areas (LSAs), focusing on compliance, measurement, and mitigation. Upon completion, learners will be able to assess EMF exposure levels, interpret regulatory requirements, and apply best practices to ensure that telecom infrastructure operates safely and in full compliance with national laws, thereby safeguarding public health and maintaining regulatory integrity.

title: Double Jeopardy Legal Aid and Other Procedural Safeguards
desc: This course offers a comprehensive analysis of Chapter XXVI of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, which outlines general provisions for inquiries and trials. It is designed for legal and law enforcement professionals to understand the significant procedural changes introduced by the new criminal laws. The curriculum delves into the doctrine of 'autrefois acquit' and 'autrefois convict' (double jeopardy) under Section 337, ensuring learners can apply this constitutional protection correctly. It further clarifies the functions of public prosecutors, the process for obtaining permission for private prosecution, and the inviolable right of an accused person to be defended, including access to legal aid at the state's expense. The course also addresses specialized procedures, such as those applicable when a corporation is an accused party and the conditions under which a pardon may be tendered to an accomplice. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to navigate these crucial procedural safeguards effectively in their professional roles.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: DPI Foundation India Legal Journey of Identity Layer
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of India's pioneering journey in building a robust Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI). The curriculum is centered around the evolution of Aadhaar, the world's largest digital identity program, and its legal underpinnings. Participants will delve into the key legislative acts, such as the Information Technology Act 2000 and the Aadhaar Act 2016, which established the framework for cybersecurity, data privacy, and consent-driven identity. The course details the role of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), its biometric de-duplication technology, and its impact on reducing fraud in welfare schemes. Furthermore, it explores the transformative integration of Aadhaar with critical platforms like the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and DigiLocker, which have revolutionized financial services and governance. The course also introduces a Model Digital Identity Act, presenting India's experience as a scalable and privacy-conscious framework for other nations.
