By completing this course, railway staff will gain the confidence and skills to protect themselves and others, manage an incident calmly, and provide crucial support that can save lives.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: First Mile Connectivity in Coal Logistics
desc: This course provides an introduction to First Mile Connectivity (FMC) in India’s coal sector, with special focus on CIL and NCL. It explains how FMC replaces conventional road-based coal transportation with mechanized systems such as conveyor belts, coal handling plants, silos, and rapid loading systems to enable faster, cleaner, and more efficient coal movement from mine pitheads to railway sidings. Participants will gain an understanding of the FMC coal logistics chain—from extraction and crushing to mechanized conveying, computerized weighing, and rapid rail loading—and compare FMC with traditional truck-based transport in terms of efficiency, coal quality, environmental impact, safety, and cost. The course also highlights CIL’s FMC expansion strategy and outlines existing and upcoming FMC projects at NCL, positioning FMC as a key driver of coal logistics modernization, energy security, and sustainable infrastructure development.

title: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act 2003
desc: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003, is a critical piece of legislation that underpins India's fiscal architecture. This course offers an in-depth examination of the Act, explaining its significance in promoting fiscal discipline and ensuring the nation's long-term economic stability. It addresses the fundamental need for a structured approach to managing public finances, which is essential for sustainable growth and equitable resource distribution across generations. Participants will delve into the core components of the FRBM framework, including the mandated targets for fiscal and revenue deficits, and the prescribed limits on government debt as a percentage of GDP. The course will analyze the key policy statements required under the Act, such as the Macro-Economic Framework Statement and the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement. It also covers the mechanisms for reporting deviations and ensuring compliance.

title: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act 2003
desc: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003, is a critical piece of legislation that underpins India's fiscal architecture. This course offers an in-depth examination of the Act, explaining its significance in promoting fiscal discipline and ensuring the nation's long-term economic stability. It addresses the fundamental need for a structured approach to managing public finances, which is essential for sustainable growth and equitable resource distribution across generations. Participants will delve into the core components of the FRBM framework, including the mandated targets for fiscal and revenue deficits, and the prescribed limits on government debt as a percentage of GDP. The course will analyze the key policy statements required under the Act, such as the Macro-Economic Framework Statement and the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement. It also covers the mechanisms for reporting deviations and ensuring compliance. Upon completion, learners, particularly those in finance, economic affairs, and public administration, will be equipped to interpret fiscal indicators, understand the government's fiscal consolidation path, and appreciate the legal imperatives driving responsible budget management.

title: Flood basaltic lava flows: Their Morphology and Emplacement
desc: Delve into the fascinating world of volcanology with this detailed course on flood basaltic lava flows. Presented by the Geological Survey of India Training Institute, this program is designed to build a comprehensive understanding of the processes that form vast volcanic provinces like the Deccan Traps. The curriculum begins with an introduction to magma types and volcanic systems, establishing the fundamental principles of lava formation. You will learn the specific terminology and classification schemes used in geology, including the critical differences between simple and compound flows, as well as the Hawaiian-derived categories of Pahoehoe and A'a lavas. The course meticulously examines the internal structures, vesicle distribution, and jointing patterns that reveal the emplacement history of these flows. Through a series of lectures enriched with field examples, you will gain the ability to analyze morphological evidence to distinguish between different lava types and understand their geological significance. This knowledge is crucial for professionals involved in geological mapping, mineral exploration, and earth sciences research, enabling them to accurately interpret complex volcanic terrains.

title: Flood Management
desc: Floods are one of the most frequent and devastating natural disasters in India, causing significant loss of life, property, and livelihoods. Effective flood management is therefore a critical component of national disaster risk reduction strategy. This course is designed to provide public functionaries with a holistic overview of the challenges and approaches associated with managing flood risks. The curriculum introduces the fundamental concepts of flood management, starting with the definitions and causes of different types of floods. It maps out the flood-prone areas across India and details the methodologies for assessing flood-related damages. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to exploring a balanced approach to flood management, covering both traditional structural measures like dams and embankments, and modern non-structural measures such as early warning systems, floodplain zoning, and community-based disaster preparedness. Upon completion, learners will be equipped with the essential knowledge to understand the complexities of flood events. They will be better prepared to contribute to planning and implementation of flood mitigation projects and policies within their respective domains, ultimately strengthening community resilience against flood-related disasters.
org: National Institute of Disaster Management - NIDM

title: Flood-Disaster Response Training
desc: This foundational course is designed to build awareness and preparedness for flood-related emergencies. It begins by defining what constitutes a flood and categorizes the different types of floods that can occur. The curriculum delves into the common causes and the far-reaching effects of floods on communities, infrastructure, and the environment. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to practical, life-saving knowledge. Learners will be guided through the essential safety procedures to implement before, during, and after a flood to protect themselves and others. Furthermore, the course elucidates the vital contribution of volunteers in disaster situations, explaining how their organized efforts in rescue, relief, and rehabilitation complement the work of official agencies like the NDRF. Upon completion, participants will have a clear understanding of flood risks and the practical steps they can take to enhance safety and contribute effectively to community response.

title: FLUE GAS SYSTEM
desc: This course offers a detailed introduction to the essential components and functions of modern Flue Gas Systems. In the context of large-scale power generation, managing flue gas is critical for both operational efficiency and environmental compliance. This module explains why these systems are integral to thermal power plants. Key learning areas include a comprehensive overview of Air Preheaters (APH), detailing their various types, advantages, and principal heating components. The course also covers the role and basic principles of Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP) in controlling particulate emissions. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify and describe the function of these key systems, understand their contribution to the overall power generation cycle, and appreciate their importance in meeting environmental standards. This knowledge is fundamental for engineers, operators, and maintenance staff working in the power sector.

title: Fodder Bank Management and Livestock Feed Security in Himachal Pradesh
desc: A Fodder Bank is a planned area developed for the cultivation, storage, and management of quality fodder, with the objective of ensuring year-round feed availability for livestock, particularly during periods of scarcity. This course explores the concept and significance of fodder banks in the Mid-Himalayan region of Himachal Pradesh, where rugged terrain and seasonal fodder shortages often limit livestock productivity. The course also highlights how fodder banks contribute to sustainable livestock management, reduce pressure on natural forests, and support smallholder farmers in improving their livelihoods.

title: Folk And Minor Art in India
desc: Delve into the vibrant world of Indian folk and minor art to understand its profound cultural and historical significance. This course offers a detailed survey of indigenous art forms, highlighting their role as carriers of generational knowledge and evolving creative practices. You will explore the context in which these arts gained academic and national interest, particularly during the colonial era's revivalist movements. The curriculum covers a wide array of stylistic variations across different regions, from the narrative scrolls of Bengal to the intricate paintings of Madhubani. Learners will be equipped with analytical frameworks—semiotic, iconic, and thematic—to critically appreciate these artworks beyond their surface beauty. Furthermore, the course engages with contemporary challenges, discussing the impact of globalization, the importance of cultural sustainability, and the debate between preservation and commercialization. By the end, you will have a nuanced understanding of the ethos of Indian folk art and its place in the modern world.

title: Food Poisoning
desc: Food poisoning is a widespread yet preventable illness affecting millions globally. This introductory course is designed to build essential awareness and practical knowledge for preventing and controlling foodborne diseases. You will begin by learning the fundamental definition of food poisoning, its common bacterial causes such as Salmonella and E. coli, and the typical transmission routes. The course details the key symptoms, including nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, and identifies high-risk populations like young children and the elderly. A significant portion of the curriculum is dedicated to prevention, focusing on the globally recognized 'Clean, Separate, Cook, and Chill' strategy. You will learn about proper handwashing techniques, avoiding cross-contamination, cooking foods to the correct temperatures, and appropriate storage methods. The course also covers initial treatment steps, emphasizing hydration with ORS, and explains when to seek professional medical help. By completing this course, you will be equipped to apply effective food safety measures in daily life, contributing to the health and well-being of yourself and your community.

title: Foreign Service and Deputation and Lien in Indian Railways
desc: This course provides Indian Railways officers with a practical understanding of the concepts and rules governing Foreign Service, Deputation, and Lien. It covers various forms of deputation, including assignments to Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), autonomous bodies, international organisations, and positions under the Central Staffing Scheme (CSS). Learners will gain insights into eligibility criteria, application and selection procedures, tenure, extensions, cooling-off periods, promotion-related provisions, maintenance of lien, and pay fixation during deputation. By the end of the course, participants will have a clear understanding of the administrative procedures, service conditions, employee rights, and financial implications associated with deputation and foreign service in Indian Railways.

title: Forensic Accounting  and Internal Controls for Fraud Prevention
desc: This course introduces the essential competencies for effective forensic accounting and emphasizes the critical role of internal controls in fraud prevention. It integrates financial forensics, investigative techniques, and critical thinking with practical control mechanisms applied in organizational and defence finance environments. Participants will learn how forensic accountants analyse financial irregularities, gather and evaluate evidence, and apply professional scepticism to detect fraud. The course also covers internal control systems, including preventive, detective, and corrective measures, and highlights the importance of segregation of duties in mitigating fraud risk. By combining behavioural insights with robust control frameworks, learners will be equipped to identify vulnerabilities, strengthen governance systems, and enhance financial integrity in high-risk environments.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Forensic Physical Evidence: Collection and Analysis
desc: This course delves into the essential principles of handling forensic physical evidence, a cornerstone of the modern justice system. It begins by establishing the context of why physical evidence is considered an unbiased witness, capable of corroborating statements, reconstructing events, and ensuring justice is served. Key learning areas include the systematic identification, documentation, and preservation of a wide range of evidence types, such as biological samples (DNA, blood), trace materials (fibers, glass), ballistics, and digital evidence from devices like mobile phones and hard disks. A significant focus is placed on the meticulous procedures required to maintain the chain of custody, which is vital for the legal integrity and admissibility of evidence in court. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to understand how proper evidence handling strengthens investigations, supports expert testimony, and ultimately contributes to building robust, evidence-based cases that can both secure convictions and exonerate the innocent.

title: Forest Fire Hazard and Safety-Disaster Response Training
desc: Forest fires pose a significant threat to our natural ecosystems, biodiversity, and the safety of communities living near forested areas. Effective management and response are crucial to mitigate their destructive impact. This course is designed to build foundational knowledge in forest fire hazards, safety, and disaster response, providing a critical learning resource for public officials, disaster response personnel, and community volunteers. The curriculum delves into the core aspects of forest fire management. You will learn to identify the various types of forest fires and their primary causes, from natural phenomena to human activities. The course provides detailed guidelines on proactive prevention measures and strategic control techniques used to manage an active fire. A significant portion is dedicated to safety protocols, outlining the essential precautions that must be taken before, during, and after a forest fire to protect lives and property. Furthermore, the training elucidates the indispensable role of volunteers in supporting official response efforts, including prevention, control, and ensuring the safety of local populations. Upon completion, learners will have a clear understanding of forest fire dynamics and be better prepared to contribute to safety and response activities within their communities, fostering a more resilient approach to disaster management.

title: Forest Landscapes of Assam: Forging Livelihoods and Sustainability
desc: On 1st November 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi put forward Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) at COP26 in Glasgow, committing to sustainable living based on conservation and moderation. In Assam, this vision found resonance in grassroots forest conservation. Bamboo, once termed the “Poor man’s timber” or “Miracle grass”, is increasingly becoming the “Kalpavriksh” of modern times for its potential in green, sustainable solutions. From 2021 to 2024, forest officers Ms. Dimpi Bora in Kamrup and Mr. Tejas Marishwamy in Goalpara supported forest-fringe communities through bamboo jewellery, handicrafts, traditional bamboo enterprises and ecotourism. Their community-centric solutions reduced forest dependence while supporting livelihoods and restoring forestlands. This case study explores how traditional knowledge, community engagement and sustainable livelihoods can strengthen forest conservation.

title: Forest Resource Management
desc: Forest Resource Management is an essential course for understanding the multifaceted approach to governing and conserving India's vital forest ecosystems. The curriculum addresses the importance of forests in the national context, starting with the constitutional provisions and legal mandates that shape their protection. You will explore the diverse range of forest products, from timber to non-timber items, and the critical ecosystem services they provide, including biodiversity support, climate regulation, and watershed protection. The course details the principles of forest classification, structure, and the core concepts of sustainable management, such as working plans and multiple-use strategies. It also confronts the real-world challenges of encroachment, poaching, and illicit felling. By examining the role of forests in environmental conservation, including soil moisture retention and erosion prevention, learners will be equipped to contribute to the sustainable stewardship of these invaluable natural resources.
org: Chandrapur Forest Academy of Administration and Management

title: Forest Rights Act - English Version
desc: Designed for civil servants and officials involved in tribal welfare and forest administration, this course offers a detailed examination of the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006. It begins by establishing the context of the Act, detailing the historical injustices faced by forest-dwelling tribal communities and the legislative intent to correct them. The curriculum delves into the specific provisions of the FRA, outlining the nature of individual and community rights, including habitation, cultivation, and the right to minor forest produce. Participants will learn the procedural aspects of the law, such as the forms used for claims, the evidence required for verification, and the critical roles of the Gram Sabha, Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC), and District Level Committee (DLC). The course aims to empower officials to not only process claims but also to provide post-recognition support, fostering livelihood improvement and sustainable forest management, thereby fulfilling the Act's mandate of social justice and empowerment.

title: Forest Rights Act - Hindi Version
desc: भारत में लाखों लोग, विशेषकर आदिवासी समुदाय, सदियों से वनों में निवास करते आए हैं, लेकिन ब्रिटिश काल के कानूनों ने उन्हें अपनी ही भूमि पर अतिक्रमणकारी बना दिया। इस ऐतिहासिक अन्याय को दूर करने के लिए 2006 में वन अधिकार अधिनियम (FRA) लागू किया गया। यह पाठ्यक्रम इसी महत्वपूर्ण कानून पर केंद्रित है, जो सिविल सेवकों को इसके प्रभावी कार्यान्वयन के लिए आवश्यक ज्ञान और कौशल से लैस करता है। पाठ्यक्रम में वनवासी समुदायों के संघर्ष के इतिहास, एफआरए के तहत मान्यता प्राप्त विभिन्न अधिकारों (जैसे व्यक्तिगत, सामुदायिक और आजीविका संबंधी अधिकार) और इन अधिकारों का दावा करने की प्रक्रिया को विस्तार से समझाया गया है। शिक्षार्थी दावा प्रक्रिया में ग्राम सभा, उप-मंडल स्तरीय समिति (SDLC) और जिला स्तरीय समिति (DLC) की भूमिकाओं और जिम्मेदारियों को समझेंगे। यह पाठ्यक्रम अधिकारियों को एफआरए को प्रभावी ढंग से लागू करने और वनवासी समुदायों के लिए न्याय सुनिश्चित करने में सक्षम बनाएगा, जिससे सतत वन प्रबंधन और सामुदायिक सशक्तिकरण को बढ़ावा मिलेगा।

title: Forests and their Management
desc: Delve into the essential field of forest management and its increasing importance in a world facing climate change. This course offers a structured journey through the core concepts of forestry, from defining what constitutes a forest to the complex methodologies used in its valuation. You will explore why managing forests is crucial, not just for timber and produce, but for ensuring food and water security, preserving wildlife, and regulating climate. The curriculum covers the principles and practices of silviculture, highlighting how forests are managed to balance economic benefits with ecological sustainability. The course also introduces learners to new and emerging trends in the field, including the use of novel technologies, urban silviculture, and the creation of pollinator gardens. Upon completion, you will have a robust understanding of how to manage forests as a vital natural resource for both present and future generations.

title: Forfeiture of Illegally Acquired Property under the NDPS Act
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the forfeiture of illegally acquired property under Chapter VA of the NDPS Act. Learners will gain a clear understanding of the legal and procedural framework for tracing, identifying, freezing, and seizing property obtained through drug-related offences. The module covers key provisions of the Act, the evaluation of assets, and the final forfeiture process. It also explains the responsibilities and powers of investigating officers and the Competent Authority, as well as the burden of proof placed on affected persons. By engaging with practical examples and scenarios, learners develop the knowledge needed to apply these provisions effectively and ensure that offenders do not benefit financially from narcotics-related crimes.
org: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy
keywords: Forfeiture of Illegal Property Rights - NDPS ACT

title: Formalities of Joining Service
desc: This foundational course is designed to equip new government employees with a comprehensive understanding of the essential formalities upon entering public service. Joining the government involves a series of critical procedural steps that are crucial for establishing a formal service record. This program demystifies these processes, ensuring that new entrants can navigate their initial administrative requirements with confidence and clarity. The course delves into the specific documentation and procedural requirements that every new official must complete. A significant portion of the curriculum is dedicated to the Service Book, which is the master document of an employee's entire career history. Learners will explore the different sections of the Service Book, understand the importance of each entry, and learn the correct procedures for its maintenance, including updates, verifications, and safekeeping. Upon completion, participants will be able to confidently manage their joining formalities and appreciate the significance of maintaining an accurate and up-to-date Service Book. This knowledge is fundamental for ensuring proper record-keeping, which impacts promotions, transfers, and retirement benefits, laying a strong foundation for a well-managed career in government service.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Formation of New Cooperative Societies: Single-State and Multi-State
desc: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the process of forming cooperative societies in India, whether at the state level or across multiple states. It introduces learners to the concept, identity, and purpose of cooperative societies and their role in socio-economic development. The course explains the legal and institutional framework governing cooperatives, including the role of the Registrar and relevant Cooperative Societies Acts. It further covers the step-by-step formation process, including preparation of registration-ready applications and effective handling of scrutiny by the Registrar. In addition, the course highlights the differences between State-level registration and the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) route, enabling learners to understand the appropriate legal pathway based on operational scope and objectives.

title: Formulation of Public Policies
desc: This foundational course is designed to equip public officials with a thorough understanding of the intricate process of public policy formulation. It addresses the critical question of how government decisions are made, translated into actionable policies, and prepared for implementation. The course begins by examining the concept of agenda setting, exploring how certain issues gain prominence and become priorities for government action. Participants will then delve into the core of policy formulation, learning about the various models and frameworks used to design effective policies. Key topics include the role of research, stakeholder consultation, and evidence-based analysis in shaping policy alternatives. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to the decision-making phase, analyzing the factors that influence government choices and the mechanisms for formal approval. Furthermore, learners will be introduced to the principles of policy appraisal and assessment, gaining skills to critically evaluate the potential impacts and feasibility of proposed policies. Upon completion, participants will be able to navigate the policy landscape with greater confidence and support the creation of robust public policies.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Forward Auction for Buyers or Bidders on GeM
desc: This course offers a detailed exploration of the Forward Auction functionality within the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). It addresses the critical need for a transparent and competitive method for government entities to dispose of surplus, obsolete, or scrap assets. The curriculum is structured to guide both buyers (auction creators) and bidders through the entire lifecycle of a Forward Auction. Key learning areas include creating and configuring an auction, understanding bidding parameters, applying effective bidding strategies for price discovery, and managing all post-auction procedures to ensure compliance. By completing this course, participants will gain the practical skills and procedural knowledge required to confidently and successfully utilize the GeM Forward Auction module, maximizing value and upholding transparency in public asset disposal.

title: Forward Auction for Sellers or Auctioneers on GeM
desc: This course is designed to equip sellers and auctioneers with a practical understanding of the Forward Auction process on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). As a critical e-procurement tool, Forward Auctions are used by government entities to sell goods through a competitive and transparent mechanism. This program demystifies the entire workflow, clarifying the roles and responsibilities involved in creating and managing auctions. Participants will be guided through the end-to-end auction lifecycle, including pre-auction preparation, live auction participation, and post-auction formalities. Key areas of focus include navigating the GeM interface, applying effective pricing and bidding strategies, ensuring compliance with platform policies, and understanding grievance redressal mechanisms. Upon completion, learners will be prepared to strategically participate in Forward Auctions, maximizing their opportunities on the GeM platform.

title: Foundation Course on Cyber Security
desc: In today's digital-first governance landscape, understanding and mitigating cyber threats is crucial for all public officials. This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the world of cyber security, establishing a baseline of knowledge for personnel across all government departments. It delves into the various facets of cyber threats, explaining how seemingly simple actions can lead to significant security incidents. Key learning areas include identifying common attack vectors like phishing and malware, implementing robust password policies, and understanding the principles of data protection and risk management. The curriculum also covers the importance of network security, incident handling procedures, and the legal framework provided by the IT Act. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped with the practical knowledge and skills to apply essential cyber hygiene, contributing to a more secure and resilient digital infrastructure for the nation.
org: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC)

title: Foundation of Criminal Law and Individual Rights
desc: This course introduces the basic concepts of criminal law in a simple, practical, and easy-to-understand manner. It helps learners understand what constitutes a crime, the rights and duties of citizens, and how the criminal justice system functions in everyday life. The course covers important topics such as FIR, bail, police powers, rights of the accused and victims, and the role of courts and investigative agencies. Through real-life examples and scenarios, learners will gain clarity on how to respond to legal situations and protect their rights. By the end of the course, learners will feel more confident in dealing with legal issues and will develop an awareness of law as a tool for justice, safety, and responsible citizenship.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Foundational Overview of Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System
desc: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS), a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India. The course explains the structure, governance framework, and technical architecture of ICJS and how it enables seamless digital integration across the key pillars of the criminal justice system, including Police (CCTNS), e-Prisons, e-Prosecution, e-Forensics, and e-Courts. It highlights the core principle of “One Data, One Entry”, enabling real-time data sharing, interoperability, and advanced search and analytics capabilities across criminal justice databases. The course also traces the digital case lifecycle—from investigation to trial and incarceration—demonstrating how integrated systems improve coordination and efficiency.
org: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy

title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence: Applications and Ethics
desc: This comprehensive course offers a foundational introduction to the transformative field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its relevance in the modern world. It is designed to demystify AI for beginners, explaining how intelligent systems are built to mimic human cognitive functions. The curriculum begins with the core concepts of AI and delves into the primary categories of machine learning: supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning. Through practical examples, learners will explore how these technologies are applied across various sectors, including healthcare diagnostics, financial fraud detection, and weather forecasting, illustrating AI's broad societal impact. A crucial component of this course is the focus on responsible AI. It addresses the ethical dimensions of developing and deploying AI, emphasizing the importance of fairness, transparency, accountability, and data privacy to ensure these technologies are used for inclusive and equitable outcomes. Upon completion, learners will possess a solid understanding of AI principles, be able to identify its key applications, and appreciate the ethical considerations necessary for its responsible implementation in governance and public service.
subDomain: Digital Tools ( MS office, Excel, & PPT) & Platforms

title: Foundations of Behavioural Safety In Defence Operations
desc: The Behavioral Safety for Industrial Workers in the Indian Defence Sector  course equips personnel working in high-hazard environments with the knowledge and practical skills to recognize, prevent, and mitigate behavioral risks that lead to workplace incidents. Designed for industrial workers in defence production establishments, ordnance factories, DRDO laboratories, and Armed Forces maintenance facilities. Course covers behavioural safety principles, common unsafe behaviours, accident causation theories, real-life defence case studies, and practical mitigation strategies. Learners explore internationally recognized safety frameworks such as Heinrich's Domino Theory, Frank Bird's Loss Causation Model, the Swiss Cheese Model, and Behaviour-Based Safety (BBS). The course emphasizes compliance with the Explosives Rules, 2008, DGQA guidelines, and safe work practices to foster a proactive safety culture, reduce human error, and strengthen operational safety in high-risk defence industry.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Foundations of Cyber Safety in Public Service
desc:
Foundations of Cyber Safety in Public Service
 is a structured learning pathway designed for government officials across departments and levels, particularly those engaged in digital systems, data management, and technology-enabled governance. Curated with courses from IIT Madras, NeGD, and upGrad, it combines academic excellence, policy insights, and industry best practices to build essential cybersecurity capabilities. Learners develop a strong foundation in cyber hygiene, digital risk management, cyber governance, and secure digital practices. A pre-assessment benchmarks existing knowledge, while a post-assessment evaluates learning outcomes and the ability to apply cybersecurity principles in government contexts, enabling officials to contribute to a secure and resilient digital governance ecosystem.

title: Foundations of Defence Industrial Optimization
desc: This course offers a strategic introduction to the optimization of India's Defence Industrial Base (DIB), a cornerstone of national sovereignty and technological advancement. It is designed for professionals seeking to understand the complex interplay between policy, industry, and national security. The curriculum delves into the historical context and evolution of India's defence industry, providing crucial context for current government initiatives like 'Make in India' and 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat'. Key learning areas include the intricacies of the Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP), the strategic importance of technology transfer for building indigenous capabilities, and the necessity of creating robust and resilient supply chains. The course also explores the transformative potential of emerging technologies like AI and robotics in modern defence. Upon completion, learners will be equipped with the foundational knowledge to contribute to policy discussions and strategic planning aimed at building a self-sufficient and globally competitive defence ecosystem.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Foundations of Effective Decision-Making in Governance
desc: Foundations of Effective Decision-Making in Governance equips government officials with practical tools to make informed, evidence-based, and accountable decisions in public administration. The course introduces four essential decision-making frameworks: Cause and Effect Analysis, Conflict Management using the CUDSA model, Data Gathering and Presentation, and the Ladder of Inference. Through realistic governance scenarios, interactive case studies, and practical exercises, participants learn to identify root causes of administrative problems, resolve workplace conflicts constructively, collect and analyse data for evidence-based decisions, and distinguish facts from assumptions to avoid cognitive bias. The course promotes systematic problem-solving, collaboration, transparency, and preventive governance, enabling officers to improve service delivery, strengthen interdepartmental coordination, and achieve better governance outcomes.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Foundations of Geographic Information Systems
desc: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and their applications in geospatial analysis. Learners will explore how GIS integrates spatial data through thematic layers to store, analyse, and visualise information for real-world decision-making. The course covers key GIS functions, the characteristics of spatial data, and the roles of geospatial, attribute, and metadata. Participants will understand the differences between raster, vector, and 3D data models, and gain a practical overview of datums, map projections, and coordinate systems. The course also introduces the QGIS interface and its core tools, providing learners with a hands-on understanding of GIS capabilities for managing and interpreting spatial information effectively.
org: Department of Space and ISRO HQ

title: Foundations of Industrial Security Management
desc: In today's interconnected and globalised industrial landscape, securing critical assets, infrastructure, and intellectual property is paramount for organisational success. This course, "Foundations of Industrial Security Management," offers a comprehensive introduction to the principles and practices that underpin modern security operations. It moves beyond traditional reactive approaches to present security as a proactive and strategic management function essential for enabling growth and building trust. Participants will delve into the core concepts of security planning, exploring structured frameworks like POSDCORB to guide decision-making. The curriculum thoroughly examines a wide spectrum of threats, from physical risks like sabotage and espionage to complex cyberattacks, using real-world case studies such as the DRDO espionage incident and the Saudi Aramco cyberattack to provide practical context. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped to identify and categorise security risks, understand the strategic importance of intellectual property protection, and appreciate the evolving role of the security manager as a key business partner. This foundational knowledge is crucial for anyone involved in protecting organisational assets and ensuring operational resilience.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Foundations of Investigation: FIR Crime Scene and Evidence Handling
desc: This course provides a practical understanding of the essential procedures that police officers must follow during criminal investigations, updated according to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. It addresses the critical importance of the new criminal laws in ensuring investigations are conducted with fairness, transparency, and efficiency. Key learning areas include the complete lifecycle of a First Information Report (FIR), from initial registration to handling special cases like e-FIRs, Zero FIRs, and information from vulnerable informants. The curriculum delves into modern crime scene documentation, emphasizing the role of photography and videography as mandated by new legal provisions. Furthermore, learners will master the protocols for evidence collection, including physical, documentary, and digital evidence like voice samples, and the correct execution of search and seizure operations. Upon completion, officers will be equipped to apply these updated legal and procedural standards, enhancing the integrity and legal validity of their investigative work.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: Foundations of Management and Organisational Behaviour
desc: Designed for current and aspiring healthcare leaders, this course delves into the core principles of effective management and organizational dynamics. It begins by tracing the historical evolution of management theories, including the contributions of Taylor, Fayol, and the Human Relations Movement, providing context for today's practices. The curriculum emphasizes the application of these theories within the unique environment of healthcare, where compassionate and efficient service delivery is paramount. Key learning areas include strategic planning, organizing resources, leading teams, and controlling processes to achieve institutional goals. The course also introduces systems thinking, enabling leaders to understand and manage healthcare organizations as complex, adaptive systems. Participants will learn to apply participative management, Management by Objectives (MBO), and other frameworks to foster a culture of accountability, improve team performance, and ultimately deliver high-quality, patient-centered care.

title: Foundations of Personal Finance and Investing
desc: Embark on your financial journey with this comprehensive introductory course designed for anyone new to personal finance and investing. The course addresses the critical need for financial literacy by breaking down complex concepts into simple, actionable steps. You will learn to create and manage a personal budget, set achievable financial goals using the SMART framework, and grasp the fundamental principles of risk and return. The curriculum delves into key investment concepts such as the impact of inflation on purchasing power and the long-term benefits of compounding. It provides a practical overview of popular investment options available in India, including mutual funds and stocks, and guides you through the process of opening a Demat account. By the end of this course, you will have the confidence and knowledge to manage your money effectively, avoid common financial pitfalls, and start building a diversified investment portfolio.

title: Foundations of Public Policy and Policy Analysis
desc: This course introduces participants to the fundamentals of public policy and provides analytical tools to understand, evaluate, and design effective policies. It offers a clear understanding of why governments take certain actions, how policy decisions are formulated, and how systematic analysis can improve decision-making processes. Through real-world examples from sectors such as health, environment, and digital governance, learners gain both theoretical grounding and practical insights into the functioning of public policy. The course emphasizes structured thinking and evidence-based analysis to help learners engage meaningfully with policy issues and governance challenges.

title: Foundations of Quantum Computing
desc: This course provides a structured introduction to quantum computing, covering its theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and strategic significance. Participants will explore the core principles of quantum mechanics that enable quantum computation, including superposition, entanglement, quantum gates, interference, and measurement. The course explains how quantum circuits function, how qubits differ fundamentally from classical bits, and why quantum algorithms provide computational advantages for specific classes of problems. It also examines current industry trends and emerging applications in optimization, drug discovery, materials science, cryptography, finance, and cybersecurity. The curriculum highlights global strategic developments, including India’s National Quantum Mission, and discusses the current NISQ (Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum) era, hybrid quantum-classical models, and key technical challenges such as noise and error correction.
org: National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology - NIELIT (formerly DOEACC Society)

title: Foundations of the Right to Information Act 2005
desc: Foundations of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is an essential course for public functionaries that provides a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles and provisions of the RTI Act. The course explores the purpose, scope, and applicability of the Act, along with the institutional framework established for facilitating access to information, including the roles and responsibilities of Public Information Officers (PIOs) and Appellate Authorities. Participants will gain an understanding of the procedures for receiving and responding to RTI applications, applicable timelines, and the categories of information exempt from disclosure. The course also highlights the legal obligations of public functionaries and the importance of adhering to the prescribed processes for effective implementation of the Act.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Framing and Amendment of Recruitment Rules
desc: This course on 'Framing and Amendment of Recruitment Rules' is designed to equip government officials with the necessary skills to manage the lifecycle of recruitment regulations. In the context of public administration, well-defined recruitment rules are critical for ensuring transparency, fairness, and the intake of qualified personnel. This program delves into the core principles and detailed procedures as prescribed by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). Key learning areas include understanding the constitutional basis for rule-making, the process of drafting new rules, and the protocols for carrying out amendments. Participants will explore how to accurately define job requirements, qualifications, and selection methods in alignment with governmental standards.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Framing and Amendment of Recruitment Rules
desc: This course on 'Framing and Amendment of Recruitment Rules' is designed to equip government officials with the necessary skills to manage the lifecycle of recruitment regulations. In the context of public administration, well-defined recruitment rules are critical for ensuring transparency, fairness, and the intake of qualified personnel. This program delves into the core principles and detailed procedures as prescribed by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). Key learning areas include understanding the constitutional basis for rule-making, the process of drafting new rules, and the protocols for carrying out amendments. Participants will explore how to accurately define job requirements, qualifications, and selection methods in alignment with governmental standards. By the end of this course, learners will be able to confidently navigate the complexities of the recruitment rule process, contributing to robust and compliant human resource management within their departments.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Framing of Policies Schemes for Promoting Welfare Measures
desc: This course delves into the critical area of employee welfare, a cornerstone of effective human resource management within the Central Government. It establishes the context by explaining why promoting the well-being of government employees is essential for organizational productivity and morale. The curriculum provides a detailed examination of the policies and schemes designed to foster a supportive and engaging work environment. Key learning areas include an in-depth look at the recreational and cultural initiatives undertaken by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), and the specific sports programs managed by the Central Civil Services Cultural & Sports Board (CCSCSB). Participants will gain a thorough understanding of the various schemes and financial incentives available to encourage employee participation in sports and cultural events. Upon completion, learners, particularly those in administrative and HR roles, will be equipped to better understand, communicate, and contribute to the implementation of these vital welfare measures, thereby fostering a more motivated and resilient workforce.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Fraud Risk Management In High Risk Environments
desc: This course provides an in-depth exploration of the behavioural, psychological, and structural dimensions of fraud in high-risk environments, such as defence procurement and public finance. It introduces participants to advanced forensic frameworks including the M.I.C.E. model, Fraud Diamond, Fraud Scale, Triangle of Fraud Action, and Dorminey’s Meta Model to explain why fraud occurs, how it is executed, and strategies to prevent it. Participants will learn to analyse behavioural red flags using global ACFE insights, differentiate between accidental and predator fraudsters, and evaluate capability-driven fraud risks. The course integrates motivation, execution, concealment, and asset conversion into a unified fraud lifecycle approach, linking these concepts to governance, internal controls, and regulatory interventions.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Frauds and Risks Management in India Post
desc: This program is designed to equip Department of Posts employees with the necessary knowledge to effectively manage frauds and risks associated with postal financial services. The course begins by establishing the context of risk in a modernized, core banking environment and outlines the primary objectives of the Fraud and Risk Management Unit (FRMU), from risk assessment to compliance. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to detailing the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for handling FRMU alerts. Learners will be guided through the step-by-step verification process at the Divisional, Head Office, and Sub-Office levels. It covers specific scenarios, including the revival of silent accounts, premature closures of schemes like PPF, and discharge of NSC/KVP certificates. Upon completion, participants will be able to apply these procedures meticulously, ensuring regulatory compliance, preventing financial misappropriation, and securing India Post's vast network of financial services.

title: Free Space Optics
desc: This course offers a detailed exploration of Free Space Optics (FSO) communication, a cutting-edge technology for high-speed data transmission. The curriculum begins by defining FSO and tracing its origins to Alexander Graham Bell's photophone, before delving into the modern systems that deliver data rates comparable to fiber optics. Participants will learn about the core components and network architecture of FSO systems, including transmitters, receivers, and operating wavelengths, with a focus on the 1550 nm spectrum for eye safety and performance. The course thoroughly examines the compelling benefits of FSO, such as its protocol independence, immunity to electromagnetic interference, high security, and cost-effective, rapid deployment for applications like building-to-building connectivity, disaster recovery, and mobile backhaul. To provide a balanced perspective, it also covers the significant limitations posed by environmental factors like fog, scintillation, and physical obstructions. Upon completion, learners will have a solid understanding of where and why FSO technology is a critical component in expanding modern telecommunication networks.

title: Freight Business in Indian Railways
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the Indian Railways freight business, covering its scale, key commodities, wagons, and logistics operations. It explains freight rate classification and tariffs, booking and delivery procedures supported by the Freight Operations Information System (FOIS), and customer-focused incentive schemes. The course also addresses handling norms, penalties, and operational best practices to ensure efficient, safe, and timely freight movement.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: Freight Train Examination and Brake Power Certification
desc: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of freight train examination in railways. Learners will explore the official sources that provide instructions for conducting examinations and understand the criteria for earning points and certificates during the process. The course covers the frequency of examinations for different types of rolling stock and details the steps involved in performing an intensive examination, including associated repair activities. Participants will learn the procedure for issuing the Brake Power Certificate (BPC), including issuing it after the attachment of a locomotive. Additional topics include air brake testing, brake gear limits and clearances, piston stroke values for different wagon types, standard buffer height, and the nominal clearance parameters and wear limits of CASNUB bogies.

title: Freight Train Operation in Indian Railways
desc: This foundational course offers an in-depth understanding of the freight train operations that form the backbone of Indian Railways' revenue and the country's transportation infrastructure. Participants will begin by learning the broad classifications of goods trains and the intricate factors that make freight operations more complex than passenger services. The curriculum details the crucial roles played by various agencies, from the on-ground control offices responsible for daily planning and execution to the strategic oversight provided by Zonal Headquarters and the Railway Board. A significant focus is placed on understanding and evaluating operational efficiency. Learners will be introduced to key performance indices such as Wagon Turnaround, locomotive utilization, interchange balance, and average speed. By the end of this course, participants will have a solid grasp of the entire freight management lifecycle, from resource planning and train ordering to performance monitoring using systems like the Freight Operations Information System (FOIS), enabling them to appreciate the scale and precision required in railway logistics.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: From Criticism to Growth: Navigating Feedback Effectively
desc: In the public sector, effective governance is built on a foundation of clear communication, accountability, and a commitment to continuous improvement. This course addresses a critical component of this foundation: the ability to navigate feedback constructively. It moves beyond the basics of delivering feedback to focus on the transformative power of receiving it well. Participants will learn to overcome common barriers such as defensiveness and fear, turning feedback into a powerful tool for self-development. The curriculum covers key areas including understanding the dual dimensions of feedback, applying strategies for both giving and receiving it, and reflecting on its value to drive performance. By the end of this course, learners will be able to apply these skills to foster transparency, strengthen decision-making, and build high-performing teams. This will not only enhance their individual career growth but also contribute to a more efficient, accountable, and citizen-centric public service.
org: Ministry of Communications- Department of Telecommunications

title: From Darkness to Dignity: Transformation of Malapur - Teaching Note
desc:
Malapur, a tribal settlement in the Satpura Hills of Maharashtra, remained cut off from welfare delivery due to absence of electricity and lack of updated Aadhaar identities. 550 residents were excluded from schemes such as PMAY, PM Vishwakarma Yojana, and nutrition programmes, as digital authentication could not function in an off-grid environment.

The case traces how two frontline postal officials — MTS Dhande and BPM Chavhan — identified these failures and responded with a field innovation. They designed and executed a portable solar-powered Aadhaar camp, carrying panels, batteries, laptops, and biometric equipment on foot across steep terrain. Over six days, they delivered Aadhaar updation, opened 341 India Post Payments Bank accounts, enabled DBT linkage, and facilitated welfare enrolment. The intervention covered all 550 persons. DBT linkage enabled rooftop solar installation in every household, bringing electricity to Malapur for the first time.

title: From Gridlock to Growth: Impact of PRAGATI in India and Beyond
desc: This course provides an in-depth analysis of India's PRAGATI, a pioneering digital governance system designed to accelerate the implementation of critical national projects. It addresses the common challenges of delays and cost overruns in public sector initiatives by showcasing a unique solution that combines technology with decisive leadership. The curriculum delves into the core components of the PRAGATI ecosystem, including the role of the Prime Minister's direct oversight, the use of integrated digital tools like Gati Shakti for real-time data monitoring, and the fostering of a 'Team India' culture to break down administrative silos between central and state governments. Learners will explore real-world case studies, from complex railway links to national social welfare schemes, to understand how this model resolves bottlenecks and drives an outcome-oriented approach. By the end of the course, participants will be able to identify the key principles of the PRAGATI framework and evaluate how its lessons in digital transformation and collaborative governance can be applied to enhance public administration and project delivery in various contexts.

title: From Legacy to Smart: The Analytics Transformation of Indian Utilities
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of how data analytics is revolutionizing the Power and Utilities (P&U) sector. In an era of digital transformation, leveraging operational data from sources like IoT devices and smart grids is crucial for maintaining a competitive edge and ensuring service reliability. The curriculum delves into practical applications, demonstrating how predictive maintenance can prevent equipment failure, how energy forecasting can balance supply and demand, and how asset optimization can maximize returns on infrastructure investments. Furthermore, the course addresses the foundational elements required for a successful analytics journey, including robust digital infrastructure, effective data governance, and a skilled workforce. It also examines common hurdles such as legacy systems, data silos, and cybersecurity risks, offering actionable strategies to mitigate them. Learners will leave equipped to champion a data-driven culture within their organizations, applying analytical insights to enhance efficiency, sustainability, and decision-making in utility operations.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: From Rural to Digital Markets: E-Saras-ONDC partnership for SHG
desc: The Deen Dayal Upadhyay National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) launched e-SARAS, a digital marketing initiative to expand market access for Self-Help Groups (SHGs) facing challenges like limited reach, poor quality control, and weak linkages. Through eSARAS.in, SHG women artisans showcased handcrafted products online. To strengthen this effort, NRLM partnered with the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) to enhance outreach and create stronger forward linkages. However, differences in institutional structures, policy shifts, and SHGs’ limited production capacity created challenges. While digital marketing improved visibility and demand, supply-side gaps persisted. The success of e-SARAS now depends on sustained NRLM–ONDC collaboration, capacity building, and stronger supply chain systems to ensure long-term growth and rural women’s economic empowerment.

title: FRSR Part I - General Rules
desc: The Fundamental Rules and Supplementary Rules (FRSR) form the bedrock of service-related administration for Central Government employees. A thorough understanding of these regulations is essential for officials to ensure consistent, fair, and compliant management of personnel matters. This course is designed to provide a detailed examination of FRSR Part I - General Rules, covering the entire lifecycle of a government servant from appointment to retirement. Participants will gain in-depth knowledge of critical topics including general conditions of service, pay fixation, special allowances, and combination of appointments. The curriculum also addresses complex situations such as deputation out of India, dismissal, removal, and suspension, along with rules for retirement and foreign service. Through a structured review of these regulations, supported by the latest government decisions and amendments, learners will develop the capability to accurately interpret and apply the FRSR. Upon completion, officials will be equipped to handle service and pay-related matters with greater confidence and precision, fostering responsible and effective public administration.

title: FRSR Part II - Travelling Allowances Rules
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the Travelling Allowance (TA) Rules applicable to central government employees, as specified in FRSR Part II. In the context of public service, correct and compliant management of travel-related expenditure is crucial for maintaining financial discipline and transparency. This program is designed to equip learners with the necessary knowledge to navigate these regulations effectively. Key learning areas include the classification of different travel entitlements, conditions for admissibility of allowances for journeys on tour, transfer, and retirement, and the procedures for calculating and claiming reimbursements. The course breaks down complex rules into understandable modules, focusing on practical application. Upon completion, learners will be able to confidently prepare and process TA claims, ensure compliance with the latest government orders, and avoid common errors, thereby contributing to efficient financial administration within their departments.

title: FRSR Part IV - Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) Rules
desc: This course delves into the specifics of Fundamental Rules and Supplementary Rules (FRSR) Part IV, focusing on Dearness Allowance (DA), Dearness Relief (DR), and Contributory Provident Fund (CPF) Rules applicable to Central Government Employees. The primary objective is to familiarize officials with this critical set of regulations, enhancing their understanding and practical skills. The curriculum is structured to explain the different types of allowances, their calculation, and applicability. Through a series of factsheets and illustrative case studies, participants will learn to confidently manage their responsibilities, ensure compliance, and apply the correct practices in handling matters related to DA and DR. Upon completion, learners will be proficient in interpreting and applying these essential financial rules in their day-to-day work, ensuring accuracy and adherence to government norms.

title: FRSR Part V - House Rent Allowances and Other Allowances
desc: This specialized course delves into the specifics of Fundamental Rules and Supplementary Rules (FRSR) Part V, which governs the provision of House Rent Allowance (HRA) and other critical allowances for Central Government personnel. In the context of public administration, the correct and timely disbursement of allowances is crucial for employee morale and financial integrity. This program is designed to build a strong foundational knowledge for officials responsible for handling these financial matters. Key learning areas include the conditions for admissibility of HRA, rules for other compensatory allowances, and the procedural requirements for claims and disbursement. Participants will learn to interpret the rules accurately, apply them to various employee scenarios, and handle complex cases with confidence. Upon completion, learners will be proficient in managing HRA and other allowance-related responsibilities, fostering transparency and accountability within their departments.

title: FTTH OLT (Optical Line Terminal)
desc: Dive into the technical fundamentals of modern broadband delivery with this course on FTTH Optical Line Terminals (OLT). The program begins by establishing the context of Passive Optical Network (PON) technology, explaining how a single fiber from a service provider can serve multiple premises. It then progresses to the working principles of GPON, detailing the use of Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) for upstream and downstream data streaming and TDMA for managing subscriber data packets. Participants will gain a clear understanding of the complete FTTH network architecture, from the core network connection at the OLT to the Optical Network Terminal (ONT) at the subscriber's end. The course also covers the physical aspects of an OLT, including its chassis, PON ports, and uplink connectivity, providing a practical overview of how this critical equipment is installed and configured in a service provider's environment to enable reliable FTTH services.

title: FTTH ONT CONFIGURATION
desc: This technical course offers a comprehensive walkthrough of the configuration process for an FTTH Optical Network Terminal (ONT) modem. It is designed for field technicians and network support staff responsible for installing and maintaining customer premises equipment. The course begins with a physical overview of a typical ONT device, explaining its various ports, buttons, and LED status indicators. It then proceeds to the software configuration, starting with setting up the correct IP address on a connected computer to gain access to the modem's management page. Learners will be guided through the web-based interface to configure critical internet settings, including selecting the PPPoE route mode, enabling Network Address Translation (NAT), and inputting VLAN ID details provided by the service provider. The curriculum also covers setting up the local and wireless LAN, including DHCP settings, SSID naming, and Wi-Fi security. Additionally, the course touches upon important security features like firewalls, MAC filtering, and port forwarding for applications such as CCTV. Upon completion, learners will be proficient in deploying and troubleshooting FTTH ONT modems in a live environment.

title: FTTH Technology
desc: This course offers a detailed examination of Fiber to the Home (FTTH) technology, designed for professionals in the telecommunications sector. The curriculum begins by establishing the context for FTTH as a solution for the growing demand for high-bandwidth services, contrasting it with other FTTx architectures. Learners will gain an in-depth understanding of the key components and their functions within a Passive Optical Network (PON), including the central role of the Optical Line Terminal (OLT) at the service provider's end and the Optical Network Terminal (ONT) at the customer's premises. The course explains the structure of the Optical Distribution Network (ODN), detailing the use of passive splitters and fiber optic cables. Furthermore, it explores practical implementation strategies, such as BSNL's revenue-sharing partner models, and typical FTTH service plans. A significant portion is dedicated to the critical aspects of network management, focusing on Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like jitter and fault rates, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as download speeds and latency, which are essential for maintaining service excellence and customer satisfaction. Upon completion, participants will be equipped with the foundational knowledge to understand, plan, and evaluate FTTH networks.

title: Full Depth Reclamation for Rehabilitation of Low Volume Roads
desc: This course delves into the principles and practices of Full Depth Reclamation (FDR) for the effective rehabilitation of low-volume and rural roads. FDR is presented as a smart, eco-friendly alternative to conventional methods, addressing severe pavement distress by recycling existing materials on-site. The curriculum covers the entire FDR process, from initial site assessment and material pulverization to the selection and application of stabilizing agents like Portland cement. Participants will learn about the critical construction steps, including mixing, grading, compaction, and curing, which are essential for creating a durable and long-lasting stabilized base. The course also explores the adaptability of FDR to various soil types and traffic conditions, emphasizing its role in reducing the need for virgin aggregates, minimizing environmental impact, and lowering the overall life-cycle cost of road maintenance. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to assess the suitability of FDR for specific projects and understand its contribution to building resilient and sustainable road infrastructure.

title: Functions and Office Procedures of an Assistant Section Officer
desc: The Assistant Section Officer (ASO) plays a vital role in the administrative machinery of the Government of India’s Central Secretariat and serves as an important link in the process of policy formulation and implementation. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the role, responsibilities, and professional standards expected of an ASO in the Central Secretariat. The course covers the position and hierarchy of an ASO within the Secretariat system, key functions and responsibilities, and the duties of a Dealing Officer as prescribed under the Manual of Office Procedure (MOP). Participants will develop an understanding of essential secretariat practices, including file management, noting, drafting, processing of cases, handling correspondence, and maintenance of official records. The course also emphasizes the professional conduct and ethical standards expected of an ASO, including diligence, integrity, impartiality, confidentiality, and accountability.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Functions and Operations of Foreign Post Office
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the operational framework of India's Foreign Post Offices (FPOs). It is designed for postal employees to build a foundational understanding of the systems that govern international mail. The curriculum begins by defining the ecosystem of international mail handling, differentiating between key entities such as the Office of Exchange (OE), Office of Exchange of Transit (OET), and FPOs. Learners will be guided through the entire lifecycle of international mail, covering the step-by-step procedures for outbound (export) and inbound (import) mail flows. This includes mail segregation, bagging, customs inspection, clearance, and dispatch. The course also sheds light on the critical role of the Customs Department in assessing and clearing articles, and explains the procedures for handling detained items. Furthermore, it provides a practical introduction to the International Postal System (IPS) software, demonstrating how it is used to scan, track, and manage mail items and dispatches, ensuring accountability and efficiency in the global postal network. Upon completion, participants will be equipped with the necessary knowledge to navigate the complexities of foreign mail operations.

title: Functions of Nodal Postal Account Office in India Post Payments Bank
desc: This course provides an in-depth examination of the fund management architecture supporting the India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), focusing on the specific functions of Postal Accounts Offices (PAOs) and Nodal Offices. In the context of expanding digital financial services in India, understanding these backend operations is crucial for ensuring transparency, accountability, and efficiency. The curriculum is designed to equip finance and accounts personnel with a thorough understanding of the entire transaction lifecycle. Key learning areas include the detailed responsibilities of PAOs and Nodal Offices, the mechanics of transaction flows, and the procedures for reconciliation and financial reversals. The course delves into specialized topics such as IPPB-specific accounting standards, the settlement processes for NEFT and RTGS transactions, and the operational logic of sweep-in and sweep-out mechanisms. Furthermore, it addresses the important aspect of GST accounting within this ecosystem. Upon completion, participants will be able to confidently manage and oversee these critical financial processes, ensuring regulatory compliance and contributing to the robust financial health of India's postal banking network.

title: Fund Management in DOP
desc: This course is designed to equip Group 'B' and 'C' officials of the Department of Posts with the necessary skills for robust fund and budget management. It provides a detailed walkthrough of the procedures governing financial transactions with banks, emphasizing the importance of accurate accounting and reconciliation. Participants will gain hands-on knowledge of the SAP CSI environment, learning to execute T-codes for bank reconciliation (ZFS67, FEBAN) and budget allocation (ZFM_UPLOAD, ZFM_POST). The course thoroughly explains the lifecycle of budget preparation, from creating Revised Estimates (RE) and Budget Estimates (BE) to compiling the Anticipated Final Grant (AFG). It also covers the generation of monthly and quarterly expenditure statements to monitor fiscal health. Upon completion, learners will be able to manage departmental funds efficiently, ensure compliance with financial rules, and utilize SAP tools for transparent and accurate financial operations, contributing to the overall financial discipline of the department.

title: Fundamental Applications of Material Science and Engineering
desc: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles of material science and their practical applications in civil and industrial contexts. It is structured to be accessible for officials and professionals without a technical background, bridging the gap between scientific concepts and their relevance in governance. The curriculum begins by classifying key engineering materials, including metals, ceramics, and polymers, and delves into their crystalline and amorphous structures. Learners will explore how imperfections and phase transformations, guided by phase diagrams and processes like heat treatment, define a material's ultimate properties. Key learning areas include the analysis of mechanical, electrical, optical, and magnetic properties, alongside practical topics such as material degradation, corrosion, and failure analysis. The course also touches upon advanced materials and non-destructive testing methods. Upon completion, participants will have the necessary knowledge to contribute to technical discussions and make strategic decisions involving material selection for public infrastructure and industrial projects, ensuring durability, efficiency, and safety.
org: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani (BITS Pilani)

title: Fundamental Knowledge of Financial Statements
desc: This introductory course is designed to equip public sector professionals with the fundamental knowledge of corporate financial statements. In today's interconnected economy, understanding the financial health of corporate entities, including Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), is crucial for effective governance, regulation, and oversight. The course begins by defining financial statements and explaining their essential role in corporate transparency and accountability. You will learn about the primary components, such as the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement, and the basic principles that guide their preparation. Furthermore, the course delves into identifying the key stakeholders—from investors and regulators to management and employees—and understanding their respective interests in these financial reports. Upon completion, learners will be better equipped to interpret financial data, contribute to informed decision-making, and exercise more effective oversight in roles related to finance, audit, and corporate affairs.

title: Fundamental of Physical Education Part - 1 : Beginner
desc: This foundational course, 'Fundamentals of Physical Education: Part 1,' is designed to provide a thorough understanding of the core principles that underpin physical education and holistic well-being. The curriculum begins by defining and differentiating key concepts such as physical activity, exercise, physical education, and movement education. It delves into the primary objectives of physical education, exploring its physical, cognitive, social, and affective domains to highlight its role in the complete development of an individual. Learners will examine the meaning and essential components of physical literacy, recognizing its importance for fostering a lifelong engagement in physical activity. The course also breaks down the concepts of physical fitness and wellness, distinguishing between health-related and skill-related components. Furthermore, it introduces the Movement Education Framework, a systematic approach to understanding how the body moves through space and effort. Upon completion, participants will have a robust conceptual toolkit to effectively teach, coach, and promote physical activity.

title: Fundamental of Physical Education Part - 2: Beginner
desc: This comprehensive beginner's course delves into the essential principles of physical education, designed for aspiring coaches, physical education teachers, and fitness enthusiasts. The program begins by establishing the context of human growth and development, detailing the characteristics of each stage from infancy to adulthood and the genetic and environmental factors that affect them. You will learn to distinguish between various components of physical fitness, such as cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, flexibility, speed, and agility. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to the practical application of knowledge, teaching you how to conduct and interpret results from standard fitness assessments like the beep test, vertical jump test, and skinfold measurements. Furthermore, the course addresses body composition, common postural deformities like scoliosis and kyphosis, and the physiological importance of proper warm-up and cool-down procedures. By completing this course, you will gain the knowledge to better understand and support the physical development and well-being of students and athletes.

title: Fundamental of Physical Education Part 1 : Intermediate
desc: This foundational course is designed to equip educators with the knowledge and skills to effectively deliver physical education in a school setting. It begins by defining the multifaceted role of a PE teacher, highlighting their responsibilities as a coach, academician, health educator, and planner. The curriculum then delves deep into the concept of physical literacy, breaking it down into its four key elements: motivation and confidence (affective), physical competence (physical), knowledge and understanding (cognitive), and lifelong engagement (behavioral). Participants will learn to identify the different stages of physical literacy development, from the 'Active Start' stage in early years to the 'Learn to Train' stage for older children. A significant focus is placed on practical application, with modules dedicated to integrating fitness into daily school activities, selecting age-appropriate exercises for students from foundation years to class 12, and structuring an effective play session. By the end of this course, learners will be prepared to create an inclusive, engaging, and developmentally appropriate physical education program that promotes a healthy and active lifestyle among students.

title: Fundamental of Physical Education Part 2 - Intermediate
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the principles and practices of physical education. It is designed for educators and coaches seeking to build robust and effective sports programs in schools.
