Key learning areas include a thorough breakdown of the NAVTEX message format, including transmitter identification, subject indicators, and message numbering. Participants will delve into the technical architecture of a NAVTEX transmitting station, exploring the functions of internal modules like the Power Amplifier (PA), filters, power detectors, and antenna systems. The course also covers network-level concepts such as time slot allocation and the role of the NAVTEX Control Centre (NCC). Upon completion, learners will be able to describe the complete operational workflow of the NAVTEX system, from message creation to transmission and reception, ensuring they can support the reliable delivery of maritime safety information.
org: Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships

title: NCP 2025 and the Future of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies
desc: This course examines the implications of the National Cooperation Policy (NCP) 2025 for Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS). The policy redefines PACS as frontline rural institutions that extend beyond traditional credit functions to operate as multipurpose cooperative enterprises delivering financial, commercial, and citizen-centric services. The course contextualizes this transformation within the broader vision of Sahkar se Samriddhi and the national objective of strengthening inclusive, participatory, and democratic economic development. It introduces the strategic pillars of NCP 2025 and explores how governance reforms, cooperation among cooperatives, institutional convergence, and scheme alignment are designed to enhance the economic scope and sustainability of PACS.

title: Need for Post Quantum Cryptography in Public Key Infrastructure
desc: The rapid advancement of quantum computing poses a significant threat to the security of classical Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), which relies on cryptographic algorithms such as RSA, Diffie–Hellman, and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) to enable secure digital communication. Quantum computers, using Shor’s algorithm, can efficiently factor large integers and solve discrete logarithm problems, thereby undermining the security foundations of these widely deployed cryptosystems. Given that PKI underpins critical sectors including e-governance, banking, healthcare, Internet of Things (IoT), and national security, the transition to quantum-safe encryption has become imperative. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) offers quantum-resistant algorithms designed to secure PKI against both classical and quantum adversaries.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881
desc: The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, is a critical piece of legislation that underpins the reliability of financial transactions in India. This course offers an in-depth examination of the Act, providing learners with the knowledge to navigate its complexities. It begins by defining negotiable instruments, including promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques, and explains their legal significance in facilitating trade and commerce. Participants will delve into the core provisions of the Act, covering topics such as the legal presumptions favoring holders, the processes of endorsement and negotiation, and the distinct rights and liabilities of each party. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to the practical and legal consequences of dishonored instruments, with a detailed focus on the procedures for handling cheque dishonor, including the relevant penal provisions. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to apply the Act's principles in banking, commercial litigation, and everyday business dealings, ensuring compliance and mitigating financial risks. This course is vital for legal practitioners, finance officers, and anyone involved in commercial transactions.
org: National Academy of Direct Taxes NADT

title: Negotiation
desc: This course delves into the fundamental principles and strategic applications of negotiation. It is designed for public sector professionals seeking to enhance their ability to manage conflicts, lead teams, and secure favorable agreements. The course begins by defining negotiation and its necessity in situations of conflict, distinguishing it from simple persuasion. It then explores the critical differences between positional bargaining, which focuses on dividing a fixed pie, and interest-based negotiation, which aims to expand the pie for a win-win result. Participants will learn how to prepare effectively for any negotiation by analyzing their Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement (BATNA), setting realistic goals, and understanding the other party's perspective. The curriculum also introduces analytical tools like decision trees to evaluate complex choices and manage risks. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped with a strategic framework to approach negotiations with confidence, transform disputes into collaborative opportunities, and achieve durable, value-creating agreements.

title: Negotiation
desc: Master the art and science of negotiation with this in-depth course designed for professionals seeking to enhance their strategic influence and conflict resolution skills. The program begins by establishing the fundamentals of distributive negotiations, teaching you how to claim value in single-issue scenarios using tactics like anchoring and strategic concessions. It then progresses to the more complex world of integrative negotiations, where you will learn to expand the pie by discovering shared interests and creating mutual value. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to dispute resolution, introducing the powerful Interests, Rights, and Power (IRP) framework to navigate disagreements, manage emotions, and move from conflict to resolution. The final module addresses the dynamics of multi-party negotiations, providing strategies for building and managing coalitions, understanding power dynamics, and achieving consensus in complex environments like inter-departmental projects or international forums. Upon completion, you will be equipped to prepare for, engage in, and lead negotiations with confidence and strategic foresight.

title: Negotiation and Conflict Resolution Skills for Law Enforcement
desc: In today's complex society, law enforcement officers require skills that extend beyond traditional enforcement. This course on Negotiation Skills is designed to meet that need, equipping police personnel to handle arguments, de-escalate tense situations, and collaborate with diverse communities. The program provides a structured approach to transforming officers into effective mediators and communicators. Key learning areas include the fundamentals of negotiation, the critical role of verbal and non-verbal communication, and the importance of cultural competence. Participants will explore practical guidelines for first responders in crisis scenarios such as hostage situations, emphasizing active listening and emotional intelligence. The course also delves into proven conflict resolution models and de-escalation techniques tailored for law enforcement contexts.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: Negotiation Skills: Managing Emotions and Biases for Win-Win Outcomes
desc: Negotiation is an integral part of everyday life and is not limited to multinational corporations or state leaders. We negotiate regularly with colleagues, supervisors, and stakeholders within and across departments on a wide range of issues. While some negotiations are formal, others are informal and occur as part of our routine interactions. Effective negotiation is often associated with strong communication skills. However, successful negotiation also depends on several underlying factors, particularly emotions, perceptions, and cognitive biases, which can significantly influence our decisions and behaviourThis course explores the role of emotions and biases in negotiation and provides learners with practical insights into managing them effectively. It aims to help participants understand how emotions influence decision-making, develop strategies for managing emotional responses, and strengthen their negotiation skills to achieve mutually beneficial, win-win outcomes.

title: Network and Telecom Security - Basics of Cryptography
desc: In an era of digital transformation, securing data transmission and storage is paramount. This course, 'Fundamentals of Cryptography for Network and Telecom Security,' offers a comprehensive introduction to the principles and practices of modern cryptography. It is designed for professionals who need to understand how data is protected in transit and at rest. The course begins by defining fundamental terms and concepts, establishing a solid base for more complex topics. Key learning areas include a detailed comparison of symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, with discussions on widely-used algorithms like DES, AES, and RSA. You will also explore the mechanics of hashing for data integrity and the Diffie-Hellman key exchange method. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), explaining how Certificate Authorities, Registration Authorities, and digital certificates (X.509) work together to create a framework of trust. Upon completion, learners will be able to recognize various cryptographic methods and understand their application in securing organizational data and daily internet communications.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network and Telecom Security - Cyber Security Ecosystem
desc: In an increasingly interconnected world, understanding the architecture of cyber security is paramount for national security and effective governance. This course delves into the comprehensive cyber security ecosystem established in India. It begins by defining cyberspace and its inherent challenges, then proceeds to detail the policies, guidelines, and procedures designed to protect critical systems from cyber threats. Key learning areas include an exploration of India's legal frameworks, such as the IT Act, 2000, and the National Cyber Security Policy, 2013. The curriculum provides a detailed breakdown of the roles and responsibilities of key government bodies, including the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), along with their specialized agencies like CERT-In and NCCC. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify the principal components of the national security apparatus and understand how they work in concert to safeguard India's digital domain.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network and Telecom Security - Physical and Host Security
desc: In an increasingly connected world, securing an organization's information and infrastructure is paramount, especially within the public sector where officials handle critical and sensitive data. This course, "Securing Network Infrastructure: Physical and Host Security Measures," offers a foundational understanding of the two core pillars of infrastructure protection. It addresses the critical need to safeguard both the physical environment and the individual computer systems (hosts) that form the backbone of any network. The curriculum is structured into two main modules. The first module delves into physical security, covering the essential controls and measures needed to protect buildings, data centers, and telecom equipment. Learners will examine topics such as perimeter security, surveillance systems like CCTV, biometric access controls, and environmental protections like fire suppression. The second module shifts focus to host security, a vital component in any office environment. It details the relevance of securing host devices, managing threats from malware and unauthorized access, and implementing best practices for operating system security, patch management, and user account control. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to discuss and apply fundamental security controls, assess risks to physical and digital assets, and contribute to a more resilient and secure organizational environment. This knowledge is essential for any officer responsible for IT assets or sensitive information.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network and Telecom Security - Virtualization Concepts
desc: In today's office environments, the need to run multiple operating systems and isolate sensitive applications for security is paramount. This course, 'An Introduction to Virtualization Concepts for Network and Telecom Security,' addresses this need by providing a foundational understanding of virtualization technologies. You will learn what virtualization is, how it abstracts software from hardware, and its significant benefits, including enhanced security, operational flexibility, and cost savings. The curriculum delves into essential components such as virtual machines (VMs), hypervisors (Type 1 and Type 2), and containers, explaining their characteristics and use cases. Furthermore, the course introduces containerization technologies like Docker and draws clear distinctions between virtualization and cloud computing. Upon completion, you will be equipped to understand how these technologies can be deployed to build more resilient, secure, and efficient IT infrastructures within a government or corporate setting.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network Firewall Defense Systems
desc: In today's interconnected digital world, securing network infrastructure is paramount for any organization. This course, 'Introduction to Network Firewall Defense Systems,' offers a foundational understanding of how firewalls act as the first line of defense against unauthorized access and malicious traffic. Participants will delve into the core concepts of firewall technology, learning to differentiate between network-based and host-based firewalls, as well as hardware and software solutions. The curriculum explores various firewall technologies, including packet filtering, stateful packet inspection, and application gateways. Additionally, the course covers crucial concepts like Network Address Translation (NAT) and the advanced capabilities of Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW). Upon completion, learners will be able to recognize different firewall types, understand the principles of firewall policy implementation, and apply security best practices to safeguard their organization's digital assets.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network Function Virtualisation in 5G
desc: This course delves into the architectural framework of Network Function Virtualization (NFV) as a foundational technology for 5G. It begins by contrasting traditional purpose-built hardware networks with the agile, software-based approach of NFV. Participants will gain a detailed understanding of the key components, including the NFV Infrastructure (NFVI), Virtualized Network Functions (VNFs), and the crucial role of Management and Orchestration (MANO). The course further explores the practical implementation of VNFs using both Virtual Machines (VMs) and containers, explaining their respective advantages and how they contribute to a cloud-native environment. A significant portion is dedicated to the synergy between NFV and Software-Defined Networking (SDN), illustrating how SDN provides the necessary network agility and automation. Upon completion, learners will be able to articulate the strategic benefits of NFV, such as operational efficiency, scalability, and the ability to deploy multi-vendor solutions, which are essential for the evolution of telecommunications.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network Monitoring and Key Management System in Kavach
desc: This self-paced, interactive course provides a comprehensive understanding of the Network Monitoring System (NMS) and Key Management System (KMS) within the Kavach Automatic Train Protection framework. Learners will explore how NMS monitors, manages, and analyzes Kavach network performance and events in real time, ensuring smooth and safe train operations. The course also covers KMS functionalities, including encryption, authentication, and session key management, which guarantee secure radio communication between Kavach components. Participants will gain insight into system connectivity, data integrity, and cybersecurity principles, enhancing their technical competency in monitoring and securing Kavach systems across Indian Railways.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications (IRISET)

title: Network Security
desc: In an era of increasing digital connectivity, securing government networks is paramount. This course delves into the core principles of network security, offering a detailed examination of the modern threat landscape. It begins by establishing the context of why network security is crucial, highlighting the vulnerabilities in both personal and official digital ecosystems. The curriculum covers a wide range of common threats, from social engineering tactics like phishing to sophisticated attacks such as ransomware and Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs). Participants will learn through practical examples and demonstrations, including how antivirus software can be bypassed and how user data can be compromised through seemingly harmless actions. The course emphasizes the end-user's critical role in the security chain and provides actionable best practices. Learners will be equipped to implement stronger security postures by understanding concepts like Zero Trust Architecture, effective password management, and the importance of creating personal and organizational security policies. The ultimate goal is to empower officials to protect sensitive government data and infrastructure from ever-evolving cyber threats.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Network Security Basics-Introduction to Networking and Security Threat
desc: In an era where digital infrastructure is critical to public service delivery, understanding the fundamentals of network security is paramount. This course is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to both computer networking and the prevalent security threats that government and public sector organizations face. It establishes a strong foundation by explaining the core principles of how networks operate, covering essential topics such as computer network types (LAN, WAN, PAN), network topologies, and the layered architectures of the OSI and TCP/IP models. Participants will also learn about key networking components and directory services like Active Directory. The second part of the course shifts focus to cybersecurity, offering a detailed overview of the threat landscape. It differentiates between threats and vulnerabilities and classifies various network security threats and attack vectors. Learners will study common attack methods, including unauthorized access, malware, phishing, SQL injection, and Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Upon completion, participants will be equipped with the essential vocabulary and conceptual understanding to identify potential security risks, engage in informed discussions about network protection, and contribute to maintaining the integrity and security of digital assets and information systems within their organizations.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Network Security Policy - Simplified
desc: In an era of increasing digital threats, a robust network security policy is fundamental to protecting an organization's critical information assets. This course offers a detailed walkthrough of the principles and practices required to build and enforce such a policy, tailored for government and public sector environments. You will begin by understanding the strategic importance of a policy vision and setting clear security goals. The course then details the key personnel and teams involved, such as the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Security Operations Center (SOC), and Incident Response teams. A significant portion of the curriculum is dedicated to exploring technical and administrative controls. You will learn about perimeter defense mechanisms like firewalls, IDS/IPS, and Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA). The course also covers network segmentation using VLANs, traffic inspection with SIEM tools, access control management, and formulating policies for BYOD and third-party connectivity. By the end of this course, you will be able to design, implement, and manage a comprehensive network security policy that aligns with organizational needs and protects against evolving cyber threats.
org: National Telecommunications Institute for Policy Research, Innovation and Training (NTIPRIT)

title: Networking Fundamentals - IP Addressing
desc: In today's digital-first governance landscape, a robust and well-managed network is critical for service delivery. This course delves into the core concepts of IP addressing that form the backbone of modern communication systems. You will begin by understanding the architecture of IPv4 addresses and how they are allocated. The course then progresses to practical, hands-on concepts such as subnetting, which is crucial for efficient network segmentation and management. Key learning areas include the distinction between network and broadcast addresses, the use of private address pools, and the application of Variable Length Subnet Masking (VLSM) and supernetting for network optimization. Furthermore, you will learn about the function of Network Address Translation (NAT) in enabling private networks to securely access the internet. Upon completion, you will possess the necessary skills to design, configure, and manage IP addressing schemes in various networking environments.
org: Ministry of Communications- Department of Telecommunications

title: Networking Fundamentals - Routing Principles
desc: Dive deep into the mechanics of network communication with this foundational course on routing principles. This program is designed to provide a clear and thorough understanding of how data travels across complex networks. You will begin by learning the concept and importance of routing, before moving on to compare different routing strategies, including manual versus automatic and static versus dynamic. The curriculum covers the inner workings of dynamic routing protocols, explaining how they build and maintain routing tables. Key learning areas include a detailed analysis of distance-vector and link-state protocols, the process of router table lookups for efficient data transmission, and the crucial differences between Interior Gateway Protocols (IGPs) and Exterior Gateway Protocols (EGPs). Upon completion, you will be equipped with the technical knowledge to understand and analyze the routing decisions that underpin reliable and efficient network infrastructure, a vital skill in today's digitally connected public sector.
org: Ministry of Communications- Department of Telecommunications

title: Neutral Sections in Indian Railways Electric Traction
desc: This course provides an in-depth understanding of Neutral Sections in the context of the Indian Railways 1x25 kV / 2x25 kV Electric Traction Overhead Equipment (OHE) system. It explains the purpose of Neutral Sections, describes the various types used across the Indian Railways OHE network, and discusses their operational significance. The course also covers the detailed maintenance schedules and best practices for ensuring the reliable functioning of Neutral Sections.
org: Indian Railways Institute of Electrical Engineering (IRIEEN)

title: New Age Learning Centre: Transforming lives of students of Changlang
desc: NALC is a free service that transforms underutilized government school libraries into modern, flexible learning spaces, offering resources like 24/7 Wi-Fi, tablets, and e-readers to improve personal development for people of all ages.

title: New Austrian Tunnelling Method for Highway Tunnel Construction
desc: Tunnel construction is among the most technically demanding activities in highway infrastructure, requiring strict engineering and quality practices to ensure structural stability, safety and durability. This course introduces the New Austrian Tunnelling Method (NATM) and its eight-stage construction sequence for highway tunnels in India. Learners explore excavation, drilling and blasting, defuming, muck removal, scaling, geological face mapping, and primary support systems including shotcrete, rock bolts, lattice girders, wire mesh and pipe roof umbrellas. The course also covers drainage, waterproofing, reinforcement, formwork and final concrete lining, along with key quality checks, acceptance criteria and safety practices. By completing the course, learners will be able to understand construction sequencing, assess quality compliance, respond to geological conditions, supervise activities effectively and contribute to the safe, durable and quality construction of highway tunnels.

title: New Criminal Laws Sexual Offences and Assault and Criminal Force
desc: This course provides a detailed examination of the significant reforms in India's criminal laws concerning offences against women, as introduced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. In the context of modernizing the justice system, the BNS replaces the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860, with a framework designed for greater clarity and victim protection. The course is structured to provide a comparative analysis, helping learners grasp the evolution of legal definitions and procedures. Key learning areas include an in-depth study of updated provisions for rape, gang rape, sexual harassment, voyeurism, and stalking. It specifically addresses new concepts such as sexual intercourse by deceitful means or by a person in authority, and assault with intent to disrobe. Furthermore, the course highlights crucial procedural safeguards, such as the protection of a victim's identity and restrictions on publishing court proceedings. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to interpret and apply these critical legal changes, ensuring a more sensitive and effective response to crimes against women within the Indian legal system. This knowledge is vital for police officers, judicial officers, legal practitioners, and public officials involved in the criminal justice process.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Arrest and the Rights of the Arrestee
desc: This course, 'New Criminal Laws: Arrest and the Rights of the Arrestee,' delves into the critical changes introduced by the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. The transition from the erstwhile Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, necessitates a clear understanding of the new legal landscape for all law enforcement personnel. The course systematically covers the key learning areas essential for compliant and effective policing. Participants will explore the specific provisions that permit an arrest without a warrant, the procedural duties and requirements mandated for police officers during an arrest, and special conditions applicable to Armed Forces personnel. Furthermore, it emphasizes the constitutional and statutory rights afforded to every arrested person, including rules on handcuffing, personal searches, medical examinations, and maximum detention periods. By completing this course, learners will be equipped to apply the new laws correctly, upholding both justice and individual rights in their daily duties.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Compelling Appearance through Summons
desc: With the introduction of new criminal laws, understanding the updated procedural framework is essential for legal and law enforcement professionals. This course delves into the critical process of issuing and serving summons under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. It provides a comprehensive overview of the legal requirements, from the initial drafting of a summons to the final proof of service. Key learning areas include the specific methods for serving summons on different parties such as individuals, corporate bodies, and public servants, including procedures for when a person cannot be located. The course also addresses the protocols for substituted service and serving summons outside local jurisdictions. Upon completion, learners will be proficient in applying these rules, ensuring that the issuance and execution of summons are conducted with legal precision, thereby upholding the integrity and efficiency of the justice system.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Conditions for Initiating Criminal Proceedings
desc: This course offers an in-depth analysis of the new legal framework governing the initiation of criminal proceedings in India. It focuses on Chapter XV (Sections 210-222) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, which replaces the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure. The content is designed for legal and law enforcement professionals to understand the critical changes and procedural nuances introduced by the new legislation. Key learning areas include the process of taking cognizance of offences by Magistrates, the powers of Sessions Courts, and the mechanisms for transferring cases to ensure fair and efficient trials. Furthermore, the course delves into significant provisions such as witness protection protocols against threats, and the specific conditions required for prosecuting public servants, judges, and for offences against the State, marriage, and defamation. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to navigate the initial stages of the criminal justice process with a clear understanding of the BNSS, 2023, enhancing their professional effectiveness and ensuring procedural compliance.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: e FIRs Zero FIRs Enquiry and Investigation
desc: With the enactment of the new criminal laws, it is crucial for law enforcement professionals to understand the updated procedural framework. This course delves into the critical changes introduced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, replacing the erstwhile Criminal Procedure Code. The curriculum is designed to provide a detailed examination of Sections 173 to 178, which govern the registration of information, preliminary enquiries, and the entire investigation process. Key learning areas include the modernized procedures for e-FIR and Zero FIR, the distinct handling of cognizable and non-cognizable cases, and the specific powers granted to police officers and magistrates. By completing this course, learners, particularly those in policing roles, will be equipped to apply these new legal provisions correctly and efficiently in their day-to-day duties, ensuring procedural integrity and effective law enforcement.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: General Search Provisions and Procedures
desc: This course offers an in-depth examination of the general search provisions and procedures as outlined in the new Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. It is specifically designed for law enforcement professionals to understand and correctly apply the updated legal framework during criminal investigations. The content delves into the nuances of Sections 102 to 110 of the BNSS, which govern the entire lifecycle of search and seizure operations, from the issuance of warrants to the final disposal of property.The curriculum addresses the critical importance of procedural compliance in modern policing. Key learning areas include the legal requirements for obtaining a search warrant, the specific duties of an officer in charge of a search, and the protocols for managing items found in a search that falls beyond the initial jurisdiction. A significant focus is placed on the new mandate for audio-video recording of procedures to enhance transparency and accountability. Furthermore, the course details the legal mechanisms for the attachment, forfeiture, or restoration of property, and the power of a Magistrate to direct searches. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to conduct search and seizure operations with a clear understanding of their legal authority and responsibilities, ensuring that evidence is collected in a manner that is fair, transparent, and legally sound.

title: New Criminal Laws: Initiating Complaints Before the Magistrate
desc: With the introduction of new criminal laws in India, it is crucial for legal and judicial officers to understand the updated procedures. This course provides a comprehensive guide to Chapter XVI of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, focusing on the critical initial stage of the criminal justice process: complaints to Magistrates. Learners will delve into the specific provisions of Sections 223 through 226, exploring the nuances of examining a complainant and their witnesses, and the special procedures required when a complaint is filed against a public servant. Furthermore, the course clarifies the legal grounds upon which a Magistrate can postpone the issuance of a process or dismiss a complaint outright. By mastering these procedures, participants will be better prepared to apply the law correctly, ensuring procedural fairness and enhancing the efficiency and integrity of the justice system.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal laws: Jurisdiction in Criminal Cases in Inquiry and Trial
desc: This course offers an in-depth examination of India's new criminal law framework, specifically focusing on the critical aspects of jurisdiction in criminal inquiries and trials under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. The content is designed to provide a clear and functional understanding of the legal principles that determine which court has the authority to hear a case. Key learning areas include a detailed breakdown of territorial jurisdiction, rules for establishing the place of trial when an act and its consequences occur in different locations, and procedures for offenses linked to other crimes. The course also explores special jurisdictional provisions for offenses committed during travel, through digital or electronic means, and those with extraterritorial dimensions. Learners will understand the specific powers of various courts, including the High Court, to resolve jurisdictional ambiguities and issue legal processes like summons or warrants beyond their immediate local limits. Upon completion, participants will be equipped with the necessary knowledge to correctly apply these new legal standards in practice, ensuring procedural compliance and effective administration of justice.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Murder Culpable Homicide and Mob Lynching
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of significant changes in India's criminal jurisprudence with the introduction of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. It is specifically designed to address the critical provisions related to offences affecting the human body, as detailed in Sections 100 to 110. The curriculum offers a foundational understanding of why these legal reforms are important for modernizing the justice system and ensuring clarity in prosecution. Key learning areas include the precise legal definitions of culpable homicide and murder, the exceptions that differentiate them, and the prescribed punishments for each. The course also explores newly defined offences and modifications to existing ones, such as causing death by negligence, particularly in 'hit and run' cases, and the abetment of suicide. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze complex legal scenarios, correctly apply the new provisions, and articulate the key differences between the BNS and the erstwhile Indian Penal Code, enhancing their professional effectiveness in the legal and law enforcement domains.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Offences Relating to Marriage and Miscarriage
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the new legal landscape for offences related to marriage and miscarriage as defined in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. In the context of significant legal reforms in India, it is crucial for law enforcement and judicial officers to be well-versed in these changes to ensure justice and protect vulnerable individuals. The curriculum delves into specific sections of the BNS, covering serious crimes such as dowry death (Section 80), cruelty by a husband or relatives (Section 86), and bigamy (Section 82). It also addresses offences involving the coercion of women and acts causing miscarriage, both with and without consent. Upon completion, learners will be able to confidently interpret and apply these new laws, understand the key distinctions from previous legislation, and follow the correct investigative procedures, particularly in sensitive cases like the suspicious death of a woman within seven years of marriage. This knowledge is essential for upholding the rule of law and safeguarding women's rights within the Indian legal system.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Organised Crime and Terrorist Act
desc: This course offers a comprehensive analysis of the significant changes introduced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) concerning national security offences. It specifically addresses the legal architecture of organised crime and terrorism under Sections 111 to 113. The curriculum is designed to provide law enforcement and legal professionals with a clear understanding of why these new provisions were introduced and how they function. Key learning areas include a detailed breakdown of the definitions of organised crime, petty organised crime, and terrorist acts, highlighting the legal thresholds and elements required for prosecution. A crucial component of the course is a comparative analysis of these new sections with previous statutes like the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), 1999, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). This comparison helps learners grasp the evolution of India's legal approach to combating organised crime and terrorism. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to accurately interpret and apply these new laws in their professional roles, enhancing their effectiveness in maintaining law and order.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Police Inquest and Magistrate Inquiry into Death
desc: With the enactment of India's new criminal laws, it is crucial for officials to master the updated procedural requirements. This course offers a detailed examination of police inquests and magistrate inquiries into the cause of death under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. The content is specifically built around Sections 194, 195, and 196, providing a clear roadmap for investigations into suicides, suspicious deaths, and other unnatural circumstances. Learners will explore the step-by-step process of a police inquest, from initial reporting to the submission of the final report. The course also thoroughly explains the enhanced authority and responsibilities of Magistrates in conducting independent inquiries, including their power to summon individuals and order exhumations. A significant focus is placed on the special provisions and safeguards for investigating custodial deaths and the unnatural death of women shortly after marriage. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to apply these new legal standards correctly, ensuring procedural compliance and upholding justice.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Search and Final Report and Custody Procedures
desc: With the introduction of India's new criminal laws, it is imperative for law enforcement personnel to understand the revised procedural mandates. The curriculum is designed to equip police officers with the necessary knowledge to conduct searches, manage custody, and handle evidence in a manner that is both legally sound and procedurally correct. Participants will explore the nuances of preparing and submitting investigation reports, including the requirements for releasing an accused individual when evidence is deficient versus proceeding when evidence is sufficient. By mastering these provisions, officers can ensure their actions are transparent, fair, and adhere to the time-bound requirements of the new legal system, thereby strengthening the rule of law and public trust in the police force.

title: New Criminal Laws: Statement Recording and Victim Examination
desc: With the introduction of India's new criminal laws, it is imperative for law enforcement professionals to master the updated procedures. This course provides a comprehensive overview of the investigation process under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. It delves into the specific powers and duties of investigating officers when summoning witnesses (Section 179), examining them (Section 180), and recording their statements (Section 181). The course also highlights the strict prohibitions against inducement (Section 182) and the formal process for recording confessions (Section 183). A dedicated module covers the sensitive and critical procedures for the medical examination of rape victims (Section 184), emphasizing the use of audio-video electronic means and the rights of the victim. Upon completion, learners will be proficient in applying these new legal standards, ensuring that investigations are conducted with greater transparency, accountability, and respect for legal and human rights, thereby strengthening the criminal justice system.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Summons to Produce Things and Search Warrants
desc: This course delves into the critical procedures governing the production of documents and the execution of search warrants under India's new criminal laws. Participants will gain a detailed understanding of Chapter VII of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, which is fundamental for lawful evidence collection and investigation. The curriculum systematically covers the conditions for issuing a summons to produce things, the specific protocols for obtaining a search warrant, and the general provisions that ensure all searches are conducted fairly and transparently. Key learning areas include the handling of postal articles for legal proceedings, procedures for dealing with stolen property and forged documents, and the legal mechanisms for forfeiting prohibited publications. Furthermore, the course highlights the vital human rights safeguards embedded in the law, such as the provisions for rescuing wrongfully confined individuals and restoring abducted females. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to apply these legal standards correctly in their professional duties, upholding both the rule of law and citizen rights.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Technology in Policing and Digital Evidence
desc: This course delves into the critical updates introduced by India's new criminal laws, specifically addressing the integration of technology in law enforcement and judicial processes. The curriculum is designed to provide a thorough understanding of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023. The context for this training is the nationwide modernization of the criminal justice system, requiring officials to adapt to new digital standards. Key learning areas include the mandatory use of audio-video electronic means for recording search and seizure, the legal framework for the admissibility of electronic evidence, and the specific conditions for submitting such evidence in court. Participants will learn the detailed procedures for issuing certificates for electronic records, managing the chain of custody for digital evidence, and conducting forensic investigations as per the new statutes. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to apply these new legal and technical procedures effectively in their roles, ensuring compliance and enhancing the integrity of evidence in criminal proceedings.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Criminal Laws: Warrant of Arrest and Process to Compel Appearance
desc: With the introduction of new criminal laws in India, it is crucial for law enforcement professionals to understand the updated procedures. This course delves into the critical aspects of compelling appearance through warrants of arrest as defined in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. Learners will explore the complete lifecycle of a warrant, from its form and duration (Section 72) to the power to direct security (Section 73) and the authorities to whom it can be directed (Sections 74-76). The curriculum thoroughly covers the procedural requirements for executing warrants both within and outside local jurisdiction, including the notification of substance (Section 77) and post-arrest protocols (Sections 78-83). By completing this course, officials will be able to perform their duties with confidence, ensuring legal compliance, procedural fairness, and upholding the rule of law in every arrest.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: New Customs Initiatives
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the modernization journey of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC). It is designed for officials and stakeholders who need to understand the paradigm shift in India's customs clearance procedures. The curriculum begins by tracing the historical context, moving from manual, paper-based systems to the current era of computer-assisted and risk-based processing. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to the 'Turant Customs' initiative, a next-generation reform program built on the principles of Faceless, Paperless, and Contactless Customs. Learners will gain a detailed understanding of critical components like the Faceless Assessment Groups (FAGs), the e-Sanchit portal for digital document submission, and the automated clearance process. The course also covers other significant initiatives such as the Single Window Interface for Trade (SWIFT), Direct Port Delivery (DPD), and the role of the Risk Management System (RMS) in balancing trade facilitation with enforcement. Upon completion, participants will be able to navigate the new digital customs landscape, appreciate the benefits of these reforms in reducing dwell time and costs, and understand their role in improving India's 'Trading Across Borders' ranking.
org: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs(CBIC)

title: New Income Tax Act 2025: Assessment and Tax Administrations
desc: The introduction of the Income Tax Act, 2025 marks a significant shift in India's tax landscape. This course is designed to provide a detailed examination of this new legislation and its practical implications for tax administration. It begins by outlining the institutional structure, including the functions of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other income tax authorities. The curriculum then guides learners through the critical processes of filing income returns, various assessment procedures such as summary and scrutiny assessments, and the framework for appeals and revisions. Special emphasis is placed on modern, technology-driven systems like e-filing and faceless assessments, which are central to the new Act. Furthermore, the course explores the provisions for alternate dispute resolution (ADR), penalties for non-compliance, and prosecution, providing a complete view of the enforcement mechanism. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped with a holistic understanding of the new tax law, enabling them to ensure fair and efficient tax compliance while upholding taxpayer rights.
org: National Academy of Direct Taxes NADT

title: New Income Tax Act 2025: Collection and  Refunds
desc: The Income Tax Act, 2025 provides a comprehensive framework for the timely collection of taxes and the efficient management of tax credits and refunds. Provisions relating to advance payment, collection, and recovery ensure that taxes are paid during the year in which income is generated and empower tax authorities to recover outstanding dues in cases of default. The mechanisms of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) and Tax Collected at Source (TCS) serve as key instruments for early and continuous tax collection by deducting or collecting tax at the point of income or transaction. The Act also establishes a structured refund system for returning excess taxes paid by taxpayers, along with applicable interest. Collectively, these provisions promote regular revenue flow to the Government, enhance compliance, reduce tax evasion, and safeguard taxpayer rights through transparent and well-defined procedures.
org: National Academy of Direct Taxes NADT

title: New Income Tax Act 2025: Heads of Income
desc: This course provides a detailed exploration of the fundamental principles of income classification under the Indian Income-tax Act. It is designed to equip learners with the knowledge to systematically categorize all forms of taxable income. The curriculum delves into each of the five statutory heads: 'Salaries,' covering income from employment; 'Income from House Property,' focusing on rental and deemed rental income; 'Profits and Gains of Business or Profession' (PGBP), for income from commercial activities; 'Capital Gains,' arising from the transfer of assets; and 'Income from Other Sources,' which includes residual income like interest and dividends. Participants will learn the specific rules, exemptions, and computational methods applicable to each head. By mastering this classification, learners will be able to accurately compute taxable income, apply relevant deductions, and ensure full compliance with tax laws, forming an essential skill set for roles in finance, accounting, and tax administration.

title: New Income Tax Act 2025: Special and Other Provisions

The course delves into targeted provisions for specific entities like non-residents, charitable trusts, and investment funds, and clarifies how to determine tax in unique scenarios involving deceased individuals or discontinued businesses. Furthermore, it covers the specific taxation framework for shipping companies and the comprehensive compliance regulations for Non-Profit Organisations (NPOs). Upon completion, learners will be equipped to navigate and apply these complex provisions effectively in their professional roles.

title: New Income Tax Act 2025: Total Income and Computation
desc: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the principles and procedures for calculating total income under the Indian Income Tax framework. It is designed for professionals who need to ensure accurate tax computation and compliance. The curriculum begins by breaking down the five heads of income—Salaries, House Property, Business or Profession, Capital Gains, and Other Sources—and explains the specific rules for computing income under each. Learners will then delve into the critical adjustment processes required to calculate Gross Total Income. This includes understanding the provisions for clubbing income of other persons and the rules for setting off and carrying forward losses from previous years. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to mastering deductions available under Chapter VI-A, such as those under Sections 80C, 80D, and 80G. By the end of the course, participants will be able to systematically compute total taxable income and determine the final tax liability, equipping them with the practical skills needed for precise and compliant tax assessment.

title: New initiative on public procurement Landscape of India
desc: This course delves into the modernization of public procurement in India, focusing on the pivotal role of the General Financial Rules (GFRs) and the Government e-Marketplace (GeM). It begins by outlining the pre-2017 procurement environment, characterized by fragmented rules and a lack of uniformity, which often led to limited competition and cartelization. The curriculum then provides a detailed exploration of GeM, the national procurement portal designed to create a transparent, efficient, and inclusive ecosystem. Participants will learn about the key functionalities of GeM, including various procurement modes like Direct Purchase, L1 Purchase, e-bidding, and Reverse Auctions. The course also covers the operational roles within the GeM portal, such as Indentor, Buyer, and DDO, and explains the tools available for ensuring price reasonability and vendor accountability. By the end of this course, government officials will be equipped to leverage GeM to conduct procurement activities that are compliant with GFRs, enhance fiscal discipline, and achieve better value for public money.

title: New TAX Regime
desc: Understanding personal income tax is crucial for financial wellness and legal compliance. This course, 'Overview of the New Tax Regime,' is specifically designed to clarify the recent changes in India's direct tax laws. It addresses the critical need for every taxpayer to understand the options available to them. The course begins by explaining the context and objectives behind the introduction of the new tax regime. It then delves into a detailed comparison of the old and new systems, covering tax rates, slabs, and the treatment of common deductions and exemptions like HRA, LTA, and Section 80C investments. Learners will be guided through practical examples to calculate their tax liability under both scenarios, enabling a clear, data-backed decision-making process. This knowledge is essential for all government employees and citizens to optimize their tax outgo and ensure they are compliant with the latest regulations. The course aims to empower you with the confidence to manage your tax affairs effectively.

title: Next Generation OTN
desc: Dive into the technical foundations of Next-Generation Optical Transport Networks (OTN) with this detailed course. As data demands from services like 5G and high-speed Ethernet continue to grow, OTN provides a crucial framework for building efficient, scalable, and robust optical backbones. This program begins by explaining why OTN is the successor to traditional transport technologies, offering a detailed comparison with SDH/SONET. You will learn about the standardized OTN architecture, including its multiplexing structure, various interfaces, and line rates from OTU1 to OTU4 (100 Gbps and beyond). The course also demystifies the OTN frame structure, detailing the roles of the OPU, ODU, and OTU layers and their associated overheads. Key features that enhance network performance, such as Forward Error Correction (FEC) for increased reach and Tandem Connection Monitoring (TCM) for multi-vendor network monitoring, are explained in depth. Upon completion, you will have a solid understanding of OTN principles, enabling you to appreciate its role in creating cost-effective and high-performance transport networks.

title: Next Generation SDH
desc: This course is designed for telecommunication professionals seeking to understand the evolution from legacy SDH to more flexible and efficient packet-aware transport networks. The content addresses the critical need for operators to upgrade existing infrastructure to support the growing demand for data services. You will learn about the architectural shift to NG-SDH and its core components, including Multi-Service Provisioning Platforms (MSPP). The course provides a detailed examination of the three key technologies that power NG-SDH: Generic Framing Procedure (GFP) for mapping various client signals, Virtual Concatenation (VCAT) for right-sizing bandwidth, and Link Capacity Adjustment Scheme (LCAS) for dynamic, hitless bandwidth adjustments. Upon completion, you will be able to analyze the benefits of NG-SDH in terms of operational efficiency, cost savings, and its role in supporting advanced services like Ethernet and storage area networking, preparing you to contribute to modern network planning and management.

title: NITI for States Platform
desc: This course is designed to equip government officials with the essential skills to effectively use the NITI for States (NFS) Platform. The NFS platform serves as a critical digital infrastructure for strengthening state-level governance and promoting collaborative federalism through knowledge sharing. This program details the platform's significance and provides a step-by-step guide to its functionalities. Participants will learn to navigate the portal, access vital resources, and understand the specific responsibilities associated with different user roles, such as Contributor, Reviewer, and Admin. The course emphasizes the practical aspects of content management, including how to contribute, review, and publish knowledge assets. By completing this course, learners will be prepared to actively participate in this digital ecosystem, leveraging the platform to share best practices, access valuable insights, and contribute to a more informed and collaborative governance framework across India.

title: Nodal Officer Functions and Workflows in e-HRMS 2.0
desc: This course provides an overview of e-HRMS 2.0, the unified digital platform for managing human resource services and employee service records across the Government of India. It focuses on the critical role of Nodal Officers in ensuring the efficient administration of employee records and the smooth functioning of the system. Learners will gain an understanding of the responsibilities of Nodal Officers in verifying employee profiles, maintaining the accuracy and authenticity of service records, and ensuring the timely processing of service-related requests. The course also covers key administrative functions, including leave management, transfers, resignations, retirement processes, reimbursement claims, Leave Travel Concession (LTC) cases, and private foreign visit approvals. Additionally, learners will explore the end-to-end approval workflows within the e-HRMS 2.0 portal and the best practices for ensuring efficient and compliant HR service delivery.
org: Department of Personnel and Training DoPT

title: Non-Fare Revenue in Indian Railways
desc: This course delves into the critical area of Non-Fare Revenue (NFR) as a vital component of Indian Railways' financial strategy. In an environment of increasing operational costs and competition, diversifying revenue sources is paramount. This program provides an in-depth look at the various avenues for generating NFR, including advertising on rolling stock and at stations, content-on-demand services, and the commercial exploitation of railway land and assets. Participants will learn about the evolution of NFR policy, the establishment of the NFR Directorate, and the specific guidelines for schemes like NINFREEZ, which empowers divisional units to implement innovative revenue-generating ideas. The course is designed to equip railway officials with the knowledge to identify, evaluate, and implement NFR projects, thereby contributing to the organization's financial health and enhancing the passenger experience through improved amenities funded by these new revenue streams.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: Non-Functional Selection and Upgradation for Organized Group
desc: This comprehensive course provides an in-depth understanding of Non-Functional Selection Grade (NFSG) and Non-Functional Upgradation (NFU) as critical tools for career management in India's Organized Group 'A' (OGA) services. The program begins by establishing the context of career progression challenges, such as promotional bottlenecks and stagnation, that many OGA services face. It then delves into the core concepts of NFSG and NFU, clarifying how they offer financial upgradation to senior officers by granting higher pay levels without an immediate change in duties or designation. Key learning areas include the specific conditions and eligibility criteria for availing these benefits, focusing on the crucial linkage to the empanelment and posting of IAS officers at the central government level. The course meticulously explains the 'two-year seniority' rule, where OGA officers senior to a posted IAS batch become eligible for NFU. Upon completion, learners will be able to accurately interpret the rules, assess eligibility, and understand the strategic importance of NFSG/NFU in maintaining morale and parity across different civil services.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Non-Timber Forest Products Its Classification Types and Uses
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs), defined as forest-derived goods of biological origin other than timber. It highlights their global significance, noting that nearly 80% of people in developing countries depend on NTFPs for their basic needs and livelihoods. The course explores the classification and diverse uses of NTFPs in India, with special reference to the Western Himalayan region. Key categories discussed include fibres, flosses, bamboos, canes, essential oils, gums, resins, tannins, and fixed oils. It also introduces sustainable livelihood strategies based on NTFPs. Additionally, the course covers important medicinal plants found in regions such as Himachal Pradesh, including Amalaki, Ashwagandha, and Brahmi, along with insights into threatened species and their conservation.

title: NotebookLM
desc: In an era of information overload, the ability to quickly analyze and synthesize complex documents is a critical skill for public sector professionals. This course provides a comprehensive introduction to NotebookLM, Google's AI-powered tool designed to streamline research and document analysis. You will explore the core functionalities, from uploading and organizing various document types to leveraging its advanced AI for generating concise summaries and extracting crucial insights. The course emphasizes hands-on learning, guiding you through practical exercises, such as analyzing budget documents, to build your confidence. By the end of this program, you will be able to integrate NotebookLM into your daily workflow to conduct research more effectively, prepare reports with greater efficiency, and make well-informed decisions based on a thorough understanding of your source materials. This will empower you to save valuable time and effort while elevating the quality of your work.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Noting and Drafting
desc: In the machinery of government, the ability to create precise notes and well-structured drafts is a cornerstone of effective administration. Every official communication, from internal file notings to formal letters, shapes policy implementation and public service delivery. This course is designed to equip public officials with the foundational skills required to excel in this critical area, ensuring clarity, accountability, and procedural correctness in all written communications within a secretariat environment. The curriculum delves into the core principles of noting, focusing on how to summarize facts, analyze issues, and provide clear recommendations on a file. It covers the distinct purposes of notes and drafts, detailing the structure, language, and tone appropriate for each. Participants will learn about different types of official correspondence, such as office memorandums, demi-official letters, and notifications, and understand the specific contexts in which they are used. By the end of this course, learners will be able to confidently prepare notes that facilitate quick and informed decision-making and draft clear, concise, and procedurally correct communications, leading to improved efficiency and professionalism.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: NTPC Control and Instrumentation
desc: This course offers a detailed examination of control and instrumentation within the power generation sector. It is designed for engineering and technical professionals seeking to understand the core systems that govern power plant operations. The curriculum begins by establishing the context of why precise control is vital for safety and efficiency in a high-pressure environment like a thermal power plant. Key learning areas include the study of various sensors and transmitters for measuring critical parameters such as pressure, temperature, flow, and level. The course delves into the architecture and function of Distributed Control Systems (DCS) and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), which are central to plant automation. Learners will explore control loop diagrams, safety interlocks, and process optimization strategies. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to better understand, monitor, and contribute to the management of automated processes in a power plant setting, enhancing their effectiveness in operational and maintenance roles.

title: NTPC Job Safety Analysis - English
desc: In any high-risk operational environment, proactive safety management is paramount to preventing accidents and ensuring workforce well-being. This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Job Safety Analysis (JSA), a fundamental tool for workplace hazard management. It is designed for personnel who are responsible for overseeing, performing, or ensuring the safety of tasks in industrial settings. The curriculum delves into the core methodology of JSA, teaching learners how to deconstruct a job into a sequence of steps, identify existing or potential hazards at each step, and determine effective preventive measures. Key learning areas include techniques for hazard recognition, risk assessment principles to prioritize dangers, and the hierarchy of controls—from elimination and substitution to engineering controls, administrative procedures, and personal protective equipment (PPE). Upon completion, participants will be equipped to conduct a JSA, write clear and safe work procedures, and effectively communicate safety instructions to their teams, thereby contributing directly to a safer, more compliant, and more productive work environment.

title: NTPC Job Safety Analysis - Hindi
desc: In any industrial environment, proactive safety management is essential to prevent accidents and ensure operational continuity. This course, 'Fundamentals of Job Safety Analysis,' offers a comprehensive introduction to one of the most effective tools for workplace risk assessment. It is specifically designed for personnel operating in environments where safety is paramount, such as the power and manufacturing sectors. The curriculum breaks down the JSA process into manageable steps, starting with how to deconstruct a job into its core tasks. Learners will then be guided on how to systematically identify potential and existing hazards at each stage, from equipment-related risks to environmental factors. A significant focus is placed on developing practical and effective control measures to eliminate or minimize these hazards. Upon completion, participants will be capable of conducting a basic JSA, documenting their findings, and contributing meaningfully to their organization's safety management system, ultimately fostering a zero-accident workplace.

title: NTPC Safety Framework - English
desc: The energy sector, particularly power generation, involves complex machinery and high-risk operations, making a structured safety approach non-negotiable. This course delves into the NTPC Safety Framework, providing a detailed examination of the policies and guidelines designed to protect employees, assets, and the environment. It serves as an essential guide for all personnel to understand their role in maintaining a secure and hazard-free workplace. Participants will learn about the core components of the framework, including risk assessment methodologies, safety audit procedures, work permit systems, and emergency preparedness plans. The course also covers the importance of regulatory compliance and the process for incident investigation and reporting to prevent future occurrences. Upon completion, learners will be able to confidently identify potential hazards in their work environment, apply the correct safety protocols for various tasks, and actively participate in the continuous improvement of safety standards. This knowledge is fundamental for fostering a proactive safety culture and ensuring operational integrity across all facilities.

title: NTPC Safety Framework - Hindi
desc: यह पाठ्यक्रम कार्यस्थल सुरक्षा के मूलभूत सिद्धांतों और एक प्रभावी सुरक्षा ढांचे के घटकों का विस्तृत अन्वेषण प्रदान करता है। सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उद्यमों, विशेष रूप से बिजली जैसे उच्च जोखिम वाले क्षेत्रों के संदर्भ में, सुरक्षा केवल एक प्राथमिकता नहीं है, बल्कि परिचालन उत्कृष्टता और कर्मचारी कल्याण की आधारशिला है। यह पाठ्यक्रम शिक्षार्थियों को सुरक्षा नीतियों, प्रक्रियाओं और मानकों के एक संरचित सेट से परिचित कराएगा जो दुर्घटनाओं को रोकने और जोखिमों को कम करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किए गए हैं। प्रमुख शिक्षण क्षेत्रों में सुरक्षा नियमों को समझना, खतरों की पहचान करना, जोखिम मूल्यांकन करना और नियंत्रण उपायों को लागू करना शामिल है। पाठ्यक्रम में व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षा उपकरणों (पीपीई) के सही उपयोग, आपातकालीन तैयारी प्रक्रियाओं और घटना रिपोर्टिंग के महत्व पर भी जोर दिया गया है। इस पाठ्यक्रम को पूरा करने पर, शिक्षार्थी अपने कार्य वातावरण में सुरक्षा प्रोटोकॉल को आत्मविश्वास से लागू करने, एक मजबूत सुरक्षा संस्कृति में योगदान करने और अपने और अपने सहयोगियों के लिए एक सुरक्षित कार्यस्थल सुनिश्चित करने में सक्रिय भूमिका निभाने में सक्षम होंगे।

title: NTPC Safety Policy - English
desc: This foundational course is designed to instill a thorough understanding of the NTPC Safety Policy. It delves into the core components of the policy, explaining why a robust safety culture is paramount in the high-risk environment of the power sector. The curriculum covers key areas such as hazard identification, risk assessment, emergency preparedness, and the specific safety protocols that all employees and contractors must follow. Participants will learn about their individual and collective responsibilities in upholding safety standards, ensuring compliance with both internal guidelines and national regulations. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped to actively contribute to a safer workplace, recognize and report potential risks, and confidently apply safety procedures in their daily activities, thereby safeguarding themselves, their colleagues, and the organization's assets.

title: NTPC Safety Policy - Hindi
desc: यह पाठ्यक्रम एक व्यापक सुरक्षा नीति को समझने के लिए एक आवश्यक मार्गदर्शिका है, जिसे हिंदी में प्रस्तुत किया गया है। आज के औद्योगिक परिदृश्य में, विशेष रूप से बिजली क्षेत्र जैसे उच्च-जोखिम वाले वातावरण में, एक मजबूत सुरक्षा संस्कृति सर्वोपरि है। यह पाठ्यक्रम इसी संदर्भ को संबोधित करता है, जिसमें बताया गया है कि क्यों एक संरचित सुरक्षा नीति न केवल नियामक अनुपालन के लिए बल्कि प्रत्येक कर्मचारी की भलाई के लिए भी महत्वपूर्ण है। पाठ्यक्रम एक सुरक्षा नीति के मुख्य स्तंभों पर प्रकाश डालता है, जिसमें जोखिम मूल्यांकन, आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया प्रक्रियाएं, और व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षा उपकरणों का सही उपयोग शामिल है। शिक्षार्थी सीखेंगे कि संभावित खतरों की पहचान कैसे करें, घटनाओं की रिपोर्ट कैसे करें, और एक सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरण में सक्रिय रूप से कैसे योगदान दें। पाठ्यक्रम पूरा करने पर, प्रतिभागी अपनी भूमिकाओं और जिम्मेदारियों को बेहतर ढंग से समझ पाएंगे, जिससे वे अपने और अपने सहयोगियों के लिए एक सुरक्षित कार्यस्थल सुनिश्चित करने में सक्षम होंगे। इसका उद्देश्य केवल नियमों को सिखाना नहीं है, बल्कि सुरक्षा को एक मुख्य मूल्य के रूप में स्थापित करना है।

title: Numerical Rating System for Railway Bridge Condition Assessment
desc: This course introduces the Numerical Rating System (NRS) used for the assessment of Indian Railway Bridges. It provides a structured approach for evaluating the physical condition of bridge components and prioritizing maintenance activities based on objective condition ratings. The system enables systematic monitoring of bridge health, identification of deterioration trends, and assessment of factors affecting structural performance and safety. Learners will understand how NRS supports data-driven decision-making in bridge maintenance by helping optimize resource allocation, reduce lifecycle costs, and improve operational safety. The course also covers inspection procedures, evaluation criteria, and reporting mechanisms used in assigning numerical ratings. By applying the NRS framework, railway professionals can ensure timely maintenance interventions and enhance the reliability and safety of bridge infrastructure.

title: Nursery Techniques
desc: Embark on a journey to master the art and science of nursery management. This course is designed for individuals seeking to build a strong foundation in horticultural and forestry nursery practices. You will begin by understanding the critical aspects of setting up a nursery, including infrastructure like greenhouses and mist chambers, and designing an efficient layout. The course then delves into the practical skills of plant propagation, covering techniques such as cuttings, grafting, budding, and layering. A significant portion is dedicated to the strategic selection of plant species tailored to specific environmental conditions and objectives. Furthermore, you will learn to identify and combat common nursery threats, including pests like white grubs and diseases such as damping off, ensuring the health and viability of your plants. Upon completion, you will be proficient in the fundamental operations required to manage a thriving and productive plant nursery, contributing to afforestation, agriculture, and conservation efforts.
org: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education

title: Nutrition and Rest for Physical Fitness of Security Forces Personnel
desc: This expert-led course is designed for police, defence, and security personnel to build long-term physical fitness, mental resilience, and operational readiness through informed nutrition, quality sleep, and healthy lifestyle practices. The course examines how sleep disruption, frequent consumption of roadside and processed foods, refined oils, toxin exposure from plastics and personal-care products, and unmanaged stress negatively affect energy levels, mood, metabolism, and overall performance. It also introduces practical, field-ready strategies such as smart food choices, hydration habits, strength training, stress management, and routine health monitoring. The course emphasizes realistic lifestyle adjustments that can be sustained even during demanding duties, patrols, and deployments.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: Occupational Safety and Health and Working Conditions Code 2020
desc: This program is designed to equip learners with a detailed understanding of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. The course begins by establishing the context of OSH, its historical development, and its importance within the framework of national labour laws. Participants will explore the fundamental changes and key features introduced by the OSH Code, replacing previous legislation. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to outlining the specific duties and responsibilities of both employers and employees to foster a safe and healthy work environment. Furthermore, it covers essential welfare provisions, regulations on working hours, and leave policies mandated by the code. Upon completion, learners will be able to interpret and apply the provisions of the OSH Code 2020, contributing to better compliance and improved working conditions in their organizations.
org: V V Giri National Labour Institute (VVGNLI) - Noida

title: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020
desc: This program is designed to equip learners with a detailed understanding of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. The course begins by establishing the context of OSH, its historical development, and its importance within the framework of national labour laws. Participants will explore the fundamental changes and key features introduced by the OSH Code, replacing previous legislation. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to outlining the specific duties and responsibilities of both employers and employees to foster a safe and healthy work environment. Furthermore, it covers essential welfare provisions, regulations on working hours, and leave policies mandated by the code. Upon completion, learners will be able to interpret and apply the provisions of the OSH Code 2020, contributing to better compliance and improved working conditions in their organizations.
org: V V Giri National Labour Institute (VVGNLI) - Noida

title: Odia Language
desc: This course is designed to equip learners with the fundamental skills required to read, write, and speak the Odia language. It offers a structured approach for beginners, starting with the building blocks of the language, including two, three, and four-letter words, correct pronunciation, and basic vocabulary for everyday objects, animals, and concepts. The curriculum progressively introduces learners to sentence construction, the use of prepositions, and understanding common phrases and collocations, which are essential for practical communication. Through a series of reading exercises, including simple passages and poems, participants will enhance their comprehension and fluency. The course also delves into grammatical aspects like synonyms and antonyms to enrich vocabulary and expression. For public servants, acquiring proficiency in a regional language like Odia is invaluable for improving citizen service delivery, fostering better community engagement, and ensuring more effective administration in regions where Odia is spoken. This program aims to build a solid foundation, enabling confident interaction and a deeper connection with the local populace.

title: Offence Related to Mischief Under the New Criminal Laws
desc: With the introduction of the new criminal laws, it is imperative for legal and law enforcement personnel to be well-versed in the updated statutes. This course provides a comprehensive and focused study on the offence of mischief under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaces the earlier Indian Penal Code. The curriculum is structured to provide a clear understanding of Sections 324 through 328, which detail the offence of mischief and its various aggravated forms, such as mischief by killing an animal or causing damage by fire or explosives. Participants will delve into the nuances of these laws, analyzing statutory illustrations and key judicial pronouncements to grasp how these provisions are interpreted and applied in real-world scenarios.
