A significant portion of the course is dedicated to understanding the framework of urban governance, with a deep dive into the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act and the six essential norms of good governance: decentralization, accountability, transparency, equity, efficiency, and participation. The course also showcases innovative practices and successful models from cities like Ahmedabad and Aizawl to provide practical insights. By the end of this course, public functionaries will be better equipped to analyze urban issues and apply governance principles to foster sustainable, resilient, and productive urban environments.

title: Urban Flooding Challenges and Solutions
desc: As cities expand and climate change intensifies rainfall, urban flooding has become a critical issue causing significant economic and social disruption. This course provides a comprehensive overview of the drivers of urban flooding, including the loss of natural percolation zones, encroachment on flood-prone areas, and the limitations of aging drainage infrastructure. It delves into globally recognized mitigation strategies such as sustainable drainage systems (SuDS), green infrastructure, and the development of retention basins. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to the Mumbai case study, showcasing successful interventions like real-time flood forecasting, advanced decision-support systems, and the creation of a city-wide disaster risk management master plan. Participants will learn to analyze the causes of urban flooding, evaluate the suitability of various mitigation measures for Indian cities, and apply risk reduction frameworks to safeguard urban infrastructure and communities. The course empowers learners to make informed decisions and lead efforts in building climate-resilient cities.

title: Urban Planning, Development and Climate Change
desc: As India undergoes rapid urbanization, its cities are increasingly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change. This course is designed to equip public officials and urban practitioners with the knowledge and tools necessary to navigate this complex challenge. It provides a detailed examination of how climate change impacts urban systems, from infrastructure and public health to biodiversity and local economies. The curriculum is structured to build a deep understanding of both the problems and the solutions. Participants will delve into the core principles of climate mitigation and adaptation within the urban context. The course covers key sectors identified by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs’ Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework, including urban planning, green cover, energy and green buildings, mobility, water management, and waste management. It also explores the multi-level governance structures, from international agreements like the Paris Accord and the New Urban Agenda to national schemes such as AMRUT and the Smart Cities Mission. By the end of this course, learners will be able to analyze climate-induced risks, apply best practices from successful case studies, and integrate a climate-resilient perspective into urban development initiatives, ultimately contributing to the creation of sustainable and thriving Indian cities.

title: Urban Solid Waste Management and Climate Change Mitigation
desc: This course examines the vital link between urban waste management and climate change, emphasizing how sustainable waste practices can contribute to climate mitigation and environmental sustainability. Aligned with the vision of Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0 and the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, the course presents waste management as a key strategy for building cleaner, greener, and climate-resilient cities. Learners will explore how improper waste disposal, particularly organic waste in landfills, generates methane and other greenhouse gases. The course covers essential concepts such as source segregation, scientific waste processing, composting, biomethanation, waste-to-energy technologies, and circular economy approaches. Participants will gain practical insights into reducing waste-related emissions, improving resource recovery, and supporting the transition toward sustainable urban development and Garbage Free Cities.

title: Urban Transport Management
desc: Dive into the critical field of Urban Transportation Management and learn how to shape the future of city mobility. This course offers a holistic understanding of planning, designing, and governing modern urban transport systems. You will explore the context of sustainable development, learning why integrated approaches to public transport, road hierarchies, and non-motorized transport (NMT) are essential for reducing congestion and enhancing urban life. The curriculum covers key technical areas, including corridor and junction design for traffic optimization, methods for identifying and rectifying accident black spots, and effective road safety strategies. Furthermore, the course examines the legal and policy landscape, with a focus on the Motor Vehicle Act 2019 and the National Urban Transport Policy. You will gain practical skills in conducting transport surveys and implementing parking management strategies. Upon completion, you will be prepared to propose and develop citizen-centric transportation solutions that promote sustainability, safety, and accessibility in our growing cities.
org: Regional Centre for Urban and Environmental Studies Lucknow

title: Urban Water Body Rejuvenation for Water Security under AMRUT 2.0
desc: This course reframes the rejuvenation of urban water bodies such as lakes, ponds, and wetlands as a critical component of urban water security, rather than a standalone beautification initiative. It aligns rejuvenation efforts with the objectives of the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0, which aims to develop cities that are water secure and climate resilient. The course addresses the degradation of urban water bodies due to pollution, encroachment, hydrological disruption, and inadequate management, all of which impact water security, biodiversity, and ecological balance. It introduces participants to key causes of degradation and a range of scientific and sustainable rejuvenation approaches.
org: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

title: Use Cases of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, designed to build capacity in integrated and evidence-based infrastructure planning. It addresses the critical need for holistic development by moving away from siloed approaches. The curriculum delves into key learning areas, including the core principles of PM GatiShakti, the application of GIS-based tools for data analysis, and the framework for multimodal connectivity. Through a series of practical use cases, learners will discover how the platform helps in optimizing route alignments, minimizing ecological impact, and reducing project timelines and costs. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to apply these principles to real-world scenarios, contributing to more efficient, coordinated, and sustainable infrastructure projects that drive national growth.
org: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade

title: Use of CTMS in BSNL
desc: This instructional course offers a detailed, step-by-step guide for BSNL employees on utilizing the Centralized Training Management System (CTMS). The content is specifically tailored to help staff understand the portal's functionalities and manage their training requirements efficiently. The course begins by explaining the prerequisites for access, including the need for a VPN-connected PC and the specific IP address. It then demonstrates the login process using an HRMS number and date of birth. Learners will be shown how to navigate the main dashboard to perform key tasks such as self-nominating for upgradation courses (e.g., EPP exams), selecting preferred training centers and exam dates, and submitting nomination forms. Additionally, the course covers how to check for important updates like course cancellations or rescheduling, browse the complete course directory, and access a wealth of study materials through the digital library. By the end of this session, employees will be proficient in using the CTMS portal for all their training needs.
subDomain: Digital Tools ( MS office, Excel, & PPT) & Platforms

title: Use of Different Means of Communication During a Disaster
desc: In the face of a disaster, effective communication is paramount to saving lives and managing response efforts. This course provides a comprehensive overview of disaster communication, equipping public officials with the necessary skills to navigate complex crisis scenarios. The curriculum begins with the fundamentals of communication in emergencies, exploring strategies to overcome common challenges such as infrastructure failure and information overload. It then progresses to cover a wide array of communication tools, from traditional radio systems to advanced technologies including AI-powered analytics, drones for situational awareness, and IoT devices for real-time data collection. Through practical insights and case studies, learners will understand how to select and deploy the appropriate technology for different disaster phases. Upon completion, participants will be able to develop robust communication plans, coordinate seamlessly with multiple agencies, and ensure that life-saving information reaches all stakeholders, including vulnerable populations.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: Use of Tunnel Boring Machine
desc: This course delves into the specialized field of mechanized tunneling with a focus on the Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM). It addresses the growing need for advanced underground construction techniques in developing urban infrastructure like metros, subways, and utility networks. The curriculum is structured to provide a foundational understanding of TBM technology, starting with its core components, including the rotating cutterhead, muck removal systems, and the installation of precast tunnel segments. Participants will learn about the entire operational lifecycle, from the complex assembly and launching process to continuous, 24/7 excavation. The course highlights the critical advantages of TBMs over conventional methods, emphasizing their efficiency, enhanced safety, and environmental benefits, which make them ideal for projects in sensitive locations. Upon completion, learners will be equipped with the knowledge to recognize the operational features of a TBM and appreciate its role in delivering modern, resilient infrastructure.

title: Used Water Management
desc: This course offers a detailed exploration of modern used water management systems, essential for public health and environmental sustainability. The curriculum is designed to build a strong foundational understanding of why managing wastewater is critical in urban and environmental contexts. Learners will delve into the technical aspects of wastewater, including its sources and characteristics, and will be introduced to the core principles of primary, secondary, and tertiary treatment technologies. The course also covers innovative approaches to water recycling and resource recovery, highlighting how treated water can become a valuable asset. Participants will gain insights into the regulatory frameworks governing water quality and disposal, and understand how to apply sustainable practices in real-world scenarios. Upon completion, learners will be prepared to contribute to the design, operation, and management of effective used water systems, ensuring the protection of our environment and communities.
org: Regional Centre for Urban and Environmental Studies Lucknow

title: Used Water Management
desc: As urban centers expand, the sustainable management of water resources has become a critical priority for governance. This course addresses the pressing need for effective used water management by providing in-depth knowledge on conservation and reuse strategies. It establishes the context by explaining the urban water cycle and the challenges posed by increasing water demand and pollution, underscoring the importance of circular economy principles in water management. Key learning areas covered include the fundamentals of wastewater treatment, various techniques for water conservation, and innovative methods for water reuse in different sectors. The curriculum, guided by expertise from the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, is designed to equip public officials with the necessary understanding to make informed decisions. Upon completion, learners will be able to identify opportunities for water conservation, evaluate different reuse technologies, and contribute to the planning and implementation of sustainable water infrastructure projects. This will empower them to support the development of resilient and water-secure cities for the future.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: User Charges on Public Services
desc: This course offers a structured understanding of how user charges and cost recovery mechanisms support the sustainable delivery of public services. It is designed to equip officers in finance and administrative roles with the knowledge to implement and manage user charge frameworks effectively. The curriculum is divided into four key areas: an introduction to the concept and rationale behind user charges; a detailed look at the rules and processes for their fixation, including cost computation; a focus on the role of autonomous bodies in managing user charges for financial sustainability; and an exploration of mechanisms for reviewing and revising charges. By covering these aspects, the course provides a robust framework for strengthening non-tax revenue, promoting resource efficiency, and ensuring the financial viability of public institutions while maintaining service quality for citizens.

title: Using Behaviour Science for Climate Adaptation and Mitigation
desc: Climate change is one of the most significant challenges of our time, and human behaviour is at its core. This course provides a deep dive into understanding and addressing the behavioural dimensions of climate change. It begins by establishing why climate change is a major behavioural problem, examining how individual actions and systemic factors across sectors like energy, agriculture, and waste management contribute to emissions. The curriculum then introduces foundational principles of behavioural science, including dual-process theory, cognitive biases, and the power of social norms. Learners will explore practical frameworks such as the COM-B model, MINDSPACE, and the Behavioural Drivers Model to analyze behaviours and identify barriers to change. The course showcases how these insights are being applied globally, with a focus on policy units like India's NITI Aayog BIU and case studies from the APAC region. By the end, participants will be equipped to design, implement, and evaluate behaviourally-informed policies and programs that encourage sustainable choices and build climate resilience.

title: Using Data for Planning and Prioritisation
desc: This course focuses on using data to enable smarter, evidence-based, and proactive decision-making in governance. It introduces three key analytical approaches: regression for predicting outcomes, classification for categorising and prioritising actions, and time series forecasting for anticipating future trends. Through practical government-focused scenarios, learners will understand how these techniques can support effective policy implementation, resource allocation, and public service delivery. The course also provides a structured and easy-to-follow analytics workflow that helps participants apply data-driven methods to real-world governance challenges. By moving beyond basic data analysis, learners will develop the ability to predict outcomes, prioritise interventions, and plan strategically for improved governance and administrative efficiency.

title: Using Data to Monitor and Improve Public Procurement
desc: This course is designed to equip public officials with the skills to use data effectively in the procurement lifecycle. It begins by establishing a strong foundation, discussing the primary objectives of public procurement through the '5Rs' framework and referencing key government documents like the GFR and Department of Expenditure manuals. The curriculum then introduces the concept of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), providing practical examples tailored to public procurement scenarios. Building on this, the course delves into identifying 'red flags'—critical indicators that signal potential issues or non-compliance in procurement processes. The final unit synthesizes these concepts, demonstrating through use-cases how data-driven decision-making can be applied at various stages of the procurement cycle. Upon completion, learners will be prepared to use past and present data to analyze performance, ensure compliance, and significantly improve procurement outcomes.

title: Utility of National Geoscience Data Repository
desc: Dive into the world of geological data with this in-depth course on the National Geoscience Data Repository (NGDR). Conceptualized by the Ministry of Mines, the NGDR is a pivotal platform designed to centralize and disseminate India's vast geoscientific data. This course provides a comprehensive walkthrough of the portal's functionalities, created to empower stakeholders in the mineral exploration and earth sciences sectors. You will begin with the fundamentals, understanding the objectives of NGDR and the user registration process. The curriculum then progresses through the various tools and data products available, covering an extensive array of domains such as geology, geochemistry, geophysics, marine data, and landslide information. Learners will gain hands-on knowledge of visualizing complex datasets, including 2D maps and 3D borehole data, and using analytical tools like proximity analysis and the query builder to extract meaningful insights. Upon completion, you will be proficient in navigating the NGDR, downloading baseline data and reports, and applying the portal's features to support scientific research, resource exploration, and strategic decision-making in line with national mineral policies. This course is essential for anyone involved in geoscience, from students and researchers to industry professionals.

title: Valuation in Customs
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of customs valuation, a critical component of India's trade and taxation system. The curriculum is centered on the legal and procedural aspects of determining the value of goods for customs purposes, which directly impacts duty assessment and compliance. Participants will begin by understanding the foundational provisions of Section 14 of the Customs Act, 1962. The course then provides a detailed examination of the Customs Valuation (Determination of Value of Imported Goods) Rules, 2007, and the Customs Valuation (Determination of Value of Export Goods) Rules, 2007, outlining the prescribed methods and principles. A key focus area is the role and functioning of the Special Valuation Branch (SVB), which handles complex cases involving related-party transactions and special circumstances. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze valuation issues, apply the correct methodologies, and ensure adherence to India's customs regulations, thereby contributing to fair and efficient trade administration.
org: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs(CBIC)

title: Valuation of Supply under GST
desc: This comprehensive course is designed to equip learners with the essential knowledge for correctly determining the value of taxable supplies under GST. The curriculum is centered around the legal framework provided in the CGST Act, 2017, and its corresponding rules. You will delve into Section 15, which defines transaction value, and understand its practical application. The course covers critical topics such as the treatment of discounts, subsidies, and incidental expenses. Furthermore, it provides a thorough examination of the CGST Rules (27-35) that prescribe valuation methods for specific situations where transaction value is not available, including supplies between related persons, transactions without monetary consideration, and supplies through an agent. By the end of this course, you will be able to navigate complex valuation challenges, ensure accurate tax assessment, and maintain compliance with India's indirect tax laws.
org: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs(CBIC)

title: Value Chain of Gas
desc: As the world shifts towards cleaner energy systems, natural gas has emerged as a pivotal fuel due to its efficiency and lower carbon footprint. This course offers an in-depth exploration of the entire natural gas industry, providing a strong technical foundation for professionals in the energy sector. The curriculum is structured to cover the three core segments of the value chain. You will begin with the upstream sector, learning about exploration, gas-reservoir characteristics, and field development. The course then moves to the midstream, detailing gas treatment, NGL recovery, pipeline transmission, and LNG operations. Finally, it covers the downstream sector, focusing on City Gas Distribution (CGD) for Piped Natural Gas (PNG) and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), as well as chemical conversion pathways for producing petrochemicals. Upon completion, learners will possess a holistic understanding of the operational, technical, and commercial aspects of the natural gas journey from reservoir to consumer.
org: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

title: Value Chain of Oil
desc: This course offers a holistic introduction to the oil and gas value chain, designed for professionals seeking a thorough understanding of the sector. It delves into the context of hydrocarbon energy, explaining why a detailed knowledge of its lifecycle is crucial for policy-making, regulation, and operational management. Key learning areas include upstream exploration techniques such as geological and seismic surveys, drilling operations, and various oil recovery methods. The curriculum also covers midstream logistics, including transportation and storage, and downstream processes like refining, crude oil classification, and petrochemical production. Furthermore, the course summarizes important government policies, such as India’s Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) Policy, 2018. Upon completion, learners will be able to connect the technical, operational, and policy aspects of the industry, enabling them to appreciate the complex interplay between the different stages of the value chain.
org: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

title: Vande Bharat Express in Indian Railways
desc: Delve into the engineering and operational excellence of the Vande Bharat Express, a landmark achievement for Indian Railways. This course details the journey from conception to reality, emphasizing its significance as a symbol of India's self-reliance in rail technology. You will explore the train's technical specifications, including its aerodynamic design, trainset configuration, and advanced propulsion system that enables high-speed travel. The curriculum covers the array of passenger-centric features, from rotating executive class seats and Wi-Fi connectivity to bio-vacuum toilets and an advanced passenger information system. A significant focus is placed on the multi-layered safety and security framework, including the indigenously developed Kavach Train Collision Avoidance System, CCTV surveillance, and enhanced fire safety measures. Upon completion, learners will have a thorough understanding of the Vande Bharat Express and its pivotal role in shaping the future of public transportation in India.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: Vande Bharat Express: Structural Design and Operations
desc: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of Train 18, India’s advanced semi-high-speed train. Learners will explore the concept, specifications, structural units, technical features, and major design characteristics of Train 18. The course covers the speed–acceleration profile, passenger capacity, shell design, construction materials, underframe specifications, and shell design validation requirements. It details bogie design, including the development process, features of the bolsterless bogie, and validation parameters, as well as the structural analysis of the bogie frame, bolted joints, and monoblock wheels. Participants will also study furnishing details, automatic plug doors, door system components, and technical data, along with the brake system, bio-vacuum toilets, interior features, FRP panels, flooring, partition systems, floor panelling, and continuous glass window design.

title: Vehicle Tracking to Ensure Cradle to Grave Disposal of Hazardous Waste
desc: The Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) implemented an innovative Vehicle Location Tracking System (VLTS) with NIC Gujarat and NIC Uttarakhand to enhance the monitoring and safe transportation of hazardous waste, promoting regulatory compliance and sustainable waste management.

title: Vessel Traffic Service (VTS)
desc: This foundational course on Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) is designed for professionals entering the maritime navigation and port management sectors. It establishes the context for VTS by explaining its importance in managing increasing shipping activities and mitigating risks such as collisions and environmental damage. Key learning areas include the legal basis for VTS under SOLAS Chapter V, the different levels of service (Information, Navigational Assistance, and Traffic Organization), and the core functions of a VTS system. The curriculum delves into the essential technological components, including RADAR, Automatic Identification System (AIS), and communication networks. The course also presents a case study of the VTS project in the Gulf of Kachchh, providing a practical example of a large-scale implementation in India. Upon completion, learners will have a robust understanding of VTS operations and their contribution to the safety of life at sea and the efficiency of maritime trade.
org: Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships

title: Vigilance Angle
desc: This introductory module is designed to demystify the critical concept of the 'vigilance angle' for government officials. The course begins by defining vigilance and its importance in maintaining integrity and accountability in public service. It then delves into the specific guidelines provided in the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Manual 2021, offering clear examples of actions that constitute a vigilance angle, such as demanding illegal gratification, forgery, or causing undue loss to the government. A key focus of the course is to draw the thin line between vigilance cases and administrative misconduct. Learners will understand which scenarios, like gross negligence or blatant violation of procedures, require consultation with the Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO). The course also covers examples of non-vigilance issues, such as lack of punctuality or insubordination, which are to be handled administratively under CCS (CCA) Rules. By the end of this session, participants will be better prepared to make sound judgments in classifying cases, ensuring that matters of integrity are investigated appropriately while administrative issues are dealt with through established disciplinary procedures.

title: Vigilance Awareness Ethics and Integrity in Railways
desc: Designed for all personnel within the railway ecosystem, this course builds a strong foundation in ethical governance and professional integrity. It begins by exploring the context and importance of accountability in public service, with a specific focus on the railway sector. The first key learning area is the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) Resolution, where learners will understand its purpose, the scope of protection for whistle-blowers, and the procedural responsibilities of competent authorities. The course then transitions to Vigilance Awareness, detailing its objectives and the proactive measures implemented by the Ministry of Railways to foster a transparent and corruption-free work environment. The final section provides practical insights into ethics, morality, and the Code of Conduct for government employees. Learners will be guided on how to apply these principles to navigate workplace dilemmas and ensure their actions align with the organization's core values. Upon completion, participants will be better prepared to contribute to a culture of integrity and accountability within Indian Railways.

title: Vigilance Clearance
desc: Vigilance clearance is a fundamental administrative process that safeguards the integrity and accountability of government services. A thorough understanding of its principles is essential for every public servant, as it directly impacts career progression, including promotions, empanelment, and post-retirement assignments. This course offers an in-depth exploration of the vigilance clearance framework in India. Learners will delve into the core criteria and protocols governing the issuance of vigilance clearance, with a specific focus on the distinct procedures for All India Services (AIS) officers and Central Civil Services. The curriculum covers the importance of due process, transparency, and equitable considerations in decision-making. Participants will gain a clear understanding of the procedural steps, from initiation to final approval, and the ethical considerations that underpin the entire system. By the end of this tutorial, officials will be equipped to navigate the vigilance clearance process confidently, ensuring compliance and reinforcing the foundations of ethical governance and public trust in administration.
org: Institute of Secretariat Training and Management

title: Vigilance Clearance
desc: Granting vigilance clearance is a critical administrative function within government ministries and departments, ensuring integrity and accountability in public service. This course offers a detailed guide to the entire process, starting with the purpose and necessity of vigilance clearance for various career events like promotions, postings to sensitive positions, foreign training, and retirement. Learners will explore the specific criteria that must be meticulously examined before issuing a clearance certificate. This includes checking for ongoing or contemplated disciplinary proceedings, suspension status, pending criminal cases, and penalties in effect. The course also clarifies complex procedural aspects, such as the application of the 'sealed cover procedure' and the specific conditions under which clearance can be rightfully denied or withheld. By completing this module, officials involved in administrative, establishment, and vigilance functions will be able to apply the correct rules and make informed decisions, upholding the principles of fairness and due process in personnel management.

title: Virtual Digital Assets: Investigative Techniques and Legal Framework
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of cryptocurrencies and their potential misuse in criminal activities. It explains Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs), blockchain transactions, wallets, major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum, smart contracts, and decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms such as Uniswap. The course highlights key risks, including unhosted wallets, mixers, privacy coins, and ransomware. Through case studies such as Tornado Cash and sample investigations, it demonstrates how on-chain analytics, exchange cooperation, and international coordination can help trace, freeze, and recover illicit funds. Additionally, the course outlines the legal powers under BNSS and financial regulations for the seizure and investigation of crypto assets.
org: Bureau of Police Research and Development BPRD

title: Virtual Private Cloud Security
desc: As organizations increasingly migrate critical workloads, applications, and sensitive data to cloud environments, securing network infrastructure has become a top priority. A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) provides organizations with a logically isolated section of a public cloud, enabling them to create secure, scalable, and highly configurable networking environments while benefiting from the flexibility and cost-efficiency of cloud computing. This module provides learners with a comprehensive understanding of Virtual Private Cloud Security, focusing on the design, implementation, monitoring, and management of secure cloud networking architectures. The course begins by introducing the concept of a Virtual Private Cloud and its role in modern cloud computing. Learners will understand how VPCs create isolated network environments within shared public cloud infrastructures, enabling organizations to securely host applications, databases, storage systems, and other cloud resources.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Virtual Private Network (VPN) Overview
desc: This course offers a detailed examination of Virtual Private Network (VPN) technologies, focusing on the architecture and application of MPLS-based solutions. The program begins by highlighting the limitations of traditional point-to-point networks, setting the stage for the introduction of VPNs as a scalable and efficient alternative. Learners will gain a thorough understanding of essential VPN terminology and the roles of different network devices, such as Provider (P), Provider Edge (PE), and Customer Edge (CE) routers. The course meticulously compares the overlay and peer-to-peer VPN models, discussing their respective advantages and drawbacks. A significant portion is dedicated to the MPLS VPN architecture, explaining how it combines the best features of previous models to solve issues like overlapping IP addresses and complex provisioning. Participants will also learn to differentiate between Layer 2 and Layer 3 VPNs and explore practical deployment scenarios, including Intranet (full-mesh and hub-and-spoke), Extranet, and Inter-AS connections. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze and understand the design of modern telecommunication networks.

title: Visakha Guidelines
desc: This course delves into the critical aspects of the Vishaka Guidelines, established in 1997 to create a secure working environment for women in India. It begins by examining the societal need for change and the catalyst incident that prompted the Supreme Court's intervention, filling a significant legal void concerning workplace harassment. The curriculum provides a detailed breakdown of what constitutes sexual harassment, covering physical, verbal, and non-verbal conduct. A key focus is on the duties mandated for employers, such as establishing a robust complaint mechanism, forming an Internal Complaint Committee (ICC), and conducting regular awareness training. Learners will gain a clear understanding of the complaint process, the structure of the ICC, and the importance of confidentiality and support for victims. The course concludes by discussing the impact of the guidelines on workplace culture and their evolution into the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act of 2013, making it essential for all employees, managers, and HR professionals to ensure a legally compliant and respectful workplace.
subDomain: Handling matters of Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy

title: Vision and Mission of India Post
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of organizational vision and mission, using India Post as a primary case study. It begins by illustrating the fundamental importance of these statements in providing strategic direction and a unified purpose for any large organization. The curriculum then focuses specifically on the Department of Posts, detailing its vision to become the customer's first choice and its multi-faceted mission. Learners will gain a clear understanding of India Post's commitment to maintaining the world's largest postal network, providing a range of services from mail and parcels to banking and insurance with speed and reliability. The course highlights how aligning actions with this vision and mission is crucial for every employee, ultimately enhancing service quality, building customer trust, and reinforcing India Post's role in national development and social security.

title: Visual AtoN
desc: This comprehensive introductory course is designed to equip maritime personnel with essential knowledge of Visual Aids to Navigation (AtoN). The course establishes the context of maritime safety, explaining why AtoN are a critical component of modern navigation. Key learning areas include a detailed breakdown of fixed and floating AtoN, covering lighthouses, beacons, daymarks, and buoys, along with their specific functions and components. Participants will delve into the science of visibility, learning to calculate geographical range and differentiate between luminous, nominal, and visual ranges. The course also explains the importance of light characteristics, including rhythmic patterns, intensity, color, and synchronization, which are vital for the correct identification of aids at sea. Upon completion, learners will be able to apply this knowledge to enhance their navigational awareness, ensuring safer passage for vessels in various maritime environments.
org: Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships

title: Visual Intelligence and Data Storytelling Essentials
desc: The Visual Intelligence Essentials–Data Storytelling course equips learners with the skills to transform complex data into clear, impactful visual narratives for effective decision-making. It covers principles of visual cognition, common pitfalls in data interpretation, and the importance of ethical and accurate data representation. Through historical examples, practical charting techniques, and real-world applications, learners develop the ability to design, interpret, and critique charts and dashboards. The course emphasizes selecting appropriate visual formats, reducing cognitive load, and communicating insights with clarity and purpose. By integrating analytical thinking with design principles, participants will enhance their ability to present data-driven insights confidently in reports, dashboards, and presentations across governance and professional contexts.
org: National Academy of Defence Production (NADP) Nagpur

title: Warabandi System
desc: In regions facing water scarcity, ensuring equitable access to irrigation is critical for agricultural sustainability and rural harmony. The Warabandi system offers a time-tested solution for rotational water distribution. This course delves into the core concepts and operational mechanics of Warabandi, explaining why it is a vital tool for modern water governance. Participants will gain a detailed understanding of how this system functions, from scheduling water turns to managing canal outlets, thereby promoting fairness among farmers regardless of their land's location. The curriculum covers the key distinctions between Khacha (government-administered) and Pucca (community-led) Warabandi, highlighting the institutional frameworks and stakeholder coordination required for each. Furthermore, the course addresses the practical challenges that impede the system's effectiveness, such as infrastructure degradation and administrative hurdles. Learners will analyze potential solutions to overcome these obstacles, equipping them to contribute to effective water distribution and strengthen community-based resource management.
org: North Eastern Regional Institute of Water and Land Management (NERIWALM)

title: Warehouse Inventory Network and Governing System
desc: This course delves into the operational framework of the Warehouse Inventory Network & Governing System (WINGS), a critical IT initiative by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) designed to modernize its vast procurement operations. The program begins by outlining the significant challenges of the manual mill-depot tagging and stack allocation process, such as complexity, cost inefficiencies, and lack of transparency. It then introduces WINGS as a robust, in-house developed solution that digitizes the entire CMR procurement lifecycle.Learners will gain a detailed understanding of the system's architecture and its application across various hierarchical levels, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, Divisional Offices, and Depots. The curriculum covers essential data entry processes, the generation of a least-cost matrix for mill tagging, and the principles of load balancing to optimize depot capacity. Through practical demonstrations, participants will explore the miller self-service portal for booking stack space and the roles of different FCI offices in maintaining the system. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to effectively use the WINGS platform, contributing to a more efficient, transparent, and cost-effective public distribution system.

title: Waste to Energy Conversion
desc: As global energy demand rises and waste generation increases, converting waste into a valuable resource is critical for sustainable development. This course offers a detailed exploration of the state-of-the-art technologies used in waste-to-energy (WTE) conversion. It begins by covering waste characterization and classification, identifying which materials are suitable for energy production. Learners will delve into the core scientific principles of thermochemical routes like combustion, gasification, and pyrolysis, as well as biological routes such as anaerobic digestion and fermentation for biofuel production. The course also examines the broader context of WTE, including its role in promoting a circular economy, policy considerations, and methods for assessing environmental sustainability through life cycle analysis. Upon completion, participants will be equipped with the technical knowledge to analyze, compare, and contribute to the planning and implementation of WTE projects, fostering environmental responsibility and resource efficiency in public and private sectors.

title: Water and Wastewater Sampling Techniques and Field Preparations
desc: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to water and environmental sampling, equipping learners with the knowledge and skills required to collect accurate, representative, and legally defensible samples. It covers fundamental sampling principles, objectives, planning methodologies, and safety practices. Participants learn a range of sampling techniques, including grab, composite, and integrated sampling, applied across diverse water sources such as rivers, lakes, reservoirs, groundwater, drains, industrial effluents, and sewage systems. The course also addresses field preparation, sample preservation, documentation, and chain-of-custody procedures. Flow measurement techniques—including bucket, float, V-notch weirs, and flow meters—are explained to support accurate assessment of water quality and pollution levels. Emphasis is placed on maintaining sample integrity, ensuring regulatory compliance, and supporting environmental protection and enforcement activities.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

title: Water and Wastewater Treatment
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the essential principles and modern technologies for water and wastewater treatment. It begins by establishing the critical importance of sanitation systems, drawing lessons from historical civilizations. Learners will gain a solid understanding of the biological and chemical processes that underpin wastewater treatment, focusing on how microorganisms are harnessed in aerobic and anaerobic environments to degrade organic waste. The course provides a detailed comparative analysis of prevalent treatment systems, including the conventional Activated sludge Process (ASP), the more efficient Sequencing Batch Reactor (SBR), and advanced Membrane Bioreactors (MBR). It addresses practical challenges and common operational failures observed in Indian Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs), offering insights into process optimization. Furthermore, the curriculum covers specialized topics such as the removal of nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to prevent eutrophication, and the essential stages of drinking water treatment, from filtration to disinfection. Upon completion, participants will be equipped with the technical knowledge to evaluate, select, and oversee water and wastewater treatment infrastructure effectively.

title: Water Law and River Valley Disputes in India
desc: Dive into the critical domain of water law and governance in India with this detailed course. You will begin by understanding the fundamental importance of water governance and the constitutional framework that underpins it. The course then navigates through the history and impact of major water-related enactments, providing context to the current legal landscape. A significant focus is placed on the mechanisms for resolving inter-state river water disputes, including the pivotal role of tribunals and judicial processes. The curriculum also examines contemporary legislative initiatives being considered to enhance water management and governance structures. Upon completion, learners will be equipped with the knowledge to analyze and interpret the complex legalities of water resource management, making it essential for professionals in policy, law, and public administration related to natural resources.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation
org: National Water Academy Central Water Commission Pune

title: Water Management Policy
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of water policy and its application in the Indian context. It begins by defining water policy and its role in ensuring equitable resource distribution for agricultural, industrial, and domestic needs, with a focus on sustainable development. The curriculum is structured around the two core pillars of water governance: the legislative framework, which covers constitutional provisions and key environmental acts, and the institutional framework, which details the roles of central and state bodies like the Ministry of Water Resources and Pollution Control Boards. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to watershed management, examining its objectives, policy formulation strategies, and the importance of public participation. Learners will gain a thorough understanding of the salient features, allocation priorities, and implementation strategies of the National Water Policy, equipping them with the knowledge to contribute to effective and sustainable water resource management in their professional roles.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

title: Water Pollution and Management Approaches
desc: In an era of increasing water scarcity and environmental stress, understanding the dynamics of water pollution and its management is paramount for public officials and environmental professionals. This course addresses the urgent need for effective water quality management by providing a detailed examination of the challenges facing global freshwater systems. Participants will gain a thorough understanding of the water cycle and the various sources of pollution that threaten this vital resource. The curriculum is structured to cover the key categories of contaminants—physical, biological, and chemical—and analyzes their detrimental effects on both human health and delicate ecosystems. Learners will be introduced to a range of established and emerging treatment options designed to mitigate pollution and restore water quality.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

title: Water Pollution and Management Approaches
desc: In an era of increasing water scarcity and environmental stress, understanding the dynamics of water pollution and its management is paramount for public officials and environmental professionals. This course addresses the urgent need for effective water quality management by providing a detailed examination of the challenges facing global freshwater systems. Participants will gain a thorough understanding of the water cycle and the various sources of pollution that threaten this vital resource. The curriculum is structured to cover the key categories of contaminants—physical, biological, and chemical—and analyzes their detrimental effects on both human health and delicate ecosystems. Learners will be introduced to a range of established and emerging treatment options designed to mitigate pollution and restore water quality. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to exploring the governance framework, detailing the crucial roles and responsibilities of state and local governments, regulatory bodies, and other stakeholders in implementing effective water safety measures and pollution prevention strategies. By the end of this course, you will be better equipped to support policies and practices that promote the circularity of water resources and address emerging water quality issues, contributing to a more sustainable and water-secure future.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

title: Water Quality Analysis and Management
desc: Ensuring the safety of drinking water is a cornerstone of public health, requiring rigorous scientific analysis and management. This course offers a detailed exploration of the methodologies used to evaluate water quality. It provides a foundational context on why monitoring water is critical for communities and the environment. Key learning areas include a thorough breakdown of physical parameters like turbidity and color; chemical parameters such as pH, hardness, and heavy metals; and biological indicators including coliform bacteria. The course specifically references the Indian Standard IS: 10500-2012, providing a regulatory framework for learners. Furthermore, it explains the distinct characteristics of surface and groundwater and details the conventional treatment processes like coagulation, filtration, and disinfection. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to interpret water quality data, understand treatment necessities, and support regulatory compliance, making them valuable assets in public health, environmental engineering, and water resource management.
org: Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad

title: Water Supply and Treatment Systems Engineering
desc: This course focuses on the complete lifecycle of planning, designing, and modernizing water supply infrastructure. It provides an understanding of key aspects involved in the development of efficient and sustainable water systems, including field investigations, preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), advanced water treatment technologies, SCADA integration, and retrofitting of existing infrastructure to meet "Drink from Tap" (DfT) standards. The course equips learners with knowledge of technical planning, resilient water distribution network design, automated monitoring and control systems, and modern approaches for improving the reliability, efficiency, and sustainability of water supply infrastructure.
org: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

title: Water Supply and Treatment Systems Management
desc: This course focuses on the financial, administrative, and environmental aspects of managing sustainable water utilities. It provides an understanding of key concepts such as capital cost optimization, regulatory water quality surveillance, Public-Private Partnership (PPP) frameworks, and environmental conservation strategies. The course also examines stakeholder engagement, institutional and governance mechanisms, water safety monitoring systems, and approaches for enhancing the sustainability and resilience of water supply services. By integrating technical, managerial, and environmental perspectives, the course equips learners with the knowledge required for the effective planning, implementation, operation, and long-term management of water utilities.
org: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

title: Water Supply and Treatment Systems Operations and Maintenance
desc: This course provides practical strategies for transitioning water utility operations from intermittent water supply to continuous (24×7) water supply. It covers the key operational and technical aspects required to achieve sustainable service delivery, including network diagnostic tools, District Metered Areas (DMAs), water loss management, pressure management, and preventive operation and maintenance practices. The course also highlights approaches for improving system efficiency, reducing Non-Revenue Water (NRW), and enhancing the reliability and longevity of water supply infrastructure.
org: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

title: Water Use Efficiency
desc: As India confronts growing water stress, optimizing water use in agriculture is paramount for national food and water security. This course provides a detailed examination of Water Use Efficiency (WUE), specifically tailored for officials and professionals in the irrigation and agriculture sectors. The program begins by defining WUE from multiple perspectives and breaks down its core components, including reservoir, conveyance, and on-farm application efficiencies. Participants will delve into the broader water economy, exploring advanced concepts like water footprint analysis, systematic water auditing, and the implications of virtual water trade. Furthermore, the course outlines practical and actionable strategies for improvement, covering both agronomic approaches like conservation tillage and mulching, and system-level upgrades such as micro-irrigation and smart irrigation technologies. It also contextualizes these practices within India's policy landscape by discussing key government initiatives like the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY). Upon completion, learners will be equipped to contribute to the planning, implementation, and evaluation of water management projects, fostering sustainable agricultural practices.
org: North Eastern Regional Institute of Water and Land Management (NERIWALM)

title: Waterproofing of Underground Structures
desc: This course covers waterproofing principles, applications, inspection, and quality control for government infrastructure. It addresses moisture ingress and waterproofing requirements for basements, underground structures, water-retaining structures, wet areas, roof slabs, and expansion joints. Learners gain practical knowledge of crystalline and cement-based waterproofing systems, including material verification, application, curing, testing, documentation, and acceptance criteria as per CPWD specifications. The course focuses on Field Inspection Officer responsibilities, including monitoring materials and workmanship, verifying application and curing, reviewing records, and identifying non-compliance. Participants will be able to effectively inspect waterproofing works, support quality assurance, and enhance the durability and service life of government assets.

title: Watershed Management
desc: This course delves into the essential principles and practices of watershed management, emphasizing its role as a critical strategy for natural resource conservation and rural development. It establishes the context by defining a watershed as a natural geo-hydrological unit and explains why its integrated management is crucial for environmental sustainability and socio-economic progress. Key learning areas include the core components of watershed development, such as soil and water conservation techniques, afforestation programs, sustainable agricultural practices, and the importance of community-led initiatives. The course also explores practical applications like watershed delineation, mapping, and surveying. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to analyze, plan, and support watershed projects that not only conserve natural resources but also create resilient livelihoods and contribute to achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
org: North Eastern Regional Institute of Water and Land Management (NERIWALM)

title: Ways of Enhancing Presentation Skills
desc: This e-learning course is designed to equip government officials and professionals with the essential skills needed to become confident and effective presenters. The program delves into the core components of successful public speaking, starting with proven strategies for managing anxiety and reframing the speaking opportunity to build a positive mindset. You will learn foundational principles such as the power of storytelling, the importance of listening to your audience, and why you shouldn't get burdened by the pursuit of perfection. The course provides a robust, practical framework centered on the '4 Ps': Plan, Prepare, Practise, and Present. Through this structure, you will learn how to meticulously plan your content, prepare compelling visual aids, practice for a smooth delivery, and present your ideas with passion and clarity. Furthermore, the course offers valuable guidance on handling audience questions and constructive criticism, ensuring you can navigate any interactive situation with professionalism. By the end of this course, you will be able to communicate your ideas coherently and persuasively in any professional setting.

title: Web Application Security for Enterprise Platforms
desc: Web Application Security for Enterprise Platforms is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of how to secure modern enterprise web applications, portals, APIs, and digital services against evolving cyber threats. As organizations increasingly rely on digital platforms to deliver critical services, ensuring robust application security has become essential to protect sensitive data, maintain system integrity, and uphold user trust. This course covers key principles of secure application design, authentication and authorization mechanisms, secure coding practices, and common web application vulnerabilities. Participants will explore widely encountered threats such as SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), session hijacking, insecure APIs, and data breaches, along with effective mitigation strategies.
org: National E-Governance Division (NEGD) MeitY Govt of India

title: Web-Based Tool: Rapid Risk Screening of Specified Dams
desc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the web-based Rapid Risk Screening of Specified Dams (RRSSD) tool, developed by the National Dam Safety Authority. As the initial stage of India's three-tier risk assessment framework under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, this tool is critical for modernizing dam safety management. The curriculum delves into the conceptual basis of rapid screening, explaining how risk is calculated by combining dam fragility factors with potential socio-economic and environmental impact parameters. Participants will learn to navigate the RRSSD platform, understand its structured workflow, and recognize the roles of different users within the dam safety ecosystem. The course highlights the importance of data validation processes for ensuring accuracy and accountability. Upon completion, learners will be able to interpret the tool's outputs, primarily the Risk Index, and understand how it informs the prioritization of dams for more detailed Tier-2 and Tier-3 assessments. This knowledge empowers officials to contribute effectively to transparent, evidence-based decision-making for enhancing dam safety across the country.
subDomain: Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation
keywords: Rapid Risk Screening of Specified Dams

title: WEBGIS भू  अभिलेख का डिजिटाइजेशन
desc: यह पाठ्यक्रम मध्य प्रदेश सरकार की एक महत्वपूर्ण डिजिटल पहल, वेबजीआईएस के माध्यम से भू-अभिलेख प्रबंधन का एक विस्तृत अवलोकन प्रदान करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। इस पाठ्यक्रम का उद्देश्य राजस्व विभाग के अधिकारियों, विशेष रूप से पटवारी और तहसीलदारों को भू-अभिलेखों को डिजिटल रूप से प्रबंधित करने के लिए आवश्यक कौशल से लैस करना है। पाठ्यक्रम में वेबजीआईएस पोर्टल का परिचय, इसके नागरिक-केंद्रित लाभ जैसे कि रीयल-टाइम अपडेशन और डेटा पारदर्शिता शामिल हैं। शिक्षार्थी एमपीभूलेख पोर्टल पर प्रमुख प्रक्रियाओं को निष्पादित करने के लिए व्यावहारिक, चरण-दर-चरण निर्देश प्राप्त करेंगे, जिसमें भूमि अधिकारों के हस्तांतरण के लिए नामांतरण (mutation) आदेशों का अनुपालन, भूमि पार्सल के लिए बंटवारा (partition) आदेशों को लागू करना और नक्शा बटांकन (map division) का कार्य शामिल है। पाठ्यक्रम पूरा करने पर, प्रतिभागी भू-अभिलेखों के प्रबंधन, सटीकता सुनिश्चित करने और नागरिकों को खसरा, खतौनी और नक्शे जैसी सेवाओं तक समय पर पहुंच प्रदान करने के लिए वेबजीआईएस प्लेटफॉर्म का कुशलतापूर्वक संचालन करने में सक्षम होंगे।
org: Commissioner of Land Records Madhya Pradesh

title: WEBGIS भू-अभिलेख का डिजिटाइजे़शन भाग-2
desc: यह पाठ्यक्रम मध्य प्रदेश भूलेख (MP Bhulekh) वेबजीआईएस प्लेटफॉर्म का उपयोग करके भू-अभिलेखों के प्रबंधन और डिजिटलीकरण पर एक व्यापक प्रशिक्षण प्रदान करता है। इसका उद्देश्य राजस्व अधिकारियों को भूमि संबंधी डेटा को संभालने के लिए आवश्यक डिजिटल कौशल से लैस करना है, जिससे पारदर्शिता, सटीकता और दक्षता में वृद्धि हो। पाठ्यक्रम को कई प्रमुख मॉड्यूलों में विभाजित किया गया है। शिक्षार्थी सीखेंगे कि एमपी भूलेख पोर्टल से ई-बस्ता, जिसमें खसरा और खतौनी जैसे महत्वपूर्ण दस्तावेज़ शामिल हैं, कैसे डाउनलोड करें। इसके बाद, पाठ्यक्रम भू-स्वामी सुधार मॉड्यूल पर केंद्रित है, जिसमें नाम, पिता का नाम और हिस्सेदारी जैसे विवरणों को सही करने की प्रक्रिया बताई गई है। इसमें यह भी शामिल है कि कैसे इन सुधारों को अनुमोदन के लिए तहसीलदार को भेजा जाता है। एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण खंड खसरा डेटा सुधार से संबंधित है, जहाँ शिक्षार्थी भूमि के क्षेत्रफल, प्रकार, भू-राजस्व और अन्य विवरणों को संशोधित करना सीखेंगे। पाठ्यक्रम में तकनीकी त्रुटियों को ठीक करने के लिए खसरा नंबर जोड़ने, हटाने या पुनः प्राप्त करने की प्रक्रिया भी शामिल है। अंत में, यह 'उड़ान खसरा' की अनूठी अवधारणा को शामिल करता है, जिसमें यह सिखाया जाता है कि सिस्टम में ऐसे खसरों को कैसे चिन्हित या हटाया जाए। यह व्यावहारिक प्रशिक्षण सरकारी अधिकारियों को अपने दैनिक कार्यों को अधिक प्रभावी ढंग से करने में सक्षम बनाएगा।
org: Commissioner of Land Records Madhya Pradesh

title: WELFARE SCHEMES ( HINDI )
desc: This course is designed to inform all personnel of the Indian Postal Department about the extensive range of welfare schemes and benefits available to them and their families. It provides a detailed exploration of the financial support systems in place, including immediate assistance in the event of an employee's death, aid for major surgeries and prolonged illnesses like tuberculosis, and support for handicapped employees. The curriculum delves into educational incentives, outlining scholarships for academic excellence in school, higher education, and even for UPSC exam preparation. Furthermore, the course explains the role of the Postal Sports Board in fostering sports and cultural activities, and details other welfare facilities such as holiday homes, recreation clubs, and special loans for Gramin Dak Sevaks (GDS). By the end of this course, learners will be thoroughly acquainted with the specific provisions for both departmental staff and GDS, enabling them to understand and access the benefits designed to enhance their quality of life and provide a safety net in times of need.

title: Wetlands Conservation and Management in India
desc: This course is designed to build foundational expertise in the crucial field of wetland preservation. The course delves into the ecological and economic importance of India's wetlands, highlighting their role in biodiversity and climate protection. Participants will navigate through five interactive modules that systematically break down complex topics, including the major threats to wetland ecosystems, the principles of 'wise use', and the structured process for creating Integrated Management Plans. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to understanding the policy, legal, and governance frameworks that underpin conservation activities in India. Upon completion, learners, including wetland managers, field staff, and environmentally-conscious citizens, will be empowered to apply this knowledge and actively participate in the sustainable management and protection of these vital natural resources.
org: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

title: Wetlands Conservation and Management in India
desc: Developed by the Wetlands Division of MoEF&CC, this self-paced e-learning course is designed to build foundational expertise in the crucial field of wetland preservation. The course delves into the ecological and economic importance of India's wetlands, highlighting their role in biodiversity and climate protection. Participants will navigate through five interactive modules that systematically break down complex topics, including the major threats to wetland ecosystems, the principles of 'wise use', and the structured process for creating Integrated Management Plans. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to understanding the policy, legal, and governance frameworks that underpin conservation activities in India. Upon completion, learners, including wetland managers, field staff, and environmentally-conscious citizens, will be empowered to apply this knowledge and actively participate in the sustainable management and protection of these vital natural resources.
org: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

title: Wheel and Wheel Profile in Indian Railways
desc: This course offers an in-depth examination of the science and engineering behind railway wheels, the crucial interface between a train and its tracks. It begins by establishing the fundamental role of wheels in ensuring stability, preventing derailments, and enhancing passenger comfort. Participants will delve into the technical aspects of wheel manufacturing, including the specific steel composition, forging, and heat treatment processes that ensure durability and strength. The course meticulously explains the significance of the wheel profile, detailing the functions of the tread and flange in navigating curves and maintaining track alignment. Furthermore, it provides a practical guide to identifying common wheel defects such as thin flanges, hollow tires, and thermal cracks. Learners will be familiarized with modern maintenance techniques like ultrasonic testing and reprofiling, alongside the strict safety standards and inspection protocols that govern wheel-set integrity in the Indian Railways network. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to contribute to safer, more reliable, and efficient railway operations.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: Whitetopping (Short Panelled Cement Concrete Pavement)
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of Whitetopping, also known as Short Panelled Cement Concrete Pavement, as a durable and cost-effective solution for road construction and rehabilitation. The curriculum is designed for engineering professionals involved in rural infrastructure development. It begins by establishing the context of rural road challenges and introduces Whitetopping as an innovative solution. Key learning areas include a detailed comparison of overlay types, the specific materials and mix designs for Whitetopping concrete, and the step-by-step structural design process following IRC guidelines. The course also covers the complete construction lifecycle, from pavement evaluation and surface preparation to texturing, curing, and joint sawing. Emphasis is placed on quality control measures and performance factors to ensure the longevity and structural integrity of the pavement. Upon completion, learners will be equipped to evaluate, design, and oversee the implementation of Whitetopping projects, contributing to the creation of sustainable and resilient rural road networks.

title: Wildlife Conservation
desc: Embark on a journey to understand the critical importance of wildlife conservation in the modern world. This course begins by defining wildlife, referencing legal frameworks like the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and exploring the diverse habitats across India. You will discover the intricate roles animals play as ecosystem engineers, examining concepts such as pollination, seed dispersal, and trophic cascades that maintain ecological balance. The curriculum further investigates the immense economic and intrinsic value of ecosystems, teaching you how to conceptualize benefits from clean air and water to cultural services. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to analyzing the primary threats to wildlife, summarized by the 'HIPPO' acronym: Habitat loss, Invasive species, Pollution, human overPopulation, and Overharvesting. You will learn to differentiate between on-site (in-situ) conservation in national parks and sanctuaries, and off-site (ex-situ) methods like zoos and seed banks. The course concludes with practical, real-world examples of how technology and simple lifestyle changes can contribute significantly to conservation efforts, empowering you to become an advocate for our planet's natural heritage.

title: Wind Energy
desc: This comprehensive introductory course delves into the essential concepts and technologies behind wind energy conversion. Participants will gain a clear perspective on why the world is transitioning to renewable energy, with a focus on the diminishing supply of fossil fuels and their environmental impact. The curriculum covers the physics of wind, explaining how it is a form of solar energy and how its kinetic energy is harnessed. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to resource assessment, teaching learners how to interpret wind maps and understand the criteria for selecting optimal locations for wind farms, such as wind speed, tower height, and terrain. The course further explores the evolution and mechanics of wind turbine technology. It contrasts horizontal and vertical axis turbines and provides a detailed breakdown of the components of a modern three-blade turbine, including the nacelle, gearbox, and control systems. By the end of this course, learners will be equipped with the fundamental knowledge to understand the principles, potential, and technology of wind power generation.

title: WINDOW'S FIREWALL
desc: This course offers an in-depth guide to mastering the Windows Firewall and Windows Defender to enhance system security. It begins by establishing a foundational understanding of what a firewall is and its critical role in cybersecurity. The curriculum then progresses into the practical aspects of firewall management, detailing the features of Windows Firewall and Defender, including the different network profiles (Domain, Private, Public). Learners will receive step-by-step instructions on navigating both basic and advanced settings. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to creating and managing custom inbound and outbound rules to control network traffic, block specific applications, ports, or IP addresses. Furthermore, the course covers essential troubleshooting techniques to resolve common firewall issues and outlines best practices for maintaining a robust security posture. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to effectively configure and monitor the Windows Firewall, ensuring a strong defense against unauthorized access and evolving cyber threats.
subDomain: Digital Tools ( MS office, Excel, & PPT) & Platforms

title: Women Health and Hygiene
desc: Menstrual health is a fundamental aspect of human rights, dignity, and public health, yet it is frequently shrouded in silence and stigma. This course provides a comprehensive overview of the challenges surrounding menstrual hygiene management (MHM), particularly in contexts where access to education, sanitation, and safe products is limited. It delves into the reasons why menstruation is a neglected topic and highlights the resulting health risks and social consequences, such as school absenteeism and diminished self-esteem. The curriculum is designed to build a strong foundational understanding of MHM, covering everything from the use of safe absorbents to appropriate disposal methods. Participants will learn to identify and analyze the cultural taboos and systemic barriers that perpetuate inequality. Ultimately, the course equips learners with the tools and perspective needed to advocate for change, promote menstrual health awareness, and contribute to creating supportive and inclusive environments in schools, workplaces, and communities, fostering gender equity and empowering women and girls.

title: Women Self Defense Techniques Course
desc: In an era where women are increasingly active in all spheres of life, personal safety remains a paramount concern. This course is designed to equip women with the fundamental skills and mindset needed to defend themselves against potential assailants. It moves beyond theory to provide practical, demonstrated techniques that can be used in real-world situations. The curriculum covers responses to various types of attacks, including being grabbed from the front or behind, neck holds, hair pulling, and chain snatching attempts. Each technique is broken down into simple, memorable steps, focusing on using an attacker's force against them. By completing this course, learners will not only acquire a vital life skill but also experience a significant boost in physical and mental resilience. The ultimate outcome is to foster a sense of empowerment, enabling women to navigate public and private spaces with greater confidence and security.

title: Women Self Defense Techniques Course (Gujarati)
desc: In an environment where crimes against women are a significant concern, possessing self-defense skills is a crucial aspect of personal security and empowerment. This course is designed to equip women with practical and effective techniques to protect themselves from common types of physical assaults. The content moves beyond theory, providing clear, step-by-step demonstrations of eight distinct self-defense maneuvers. Key learning areas include methods to counter attacks from behind, escape from neck and shoulder grabs, defend against hair pulling, and neutralize an aggressor. The techniques focus on using an attacker's force against them and targeting vulnerable points to create an opportunity for escape. By mastering these skills, learners will not only enhance their physical safety but also build immense self-confidence and mental resilience. This training empowers women to navigate public and private spaces with greater awareness and the ability to protect themselves and others, contributing to a stronger, more self-reliant community.

title: WOOD PRESERVATION
desc: This detailed course delves into the science and application of wood preservation. It begins by establishing the importance of treating timber in the context of resource conservation and sustainable utilization. You will learn to identify the various biotic and abiotic factors responsible for wood degradation, such as white rot, brown rot, termites, and marine borers. The curriculum covers the classification of timber based on natural durability and treatability, providing a framework for selecting appropriate materials and methods. A significant portion of the course is dedicated to exploring different types of wood preservatives, including oil-type, water-soluble, and eco-friendly options like CCA, CCB, and borates. Learners will be guided through various treatment methodologies, from non-pressure techniques like brushing and dipping to industrial-scale pressure treatments and the sap displacement method for green timber and bamboo. By the end of this course, you will have the knowledge to select and apply preservation techniques effectively, ensuring the longevity of wood products while adhering to safety and environmental standards.
org: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education

title: WOOD SEASONING AND PRESERVATION
desc: This course offers an in-depth exploration of the principles and practices of wood seasoning and preservation. It is designed for professionals and technicians involved in forestry, timber processing, and woodworking who seek to master the art and science of drying wood effectively. The curriculum begins with the fundamentals, explaining why seasoning is crucial for preventing defects, increasing strength, and ensuring the dimensional stability of finished products. You will learn to measure moisture content, understand the concepts of free and bound water, and recognize the significance of the fiber saturation point. The course systematically compares different drying methods, including air seasoning, forced-air drying, kiln drying (steam, dehumidification, vacuum, solar), and analyzes their efficiency and energy consumption. A significant portion is dedicated to practical application, covering timber classification, pre-sorting, correct stacking techniques, and the interpretation of kiln schedules. Furthermore, learners will gain the ability to diagnose, prevent, and manage a wide range of drying defects, ensuring the production of high-quality, durable timber for various applications.
org: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education

title: Work Ethics
desc: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles of work ethics and their importance in the modern professional landscape. It establishes the context for why a strong ethical framework is critical for both individual success and organizational health, particularly within the public sector. Key learning areas include the core values that form the bedrock of ethical behavior, such as integrity, honesty, accountability, responsibility, and dedication. The curriculum delves into how these ethics translate into tangible actions, from enhancing productivity and meeting deadlines to fostering cooperation and building strong relationships with colleagues and clients. Learners will understand the distinction between personal and professional ethics and how to navigate challenging situations with a clear moral compass. Upon completion, participants will be equipped to apply these ethical standards in their daily roles, contributing to a more transparent, respectful, and effective work environment.
org: Indian Railway Institute Of Transport Management (IRITM)

title: Work Team Resilience
desc: In today's dynamic and unpredictable work environments, the ability of a team to navigate setbacks is crucial for sustained success. This course, 'Building Work Team Resilience to Thrive Under Pressure,' offers an in-depth exploration of the principles and practices that foster collective resilience. The program begins by establishing a clear definition of a true 'team' versus a 'group' and introduces the core components of resilience: capacity, setback, and the ability to bounce back. Participants will then dive into the four essential resources that fuel a team's ability to recover from challenges: team potency, shared mental models, the capacity to improvise, and psychological safety.
